questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to examine BigQuery data from a particular table several times per day. The underlying table being queried is several petabytes in size, but you need to filter the data and provide straightforward aggregations to downstream users. You want queries to run faster and to obtain up-to-date insights sooner. What should you do?

options.text: Run a scheduled query to pull the necessary data at specific intervals dally.
Use a cached query to accelerate time to results.
Limit the query columns being pulled in the final result.
Create a materialized view based off of the query being run.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery materialized views precompute and periodically cache query results, including filters and aggregations. They reduce repeated scanning of large base tables and use incremental base-table changes where possible to return up-to-date results with improved performance and efficiency.

**Learn more:** [Use materialized views](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/materialized-views-use) · [Optimize query computation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-performance-compute)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An Oracle database is deployed on a VM within a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network. You need to replicate and continuously synchronize 50 tables to BigQuery while minimizing infrastructure-management effort. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy Apache Kafka in the same VPC network, use Kafka Connect Oracle Change Data Capture (CDC), and Dataflow to stream the Kafka topic to BigQuery.
Create a Pub/Sub subscription to write to BigQuery directly. Deploy the Debezium Oracle connector to capture changes in the Oracle database, and sink to the Pub/Sub topic.
Deploy Apache Kafka in the same VPC network, use Kafka Connect Oracle change data capture (CDC), and the Kafka Connect Google BigQuery Sink Connector.
Create a Datastream service from Oracle to BigQuery, use a private connectivity configuration to the same VPC network, and a connection profile to BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
Datastream provides managed change data capture from Oracle to BigQuery. A private connectivity configuration lets Datastream communicate with a source database over a private VPC network, and Datastream connection profiles support both Oracle sources and BigQuery destinations. This avoids managing Kafka, Debezium, or Dataflow infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Create connection profiles | Datastream | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/create-connection-profiles?hl=en) · [Manage private connectivity configurations | Datastream | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/manage-private-connectivity-configurations?hl=en)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company plans to implement a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system that lets employees query a large knowledge base of internal documents, such as policy manuals and project reports. You need to prepare this unstructured text for embedding in the RAG system. What should you do to ensure that the system retrieves the most relevant information?

options.text: Use Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP) to scan and redact sensitive information within the documents before processing.
Store the documents as compressed files in a traditional relational database to enable more efficient storage and retrieval.
Convert the unstructured documents into high-dimensional numerical vectors that capture the semantic meaning and relationships of the text.
Index each word from the documents into a search engine to enable keyword-based search.

questions.explanation: RAG systems use embeddings: high-dimensional numerical vectors that represent the semantic meaning and relationships in text. Similarity search over these vectors retrieves passages relevant to a query even when the wording differs.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a large ecommerce company and store customer order data in Bigtable. A garbage collection policy deletes data after 30 days, and the number of versions is set to 1. When data analysts run a query to report total customer spending, they sometimes see customer data older than 30 days. You need to ensure the analysts do not see customer data older than 30 days while minimizing cost and overhead. What should you do?

options.text: Set the expiring values of the column families to 29 days and keep the number of versions to 1.
Use a timestamp range filter in the query to fetch the customer's data for a specific range.
Schedule a job daily to scan the data in the table and delete data older than 30 days.
Set the expiring values of the column families to 30 days and set the number of versions to 2.

questions.explanation:
Bigtable garbage collection is asynchronous, so expired cells can remain visible in reads until a later compaction removes them. A timestamp range filter restricts query results to cells within the required recent time window, immediately excluding data older than 30 days without introducing a separate deletion process. Google Cloud recommends applying read filters that exclude the same values as the garbage-collection rules.

**Learn more:** [Garbage collection overview | Bigtable | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/garbage-collection) · [Reads | Bigtable | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/reads)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is carrying out data preprocessing for a learning algorithm in Google Cloud Dataflow. Numerous data logs are generated during this step, and the team wants to analyze them. Because the campaign is dynamic, the data grows exponentially each hour.  
  
The data scientists wrote the following code to read data for new key features in the logs.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810093390-0a21gdsq.png)  
  
You want to improve the performance of this data read. What should you do?

options.text: Specify the TableReference object in the code.
Use .fromQuery operation to read specific fields from the table.
Use of both the Google BigQuery TableSchema and TableFieldSchema classes.
Call a transform that returns TableRow objects, where each element in the PCollection represents a single row in the table.

questions.explanation:
Reading only the required columns reduces the volume of data that Dataflow ingests from BigQuery. A `.fromQuery` read can select those specific fields, avoiding an unnecessary full-table, all-column read as the log table grows.

**Learn more:** [Read from BigQuery to Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/read-from-bigquery)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You run a database that stores stock trades and an application that retrieves the average stock price for a specified company over an adjustable time window. The data is stored in Cloud Bigtable, with the stock-trade datetime at the start of the row key. Your application has thousands of concurrent users, and you observe performance beginning to degrade as additional stocks are added. What should you do to improve your application's performance?

options.text: Change the row key syntax in your Cloud Bigtable table to begin with the stock symbol.
Change the row key syntax in your Cloud Bigtable table to begin with a random number per second.
Change the data pipeline to use BigQuery for storing stock trades, and update your application.
Use Cloud Dataflow to write a summary of each day's stock trades to an Avro file on Cloud Storage. Update your application to read from Cloud Storage and Cloud Bigtable to compute the responses.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Bigtable stores row keys in lexicographic order, so using a timestamp as the row-key prefix concentrates sequential writes into a small key range and creates a hotspot. Starting the key with the stock symbol distributes traffic across symbols and keeps a single company’s timestamped trades contiguous, supporting efficient reads for a requested time range.

**Learn more:** [Schema design best practices | Bigtable](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design) · [Schema design for time series data | Bigtable](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design-time-series)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two projects that run BigQuery jobs:  
  
- One project runs production jobs with strict completion-time SLAs. These high-priority jobs must have the required compute resources available when needed. They generally never fall below 300-slot utilization, but occasionally spike by an additional 500 slots.  
- The other project is for users to run ad-hoc analytical queries. This project generally never uses more than 200 slots at a time. You want these ad-hoc queries billed according to the amount of data users scan, rather than slot capacity.  
  
You need to make sure that both projects have the appropriate compute resources available. What should you do?

options.text: Create a single Enterprise Edition reservation for both projects. Set a baseline of 300 slots. Enable autoscaling up to 700 slots.

Create two reservations, one for each of the projects. For the SLA project, use an Enterprise Edition with a baseline of 300 slots and enable autoscaling up to 500 slots. For the ad-hoc project, configure on-demand billing.

Create two Enterprise Edition reservations, one for each of the projects. For the SLA project, set a baseline of 300 slots and enable autoscaling up to 500 slots. For the ad-hoc project, set a reservation baseline of 0 slots and set the ignore idle slots flag to False.
Create two Enterprise Edition reservations, one for each of the projects. For the SLA project, set a baseline of 800 slots. For the ad-hoc project, enable autoscaling up to 200 slots.

questions.explanation:
A dedicated Enterprise Edition reservation isolates the SLA workload and supplies its always-needed 300 baseline slots, while autoscaling can add up to 500 slots for occasional demand spikes. Keeping the ad-hoc project on on-demand billing charges its queries by data processed rather than by reserved slot capacity. BigQuery reservations are intended for capacity-based billing and workload isolation; on-demand compute is billed per TiB scanned.

**Learn more:** [Understand reservations](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reservations-workload-management) · [Estimate and control costs](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-costs)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Business owners at your company have provided a database of bank transactions. Each row includes the user ID, transaction type, transaction location, and transaction amount. They ask you to investigate which types of machine learning can be applied to the data. Which three machine-learning applications can you use? (Choose three.)

options.text: Supervised learning to determine which transactions are most likely to be fraudulent.
Unsupervised learning to determine which transactions are most likely to be fraudulent.
Clustering to divide the transactions into N categories based on feature similarity.
Supervised learning to predict the location of a transaction.
Reinforcement learning to predict the location of a transaction.
Unsupervised learning to predict the location of a transaction.

questions.explanation:
Unsupervised anomaly detection can flag transactions that differ substantially from normal transaction patterns as potentially fraudulent. Clustering is an unsupervised technique that groups transactions into a specified number of categories according to feature similarity. Because transaction location is present for historical rows, it can be used as the label in a supervised classification model that predicts the location for a new transaction. Supervised fraud detection would require known fraud labels, which are not included.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have **100 GB** of data in a BigQuery table. questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage Archive provides low-cost storage for infrequently accessed data, and BigQuery can query Archive-class Cloud Storage files through an external table. A locked bucket retention policy makes the retention configuration irreversible: it cannot be removed and its retention period cannot be decreased, thereby preserving the exported data for the required three years. Object versioning alone does not provide that immutable retention guarantee.

**Learn more:** [Use and lock retention policies](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/using-bucket-lock) · [Create Cloud Storage external tables](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/external-data-cloud-storage)

questions.explanation:
Cloud Bigtable requires reads and writes to be distributed evenly across a table's row space for good performance. A row-key schema that spreads access across the key space prevents hotspots and improves throughput without requiring additional capacity. Sequential numeric IDs and a single frequently updated row concentrate traffic and cause hotspots.

The requirement is to create a unified data-governance framework that supports centralized metadata discovery, data-quality monitoring, and consistent security-policy application across these different data stores without physically moving or duplicating the data. You need to implement a solution that provides this federated governance. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Export metadata out of Dataplex Universal Catalog by running a metadata export job.2. Implement Dataproc Metastore to manage table schemas and Apache Hive metastore for metadata discovery.3. Manage security using a combination of BigQuery row-level security and Cloud Storage policies.

1. Use Dataplex to organize the BigQuery datasets and Cloud Storage buckets into lakes and zones.2. Use Dataplex for automated metadata discovery, centralized security policy management, data profiling, and data quality tasks.

1. Deploy a centralized Cloud SQL database to store metadata extracted from BigQuery and Cloud Storage using custom scripts.2. Integrate the database with Looker Studio for data discovery and visualization.3. Implement a custom policy engine using Cloud Run functions triggered by changes in IAM policies to enforce consistent security across projects.

1. Create a Looker Studio dashboard on BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA views to visualize and monitor data quality.2. Manage security using IAM policies at the project level, supplemented by BigQuery authorized views for granular access control.

questions.explanation:
Dataplex provides federated governance for existing Cloud Storage buckets and BigQuery datasets by registering them as assets organized into logical lakes and raw or curated zones, without requiring data relocation. It supports automated metadata discovery and provides data profiling and data-quality scans, while lake and zone resources support centralized IAM policy management.

Your infrastructure team has established an interconnect link between Google Cloud and the on-premises network. You are designing a high-throughput streaming pipeline to ingest streaming data from an Apache Kafka cluster hosted on-premises. You want to store the data in BigQuery with the lowest possible latency. What should you do?

options.text: Setup a Kafka Connect bridge between Kafka and Pub/Sub. Use a Google-provided Dataflow template to read the data from Pub/Sub, and write the data to BigQuery.
Use a proxy host in the VPC in Google Cloud connecting to Kafka. Write a Dataflow pipeline, read data from the proxy host, and write the data to BigQuery.
Use Dataflow, write a pipeline that reads the data from Kafka, and writes the data to BigQuery.
Setup a Kafka Connect bridge between Kafka and Pub/Sub. Write a Dataflow pipeline, read the data from Pub/Sub, and write the data to BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
Dataflow supports a streaming Apache Kafka-to-BigQuery pipeline, including self-managed or external Kafka clusters, provided the Kafka broker is reachable from Dataflow worker machines. Reading Kafka directly and writing to BigQuery avoids the additional Kafka Connect and Pub/Sub stages, reducing end-to-end latency.

**Learn more:** [Apache Kafka to BigQuery template](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/templates/provided/kafka-to-bigquery)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for an airline and must store weather data in a BigQuery table. The weather data will serve as input to a machine learning model. The model uses only the most recent 30 days of weather data. You want to avoid retaining unneeded data and minimize costs. What should you do?

options.text: Create a BigQuery table where each record has an ingestion timestamp. Run a scheduled query to delete all the rows with an ingestion timestamp older than 30 days.
Create a BigQuery table partitioned by datetime value of the weather date. Set up partition expiration to 30 days.
Create a BigQuery table partitioned by ingestion time. Set up partition expiration to 30 days.
Create a BigQuery table with a datetime column for the day the weather data refers to. Run a scheduled query to delete rows with a datetime value older than 30 days.

questions.explanation:
A time-unit column-partitioned BigQuery table can be partitioned by the weather-date DATETIME value, and a 30-day partition expiration automatically deletes each partition based on its partition boundary. This aligns retention with the dates the model uses and removes obsolete data without scheduled deletion queries.

**Learn more:** [Managing partitioned tables | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-partitioned-tables) · [Introduction to partitioned tables | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/partitioned-tables)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are creating a report-only data warehouse in which data is streamed into BigQuery through the streaming API. In accordance with Google's best practices, you maintain both a staging table and a production table for the data. How should you design data loading so that there is only one master dataset, without impacting the performance of either ingestion or reporting?

options.text: Have a staging table that is an append-only model, and then update the production table every three hours with the changes written to staging.
Have a staging table that is an append-only model, and then update the production table every ninety minutes with the changes written to staging.
Have a staging table that moves the staged data over to the production table and deletes the contents of the staging table every three hours.
Have a staging table that moves the staged data over to the production table and deletes the contents of the staging table every thirty minutes.

questions.explanation:
Recently streamed BigQuery rows can take up to 90 minutes to become available for copy operations. Consolidating staged rows into the production table and clearing the staging table every three hours leaves production as the only master dataset and batches production writes at a frequency that avoids unnecessary ingestion and reporting overhead. BigQuery also recommends fewer, larger writes to final production tables.

**Learn more:** [Transform data with data manipulation language (DML) | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/data-manipulation-language) · [Optimize load jobs | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/optimize-load-jobs)

You use a Dataflow streaming job to read messages from a message bus that does not support exactly-once delivery. The job applies transformations and loads the output into BigQuery. You want to ensure the data is streamed into BigQuery with exactly-once delivery semantics. You expect BigQuery ingestion throughput of approximately 1.5 GB per second. What should you do?

options.text: Use the BigQuery Storage Write API and ensure that your target BigQuery table is regional.
Use the BigQuery Storage Write API and ensure that your target BigQuery table is multiregional.
Use the BigQuery Streaming API and ensure that your target BigQuery table is regional.
Use the BigQuery Streaming API and ensure that your target BigQuery table is multiregional.

questions.explanation:
Dataflow's `STORAGE_WRITE_API` write mode guarantees exactly-once semantics. BigQuery Storage Write API throughput is 3 GB/s in the US and EU multi-regions, while regional locations have a 300 MB/s quota; therefore, 1.5 GB/s requires a multiregional target table.

**Learn more:** [Write from Dataflow to BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/write-to-bigquery) · [BigQuery quotas and limits](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/quotas)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial services company has a critical daily reconciliation process with several distinct steps: retrieving data from an external SFTP server, decrypting the files, loading them into Cloud Storage, and finally executing a series of BigQuery SQL transformations. Each step has strict dependencies, and the entire process must notify you if it is not complete by 7:00 AM. Manual intervention for failures is expensive and delays compliance reporting. You need a highly observable, robust solution that allows individual steps to be easily re-run when errors occur. What should you do?

options.text: Develop a Cloud Composer DAG that includes a single PythonOperator to execute a Python script that runs each step sequentially, incorporating error handling and retries. Upload the scripts to a Cloud Composer environments DAGs folder, and configure it to run daily.
Implement a Cloud Composer DAG, with each step defined as a separate task using appropriate Airflow operators, and schedule the DAG for daily execution.

Define a Cloud Composer DAG to orchestrate the SFTP fetch and decryption steps, and then use Cloud Scheduler to trigger a separate Dataflow job that handles the Cloud Storage load and BigQuery transformations and schedule to run daily.

Create a Cloud Composer DAG that includes a single BashOperator to execute a top-level shell script, which in turn calls individual scripts for each pipeline step. Upload the scripts to a Cloud Composer environment’s DAGs folder, and configure it to run daily.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Composer DAG with a separate Airflow task for each pipeline step makes dependencies explicit and provides task-level status, logs, retries, and recovery. Failed tasks can be cleared and rerun independently, rather than repeating the entire reconciliation process. Cloud Composer supports monitoring individual DAG runs and tasks, and Airflow retries are configured at the task level.

**Learn more:** [Schedule and trigger Airflow DAGs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/composer/docs/composer-3/schedule-and-trigger-dags) · [View DAGs, DAG runs, and tasks](https://docs.cloud.google.com/composer/docs/composer-3/view-dags)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to store your team’s shared tables in one dataset so the data is readily available to multiple analysts. The data must be readable by analysts but not modifiable by them. At the same time, you need to give analysts individual workspaces in the same project where they can create and store tables for their own use, without those tables being accessible to other analysts. What should you do?

options.text: Give analysts the BigQuery Data Viewer role at the project level. Create one other dataset, and give the analysts the BigQuery Data Editor role on that dataset.
Give analysts the BigQuery Data Viewer role at the project level. Create a dataset for each analyst, and give each analyst the BigQuery Data Editor role at the project level.

Give analysts the BigQuery Data Viewer role on the shared dataset. Create a dataset for each analyst, and give each analyst the BigQuery Data Editor role at the dataset level for their assigned dataset.
Give analysts the BigQuery Data Viewer role on the shared dataset. Create one other dataset and give the analysts the BigQuery Data Editor role on that dataset.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery Data Viewer grants read access to the shared dataset without allowing table modifications. Assigning BigQuery Data Editor separately at the dataset level gives each analyst write access only to their own dataset, preserving isolation from other analysts’ tables.

questions.question: You are using Dataflow to create a streaming data pipeline that analyzes user website click activity from Pub/Sub. You need to calculate the number of clicks for each user site visit. A site visit is defined as a period of activity followed by 30 minutes of inactivity for a particular user. What should you do?

options.text: Use tumbling windows with a 30-minute window.
Use hopping windows with a 30-minute window, and a 1-minute period.
Use hopping windows with a 30-minute window, and a 30-minute period.
Use session windows with a 30-minute gap duration.

questions.explanation:
Session windows group events for each key based on inactivity: events within the configured gap belong to the same session, and an event after that gap starts a new session. A 30-minute gap duration therefore defines each user’s site visit correctly.\
\

questions.question: You are using Dataflow to create a streaming data pipeline that analyzes user website click activity from Pub/Sub. options.text: Cloud Spanner
Cloud Bigtable
Cloud Firestore
Cloud SQL

questions.explanation:
Cloud SQL is a fully managed, cost-effective relational database service for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server. It supports migrating an existing relational application with minimal refactoring while reducing database-administration overhead. Cloud Bigtable and Cloud Firestore are NoSQL services, while Cloud Spanner is intended for horizontally scalable, globally distributed relational workloads and is generally a less cost-focused fit for this requirement.

**Learn more:** [Cloud SQL overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/introduction) · [Cloud SQL product page](https://cloud.google.com/sql)

Dialogflow Enterprise Edition
AutoML Natural Language

questions.explanation:
Dialogflow Enterprise Edition provides conversational intent recognition for voice interactions and supports fulfillment logic that calls backend services to complete actions such as order placement. Speech transcription, general text analysis, and custom text-model training alone do not provide this end-to-end conversational fulfillment capability.\
\
**Learn more:** [Fulfillments | Dialogflow CX | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/fulfillment)

questions.question: You are a retailer that wants to integrate its online sales capabilities with various in-home assistants, such as Google Home. You need to interpret customer voice commands and submit an order to backend systems. Which solution should you choose?

options.text: Use Analytics Hub to facilitate data sharing.
Create authorized datasets to publish shared data in the subscribing team's project.
Create a new dataset for sharing in each individual team’s project. Grant the subscribing team the bigquery.dataViewer role on the dataset.
Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to copy datasets to a centralized BigQuery project for sharing.

questions.explanation:
Analytics Hub supports a secure publish-and-subscribe model for BigQuery data, including discovery of listings and self-service subscriptions. A subscription creates a read-only linked dataset that references the shared source rather than copying it, which provides zero-copy sharing, avoids replication costs, and makes current source data available to subscribers.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to BigQuery sharing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/analytics-hub-introduction?hl=en)

questions.question: MJTelco's Google Cloud Dataflow pipeline is now prepared to begin receiving data from the 50,000 installations. You want Cloud Dataflow to scale its compute power up as needed. Which Cloud Dataflow pipeline configuration setting should you update?

options.text: The zone
The number of workers
The disk size per worker
The maximum number of workers

questions.explanation:
Dataflow horizontal autoscaling increases or decreases worker instances according to pipeline demand. The maximum number of workers (`maxNumWorkers`) defines the upper limit of worker instances that Dataflow can allocate during execution; the number of workers only establishes the initial worker count.\
\
**Learn more:** [Horizontal Autoscaling | Cloud Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/horizontal-autoscaling) · [Pipeline options | Cloud Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/pipeline-options)

questions.question: MJTelco's Google Cloud Dataflow pipeline is now prepared to begin receiving data from the 50,000 installations. You want Cloud Dataflow to scale its compute power up as needed. Which Cloud Dataflow pipeline configuration setting should you update?

options.text: Implement a data pipeline using Pub/Sub for streaming the data changes from MySQL.
Configure a scheduled transfer in BigQuery Data Transfer Service to ingest data from the MySQL database with a scheduled transfer configuration.
Leverage Database Migration Service for continuous replication of the entire database to Cloud SQL.
Use Cloud SQL federated queries to directly query the on-premises MySQL database from BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery Data Transfer Service provides a managed MySQL connector for MySQL instances hosted on premises and can run recurring scheduled transfers into BigQuery. Its incremental-transfer mode loads only data changed since the prior transfer, with append or upsert write modes.

**Learn more:** [Load MySQL data into BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/mysql-transfer)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A live TV program lets viewers vote with their mobile phones. The event produces a high volume of data over a 3-minute window. You are responsible for the **Voting infrastructure** and must make sure the platform handles the load and every vote is processed. Partial results must be shown while voting remains open. Once voting is closed, the votes must be counted exactly once while optimizing cost. What should you do?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783859953708-zy08s6zj.png)

options.text: Create a Memorystore instance with a high availability (HA) configuration.
Create a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database with high availability (HA) configuration and multiple read replicas.
Write votes to a Pub/Sub topic and have Cloud Functions subscribe to it and write votes to BigQuery.

Write votes to a Pub/Sub topic and load into both Bigtable and BigQuery via a Dataflow pipeline. Query Bigtable for real-time results and BigQuery for later analysis. Shut down the Bigtable instance when voting concludes.

questions.explanation:
Pub/Sub provides durable, asynchronous ingestion that decouples the burst of vote submissions from processing. A Dataflow streaming pipeline can process the stream and write it to both Bigtable and BigQuery. Bigtable supports high read/write throughput with low latency, making it suitable for serving live partial results, while BigQuery retains the data for the final analysis and count. Removing the temporary Bigtable capacity after voting ends minimizes the cost of the short-lived real-time serving workload.

**Learn more:** [Bigtable overview](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/overview) · [Stream from Pub/Sub to BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/tutorials/dataflow-stream-to-bigquery)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your platform in an on-premises environment produces **100 GB** of data each day, consisting of millions of structured JSON text files. The on-premises environment is not accessible from the public internet. You want to use Google Cloud products to query and explore the platform data. What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Scheduler to copy data daily from your on-premises environment to Cloud Storage. Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to import data into BigQuery.
Use a Transfer Appliance to copy data from your on-premises environment to Cloud Storage. Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to import data into BigQuery.
Use Transfer Service for on-premises data to copy data from your on-premises environment to Cloud Storage. Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to import data into BigQuery.
Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service dataset copy to transfer all data into BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
Storage Transfer Service for on-premises data uses transfer agents in the on-premises environment to move files to Cloud Storage without requiring the source environment to be publicly reachable. BigQuery Data Transfer Service can schedule recurring loads from Cloud Storage into BigQuery and supports newline-delimited JSON files, enabling the data to be queried and explored in BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Protect file system data — Storage Transfer Service](https://cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/on-prem-security) · [Load Cloud Storage data into BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/cloud-storage-transfer)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying a batch pipeline in Dataflow. The pipeline reads data from Cloud Storage, transforms it, and then writes it to BigQuery. The security team has enabled an organizational constraint in Google Cloud that requires every Compute Engine instance to use only internal IP addresses and no external IP addresses. What should you do?

options.text: Ensure that your workers have network tags to access Cloud Storage and BigQuery. Use Dataflow with only internal IP addresses.
Ensure that the firewall rules allow access to Cloud Storage and BigQuery. Use Dataflow with only internal IPs.
Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter that contains the VPC network and add Dataflow, Cloud Storage, and BigQuery as allowed services in the perimeter. Use Dataflow with only internal IP addresses.
Ensure that Private Google Access is enabled in the subnetwork. Use Dataflow with only internal IP addresses.

questions.explanation:
Dataflow workers that use only internal IP addresses require Private Google Access on their subnetwork to reach Google APIs and services, including Cloud Storage and BigQuery. This is required when external IP addresses are disabled.

**Learn more:** [Plan your Dataflow pipeline](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/plan-pipelines) · [Troubleshoot Dataflow networking issues](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/troubleshoot-networking)

questions.question: You submit a new batch job to Dataflow. The job starts successfully, processes several elements, and then unexpectedly fails and shuts down. You open the Dataflow monitoring interface and see errors related to a specific `DoFn` in the pipeline. What is the most likely cause of these errors?

options.text: Job validation
Exceptions in worker code
Graph or pipeline construction
Insufficient permissions

questions.explanation:
Exceptions in Apache Beam user code, including a `DoFn`, are reported in the Dataflow monitoring interface. An unhandled exception while processing an element causes its work item to fail; repeated failures of a batch work item cause Dataflow to fail the pipeline.\
\
**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot Dataflow errors](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/common-errors)

questions.question: You submit a new batch job to Dataflow. The job starts successfully, processes several elements, and then unexpectedly fails and shuts down. You open the Dataflow monitoring interface and see errors related to a specific `DoFn` in the pipeline. What is the most likely cause of these errors?

options.text: BigQuery
Cloud SQL
Cloud Bigtable
Cloud Datastore

questions.explanation:
Cloud SQL is a fully managed relational database service and is appropriate for structured transactional data with related user, account, and order records. A relational schema supports normalized tables, relationships, and transactional integrity for the operational data of the service.

**Learn more:** [Cloud SQL overview](https://cloud.google.com/sql)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a manufacturing plant that combines application log files into one log file each day at 2:00 AM. You have written a Google Cloud Dataflow job to process this log file. You need to ensure that the log file is processed once daily as inexpensively as possible. What should you do?

options.text: Change the processing job to use Google Cloud Dataproc instead.
Manually start the Cloud Dataflow job each morning when you get into the office.
Create a cron job with Google App Engine Cron Service to run the Cloud Dataflow job.
Configure the Cloud Dataflow job as a streaming job so that it processes the log data immediately.

questions.explanation:
App Engine Cron Service supports recurring scheduled tasks and can invoke an App Engine handler that launches a Dataflow pipeline. Scheduling the existing batch pipeline once per day processes the consolidated file automatically without operating a continuously running streaming job.

**Learn more:** [Scheduling Dataflow pipelines using App Engine Cron Service or Cloud Functions](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/scheduling-dataflow-pipelines-using-app-engine-cron-service-or-cloud-functions) · [Scheduling jobs with cron.yaml](https://docs.cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/flexible/scheduling-jobs-with-cron-yaml)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your large e-commerce company relies on BigQuery for its data warehousing requirements. It has two main workload types:  
  
- **Analyst dashboards:** Interactive queries that business analysts run throughout the day and that require low latency for real-time insights.  
- **ETL jobs:** Large, complex batch queries that load and transform data overnight. These jobs are cost-sensitive, can tolerate longer execution times, and do not have the same performance requirements as the dashboards.  
  
Analysts report inconsistent dashboard performance, especially during peak business hours. You must ensure dependable performance for both workload types while optimizing costs. What should you do?

options.text: Use BigQuery editions to create an autoscaling reservation with dedicated slots for analyst dashboards, while running ETL jobs with a separate reservation or using the on-demand billing model.
Implement a custom autoscaling solution using Cloud Run functions to dynamically adjust available BigQuery slots based on time of day.
Migrate all ETL jobs to Cloud SQL to reduce BigQuery’s workload.
Run all analyst dashboard queries as interactive queries and configure ETL jobs to run as batch queries.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery reservations allocate slots into workload-specific pools and can isolate critical production workloads from competing ETL activity. An autoscaling reservation assigned to dashboard workloads supplies capacity as demand changes, while a separate ETL reservation or on-demand pricing lets the less time-sensitive, cost-sensitive batch workload use an appropriate cost model. BigQuery documentation identifies separate reservations and assignments as a way to isolate workloads and improve performance consistency.

**Learn more:** [Understand reservations | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reservations-workload-management) · [Get started with reservations | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reservations-get-started)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You configured a streaming data insertion into a Redis cluster through a Kafka cluster. Both clusters run on Compute Engine instances. You must encrypt data at rest using encryption keys that you can create, rotate, and destroy as needed. What should you do?

options.text: Create a dedicated service account, and use encryption at rest to reference your data stored in your Compute Engine cluster instances as part of your API service calls.
Create encryption keys in Cloud Key Management Service. Use those keys to encrypt your data in all of the Compute Engine cluster instances.
Create encryption keys locally. Upload your encryption keys to Cloud Key Management Service. Use those keys to encrypt your data in all of the Compute Engine cluster instances.
Create encryption keys in Cloud Key Management Service. Reference those keys in your API service calls when accessing the data in your Compute Engine cluster instances.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Key Management Service customer-managed encryption keys (CMEKs) let you control the key lifecycle, including rotation and destruction, and can be used to protect Compute Engine storage resources at rest. The KMS key is configured for the Compute Engine resource rather than supplied in application API calls.

**Learn more:** [Protect resources with Cloud KMS keys](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/customer-managed-encryption) · [About disk encryption](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/disk-encryption)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a BigQuery administrator supporting data consumers who run ad hoc queries and downstream reports in tools such as Looker. All data and users are consolidated under one organizational project. You recently observed slower query results and want to troubleshoot where the delays are occurring. You suspect that job queuing or slot contention might be happening as users run jobs, slowing access to results. You need to investigate query-job information and identify where performance is being impacted. What should you do?

options.text: Use slot reservations for your project to ensure that you have enough query processing capacity and are able to allocate available slots to the slower queries.
Use Cloud Monitoring to view BigQuery metrics and set up alerts that let you know when a certain percentage of slots were used.
Use available administrative resource charts to determine how slots are being used and how jobs are performing over time. Run a query on the INFORMATION_SCHEMA to review query performance.
Use Cloud Logging to determine if any users or downstream consumers are changing or deleting access grants on tagged resources.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery administrative resource charts expose historical slot usage, job concurrency, and job-duration trends, making them suitable for locating contention and queue-related slowdowns. Querying `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` job views supplies near-real-time job metadata and performance details for investigating the affected queries. [Monitor health, resource utilization, and jobs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/admin-resource-charts) [JOBS view](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/information-schema-jobs)

**Learn more:** [Monitor health, resource utilization, and jobs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/admin-resource-charts) · [JOBS view](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/information-schema-jobs)

options.text: Use Cloud Dataproc to run your transformations. Monitor CPU utilization for the cluster. Resize the number of worker nodes in your cluster via the command line.
Use Cloud Dataproc to run your transformations. Use the diagnose command to generate an operational output archive. Locate the bottleneck and adjust cluster resources.
Use Cloud Dataflow to run your transformations. Monitor the job system lag with Stackdriver. Use the default autoscaling setting for worker instances.
Use Cloud Dataflow to run your transformations. Monitor the total execution time for a sampling of jobs. Configure the job to use non-default Compute Engine machine types when needed.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Dataflow runs managed streaming transformations and horizontal autoscaling can add or remove worker instances as workload demand changes. Cloud Monitoring exposes system-lag metrics for streaming Dataflow jobs, enabling monitoring while autoscaling handles fluctuating input volume without manual cluster resizing.

**Learn more:** [Use Cloud Monitoring for Dataflow pipelines](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/using-cloud-monitoring) · [Horizontal Autoscaling](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/horizontal-autoscaling)

An external customer sends you a daily database data dump. The data lands in Google Cloud Storage (GCS) as comma-separated values (CSV) files. You want to analyze the data in Google BigQuery, but some rows might be incorrectly formatted or corrupted. How should you build this pipeline?

options.text: Use federated data sources, and check data in the SQL query.
Enable BigQuery monitoring in Google Stackdriver and create an alert.
Import the data into BigQuery using the gcloud CLI and set max_bad_records to 0.
Run a Google Cloud Dataflow batch pipeline to import the data into BigQuery, and push errors to another dead-letter table for analysis.

questions.explanation:
A batch Dataflow pipeline can ingest CSV files from Cloud Storage into BigQuery while separating rejected CSV records into a bad-records/dead-letter table for later analysis. The Google-provided Cloud Storage CSV-to-BigQuery template supports a `badRecordsOutputTable` specifically for rejected data, allowing valid records to be loaded without losing visibility into malformed or corrupted rows.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage CSV files to BigQuery template](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/templates/provided/cloud-storage-csv-to-bigquery) · [Write from Dataflow to BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/write-to-bigquery)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You currently operate a single on-premises Kafka cluster in a data center in the `us-east` region that ingests messages from IoT devices worldwide.  
  
Because large parts of the globe have unreliable internet connectivity, messages can accumulate at the edge, arrive simultaneously, and create a load spike on your Kafka cluster. This is becoming hard to manage and prohibitively costly. What is the Google-recommended cloud-native architecture for this scenario?

options.text: Edge TPUs as sensor devices for storing and transmitting the messages.
Cloud Dataflow connected to the Kafka cluster to scale the processing of incoming messages.
An IoT gateway connected to Cloud Pub/Sub, with Cloud Dataflow to read and process the messages from Cloud Pub/Sub.
A Kafka cluster virtualized on Compute Engine in us-east with Cloud Load Balancing to connect to the devices around the world.

questions.explanation:
An IoT gateway can aggregate data from remote devices and connect directly to Cloud Pub/Sub. Pub/Sub is a highly scalable asynchronous messaging service that decouples publishers from consumers, allowing ingestion bursts to be buffered independently of downstream processing. Dataflow can then read and process the Pub/Sub stream using managed streaming infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Device on Pub/Sub connection to Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/connected-devices/device-pubsub-architecture?hl=en) · [Architectural overview of Pub/Sub](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/architecture)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must insert minute-resolution data from 50,000 sensors into a BigQuery table. You anticipate substantial growth in data volume and require the data to be available within 1 minute of ingestion for real-time analysis of aggregated trends. What should you do?

options.text: Use bq load to load a batch of sensor data every 60 seconds.
Use a Cloud Dataflow pipeline to stream data into the BigQuery table.
Use the INSERT statement to insert a batch of data every 60 seconds.
Use the MERGE statement to apply updates in batch every 60 seconds.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Dataflow supports scalable streaming pipelines with low latency and is appropriate for processing sensor data at scale and writing it to BigQuery. BigQuery guidance specifically recommends Dataflow when custom streaming sources or preprocessing must be streamed into BigQuery at large throughput; streaming data supports near-real-time analysis.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to loading data | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data) · [Dataflow overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use Bigtable to store and serve stock-market data for each major index. To support the trading application, you must retrieve only the latest streaming stock prices. How should you design the row key and tables so the data can be accessed with the simplest query?

options.text: Create one unique table for all of the indices, and then use the index and timestamp as the row key design.
Create one unique table for all of the indices, and then use a reverse timestamp as the row key design.
For each index, have a separate table and use a timestamp as the row key design.
For each index, have a separate table and use a reverse timestamp as the row key design.

questions.explanation:
A reversed timestamp orders rows from newest to oldest in Bigtable. Keeping each index in its own table lets a forward read of the first row return that index’s latest price, without a reverse scan or filtering through records for other indices.

**Learn more:** [Schema design best practices | Bigtable | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design?hl=en)

An encryption key stored in Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS) has been exposed. You must re-encrypt all CMEK-protected Cloud Storage data that used this key, and then delete the compromised key. You also want to lower the risk that objects are written without customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) protection in the future. What should you do?

options.text: Rotate the Cloud KMS key version. Continue to use the same Cloud Storage bucket.
Create a new Cloud KMS key. Set the default CMEK key on the existing Cloud Storage bucket to the new one.
Create a new Cloud KMS key. Create a new Cloud Storage bucket. Copy all objects from the old bucket to the new one bucket while specifying the new Cloud KMS key in the copy command.
Create a new Cloud KMS key. Create a new Cloud Storage bucket configured to use the new key as the default CMEK key. Copy all objects from the old bucket to the new bucket without specifying a key.

questions.explanation:
Cloud KMS key rotation does not automatically re-encrypt data already encrypted with an earlier key version. Rewriting objects by copying them to a new bucket encrypts the destination objects again. A bucket default CMEK is applied to objects added to that bucket when no object-specific key is supplied, so configuring the new bucket with the replacement key protects both the copied objects and future writes. After the old objects have been re-encrypted and no longer require the compromised key, its key version can be destroyed.

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed encryption keys | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/customer-managed-keys) · [Key rotation | Cloud Key Management Service](https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/key-rotation)

You have designed a BigQuery data warehouse for analyzing sales data. You need a self-service, low-maintenance, cost-effective way to share the sales dataset with other business units in your organization. What should you do?

options.text: Create an Analytics Hub private exchange, and publish the sales dataset.
Enable the other business units’ projects to access the authorized views of the sales dataset.
Create and share views with the users in the other business units.
Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to create a schedule that copies the sales dataset to the other business units’ projects.

questions.explanation:
A private Analytics Hub exchange supports governed, self-service sharing of a BigQuery dataset within an organization. Subscribers can create read-only linked datasets, so the shared data is accessed without replication; this avoids maintaining copied datasets and their associated storage and refresh costs.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to BigQuery sharing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/analytics-hub-introduction?hl=en) · [Manage data exchanges](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/analytics-hub-manage-exchanges?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An aerospace company stores its flight data in a proprietary data format. You need to connect this new data source to BigQuery and stream the data into BigQuery. You want to import the data into BigQuery efficiently while using as few resources as possible. What should you do?

options.text: Write a shell script that triggers a Cloud Function that performs periodic ETL batch jobs on the new data source.
Use a standard Dataflow pipeline to store the raw data in BigQuery, and then transform the format later when the data is used.
Use Apache Hive to write a Dataproc job that streams the data into BigQuery in CSV format.
Use an Apache Beam custom connector to write a Dataflow pipeline that streams the data into BigQuery in Avro format.

questions.explanation:
A custom Apache Beam I/O connector lets a Dataflow streaming pipeline read a proprietary source directly and transform its records for BigQuery. Avro is an efficient BigQuery load format; Google Cloud documentation notes that Avro typically outperforms JSON for file loads.

**Learn more:** [Apache Beam I/O connector best practices](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/io-connector-best-practices) · [Write from Dataflow to BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/write-to-bigquery)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are moving your data warehouse to BigQuery. All data has been migrated into tables within a dataset. Multiple users in your organization will use this data, but they must be able to view only particular tables according to their team membership. How should user permissions be configured?

options.text: Assign the users/groups data viewer access at the table level for each table
Create SQL views for each team in the same dataset in which the data resides, and assign the users/groups data viewer access to the SQL views
Create authorized views for each team in the same dataset in which the data resides, and assign the users/groups data viewer access to the authorized views

Create authorized views for each team in datasets created for each team. Assign the authorized views data viewer access to the dataset in which the data resides. Assign the users/groups data viewer access to the datasets in which the authorized views reside

questions.explanation:
Authorized views expose only the selected table data while withholding direct access to the underlying source tables. BigQuery requires an authorized view to be in a dataset different from the source-data dataset. Authorizing those views against the source dataset and granting each team Data Viewer access only to its view dataset enforces team-specific access without granting access to the underlying dataset.

**Learn more:** [Authorized views | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/authorized-views)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are selecting a NoSQL database to process telemetry data submitted by millions of Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices. Data volume is increasing by 100 TB per year, and every data entry contains about 100 attributes. The data-processing pipeline does not need atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability (ACID).  
  
High availability and low latency are required. You need to analyze the data by querying individual fields. Which three databases satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Redis
HBase
MySQL
MongoDB
Cassandra
HDFS with Hive

questions.explanation:
HBase provides distributed, scalable storage with random real-time read/write access and is suited to massive IoT telemetry streams. MongoDB stores flexible documents as field/value pairs and supplies field-oriented query capabilities, horizontal scaling, and built-in high availability. Cassandra is a distributed NoSQL database designed for linear scale, high availability, and low-latency reads and writes, with an eventually consistent model appropriate when full ACID guarantees are unnecessary.

**Learn more:** [Apache HBase Home](https://hbase.apache.org/) · [What is MongoDB?](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to build a machine learning model with BigQuery ML and create a Vertex AI endpoint to host the model. This must support near-real-time processing of continuous streaming data from multiple vendors. The data can include invalid values. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new BigQuery dataset and use streaming inserts to land the data from multiple vendors. Configure your BigQuery ML model to use the
Use BigQuery streaming inserts to land the data from multiple vendors where your BigQuery dataset ML model is deployed.
Create a Pub/Sub topic and send all vendor data to it. Connect a Cloud Function to the topic to process the data and store it in BigQuery.
Create a Pub/Sub topic and send all vendor data to it. Use Dataflow to process and sanitize the Pub/Sub data and stream it to BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
Pub/Sub decouples multiple streaming data producers from consumers, and Dataflow provides a managed streaming pipeline for transforming, validating, and sanitizing records before they are written to BigQuery. This ensures invalid data can be handled before it is used by the BigQuery ML workflow. Google’s Pub/Sub-to-BigQuery Dataflow patterns support streaming ingestion and message transformation, including field validation.

**Learn more:** [Stream from Pub/Sub to BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/tutorials/dataflow-stream-to-bigquery) · [Performance characteristics of Pub/Sub to BigQuery pipelines](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/pubsub-bigquery-performance)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to migrate an existing Teradata data warehouse to BigQuery. You need to move the historical data to BigQuery by using the most efficient method requiring the least programming, but local storage on the existing data warehouse is limited. What should you do?

options.text: Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service by using the Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) driver with FastExport connection.
Create a Teradata Parallel Transporter (TPT) export script to export the historical data, and import to BigQuery by using the bq command-line tool.
Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service with the Teradata Parallel Transporter (TPT) tbuild utility.
Create a script to export the historical data, and upload in batches to Cloud Storage. Set up a BigQuery Data Transfer Service instance from Cloud Storage to BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery Data Transfer Service, together with its Teradata migration agent, supports Teradata Parallel Transporter (TPT) extraction through the `tbuild` utility. TPT is the recommended, typically faster extraction method, and the migration agent uploads extracted files to Cloud Storage and deletes them from the local staging directory, minimizing ongoing local-storage use.

**Learn more:** [Teradata to BigQuery migration: Overview](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/migration/teradata-overview) · [Migrate schema and data from Teradata](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/migration/teradata)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You stream order data using a Dataflow pipeline and write the aggregated output to Memorystore. You provisioned a Memorystore for Redis instance with Basic Tier and 4 GB capacity, which 40 clients use for read-only access. You expect the number of read-only clients to rise significantly to a few hundred and need to support that demand. You want to ensure read and write availability is unaffected and that any changes can be deployed quickly. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new Memorystore for Redis instance with Standard Tier. Set capacity to 4 GB and read replica to No read replicas (high availability only). Delete the old instance.
Create a new Memorystore for Redis instance with Standard Tier. Set capacity to 5 GB and create multiple read replicas. Delete the old instance.

Create a new Memorystore for Memcached instance. Set a minimum of three nodes, and memory per node to 4 GB. Modify the Dataflow pipeline and all clients to use the Memcached instance. Delete the old instance.
Create multiple new Memorystore for Redis instances with Basic Tier (4 GB capacity). Modify the Dataflow pipeline and new clients to use all instances.

questions.explanation:
Memorystore for Redis Standard Tier with read replicas provides replication, automatic failover, and distributed read capacity. Read-only clients can use the read endpoint, which balances connections across the replicas, while writes continue through the primary endpoint. Read replicas require a node size of at least 5 GB; therefore, a new 5 GB Standard Tier instance with multiple read replicas satisfies both the scaling and availability requirements.

**Learn more:** [Redis tier capabilities](https://docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/redis-tiers) · [About read replicas](https://docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/about-read-replicas)

You migrated a Hadoop job from an on-premises cluster to Dataproc and GCS. Your Spark job is a complex analytical workload with many shuffle operations, and the initial data consists of Parquet files averaging 200–400 MB each. After migrating to Dataproc, you observe some performance degradation and want to optimize it. Your organization is highly cost-sensitive, so you want to keep using Dataproc on preemptible VMs, with only 2 non-preemptible workers for this workload.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Increase the size of your parquet files to ensure them to be 1 GB minimum.
Switch to TFRecords formats (appr. 200MB per file) instead of parquet files.
Switch from HDDs to SSDs, copy initial data from GCS to HDFS, run the Spark job and copy results back to GCS.
Switch from HDDs to SSDs, override the preemptible VMs configuration to increase the boot disk size.

questions.explanation:
Shuffle data is written to worker-local disks. SSD-backed disks provide substantially better IOPS for shuffle-heavy Spark workloads, while increasing the preemptible workers’ boot-disk size provides additional shuffle capacity and can increase persistent-disk throughput. Keeping the source data in Cloud Storage avoids relying on transient HDFS storage on a preemptible-worker cluster.

**Learn more:** [Hadoop data storage | Managed Service for Apache Spark](https://docs.cloud.google.com/managed-spark/docs/concepts/hdfs) · [Dataproc Enhanced Flexibility Mode](https://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/concepts/configuring-clusters/enhanced-flexibility-mode)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing storage for 20 TB of text files while deploying a data pipeline on Google Cloud. Your input data is in CSV format. You want to minimize the cost of querying aggregate values for multiple users who will query the data in Cloud Storage with multiple engines. Which storage service and schema design should you use?

options.text: Use Cloud Bigtable for storage. Install the HBase shell on a Compute Engine instance to query the Cloud Bigtable data.
Use Cloud Bigtable for storage. Link as permanent tables in BigQuery for query.
Use Cloud Storage for storage. Link as permanent tables in BigQuery for query.
Use Cloud Storage for storage. Link as temporary tables in BigQuery for query.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage provides economical shared storage for CSV files that can be accessed by multiple query engines. A permanent BigQuery external table defines a reusable schema over the Cloud Storage data and can be shared with users who have access to the underlying files. Temporary external tables are for one-time or ad hoc queries and cannot be shared.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to external tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/external-tables) · [Create Cloud Storage external tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/external-data-cloud-storage)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You run your BigQuery project using the on-demand billing model and execute a change data capture (CDC) process that ingests data. The CDC process loads 1 GB of data every 10 minutes into a temporary table, then performs a merge into a 10 TB target table. This process is highly scan-intensive, and you want to investigate options that provide a predictable cost model.  
  
You need to create a BigQuery reservation using utilization information collected from BigQuery Monitoring and apply the reservation to the CDC process. What should you do?

options.text: Create a BigQuery reservation for the dataset.
Create a BigQuery reservation for the job.
Create a BigQuery reservation for the service account running the job.
Create a BigQuery reservation for the project.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery reservations provide dedicated slot capacity for predictable compute costs. A reservation assignment links a project, folder, or organization to the reservation, and query jobs submitted by an assigned project use that reservation’s slots. Assigning the CDC workload’s project is therefore the appropriate scope.

**Learn more:** [Manage workload assignments](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reservations-assignments?hl=en) · [Get started with reservations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reservations-get-started)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A TensorFlow machine learning model running on Compute Engine virtual machines (`n2-standard-32`) takes two days to finish training. The model uses custom TensorFlow operations that must execute partially on a CPU. You want to reduce the training time cost-effectively. What should you do?

options.text: Change the VM type to n2-highmem-32.
Change the VM type to e2-standard-32.
Train the model using a VM with a GPU hardware accelerator.
Train the model using a VM with a TPU hardware accelerator.

questions.explanation:
GPU-attached Compute Engine VMs can accelerate TensorFlow training while retaining CPU execution for custom or unsupported operations. Cloud TPUs are optimized for compatible, XLA-compiled matrix workloads and are not suited to neural-network workloads with custom operations in the main training loop; simply changing CPU VM families does not add accelerator compute.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Cloud TPU](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/intro-to-tpu) · [Available TensorFlow Ops](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/tensorflow-ops)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to schedule multiple sequential loading and transformation jobs. An upstream process will add data files to a Cloud Storage bucket, but there is no set schedule for when new data arrives. Next, a Dataproc job is triggered to perform transformations and write the data to BigQuery. You must then run additional transformation jobs in BigQuery. The transformation jobs differ for every table. These jobs can take hours to finish. You need to identify the most efficient and maintainable workflow for processing hundreds of tables while delivering the freshest data to end users. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Create an Apache Airflow directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer with sequential tasks by using the Cloud Storage, Dataproc, and BigQuery operators.2. Use a single shared DAG for all tables that need to go through the pipeline.3. Schedule the DAG to run hourly.

1. Create an Apache Airflow directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer with sequential tasks by using the Cloud Storage, Dataproc, and BigQuery operators.2. Create a separate DAG for each table that needs to go through the pipeline.3. Schedule the DAGs to run hourly.

1. Create an Apache Airflow directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer with sequential tasks by using the Dataproc and BigQuery operators.2. Use a single shared DAG for all tables that need to go through the pipeline.3. Use a Cloud Storage object trigger to launch a Cloud Function that triggers the DAG.

1. Create an Apache Airflow directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer with sequential tasks by using the Dataproc and BigQuery operators.2. Create a separate DAG for each table that needs to go through the pipeline.3. Use a Cloud Storage object trigger to launch a Cloud Function that triggers the DAG.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Storage object trigger provides event-driven processing as soon as new data arrives, avoiding the latency of an hourly schedule. A Cloud Function can invoke a Cloud Composer DAG through the Airflow REST API, and each DAG can sequence the Dataproc transformation followed by its table-specific BigQuery transformations. Separate DAGs isolate the distinct, long-running workflows for individual tables and allow independent execution and maintenance.

**Learn more:** [Trigger DAGs with Cloud Functions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/composer/docs/composer-3/triggering-with-gcf?hl=en) · [Schedule and trigger Airflow DAGs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/composer/docs/composer-2/schedule-and-trigger-dags)

You have a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance in Region’ with one read replica in Region2 and another read replica in Region3. An unexpected event in Region’ requires you to perform disaster recovery by promoting the read replica in Region2. You need to ensure that your application has the same database capacity available before you switch over the connections. What should you do?

options.text: Enable zonal high availability on the primary instance. Create a new read replica in a new region.
Create a cascading read replica from the existing read replica in Region3.
Create two new read replicas from the new primary instance, one in Region3 and one in a new region.
Create a new read replica in Region1, promote the new read replica to be the primary instance, and enable zonal high availability.

questions.explanation:
After a read replica is promoted, it becomes a standalone writable primary. Other replicas of the former primary must be recreated from the newly promoted primary. Creating two new replicas from the new primary restores the original capacity of one primary and two read replicas before application connections are redirected.

**Learn more:** [Promote replicas for regional migration or disaster recovery | Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/replication/cross-region-replicas) · [About replication in Cloud SQL | Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/replication)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a model to identify the factors that result in sales conversions for your customers. You have finished processing the data and want to proceed with the model-development lifecycle. What should you do next?

options.text: Use your model to run predictions on fresh customer input data.
Monitor your model performance, and make any adjustments needed.
Delineate what data will be used for testing and what will be used for training the model.
Test and evaluate your model on your curated data to determine how well the model performs.

questions.explanation:
After data processing, the curated dataset should be divided into training and testing portions. The training data is used to fit the model, and the held-out test data is used later to assess how well the trained model generalizes. Making predictions on new inputs and monitoring performance occur after the model is deployed.

**Learn more:** [Google Machine Learning Crash Course: Datasets, Generalization, and Overfitting](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/generalization/peril-of-overfitting)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing an architecture that processes data from Cloud Storage to BigQuery by using Dataflow. The network team has supplied the Shared VPC network and subnetwork that your pipelines must use. You need to enable deployment of the pipeline on the Shared VPC network. What should you do?

options.text: Assign the compute.networkUser role to the Dataflow service agent.
Assign the compute.networkUser role to the service account that executes the Dataflow pipeline.
Assign the dataflow.admin role to the Dataflow service agent.
Assign the dataflow.admin role to the service account that executes the Dataflow pipeline.

questions.explanation:
A Shared VPC subnetwork used by Dataflow must grant the Compute Network User role (`roles/compute.networkUser`) to the Dataflow service agent, typically at the specified subnet level in the host project. This permits Dataflow to use the shared subnet when it creates and manages worker VMs; the Dataflow Admin role does not supply this network-use permission.

**Learn more:** [Specify a network and subnetwork | Cloud Dataflow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/specifying-networks) · [Troubleshoot Dataflow permissions | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/troubleshoot-permissions)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage a Dataplex environment that contains raw and curated zones. A data engineering team uploads JSON and CSV files to a bucket asset in the curated zone, but Dataplex does not automatically discover the files. What should you do to ensure Dataplex discovers them?

options.text: Move the JSON and CSV files to the raw zone.
Enable auto-discovery of files for the curated zone.
Use the bg command-line tool to load the JSON and CSV files into BigQuery tables.
Grant object level access to the CSV and JSON files in Cloud Storage.

questions.explanation:
For Cloud Storage assets in a curated Dataplex zone, structured data must use Parquet, Avro, or ORC and be organized in a Hive-compatible directory layout. CSV and JSON are supported semi-structured formats for raw zones, so the files must be placed in the raw zone for Dataplex discovery. [Google Cloud Dataplex Zone reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataplex/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.lakes.zones)

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud Dataplex Zone reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataplex/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.lakes.zones)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are troubleshooting a Dataflow pipeline that moves data from Cloud Storage to BigQuery. You discovered that the Dataflow worker nodes cannot communicate with each other. Your networking team uses Google Cloud network tags to define firewall rules. You need to identify the issue while following Google-recommended networking security practices. What should you do?

options.text: Determine whether your Dataflow pipeline has a custom network tag set.
Determine whether there is a firewall rule set to allow traffic on TCP ports 12345 and 12346 for the Dataflow network tag.
Determine whether there is a firewall rule set to allow traffic on TCP ports 12345 and 12346 on the subnet used by Dataflow workers.
Determine whether your Dataflow pipeline is deployed with the external IP address option enabled.

questions.explanation:
Dataflow workers that require direct inter-worker communication must be allowed to send and receive traffic on TCP ports 12345 and 12346. Firewall rules should target and source the Dataflow network tag so that access is limited to the worker VMs instead of being opened broadly across the subnet.

**Learn more:** [Configure internet access and firewall rules | Cloud Dataflow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/routes-firewall) · [Troubleshoot Dataflow networking issues | Cloud Dataflow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/troubleshoot-networking)
