questions.question:
You have data shown in the graphic below. Its two dimensions are X and Y, and each dot’s shade indicates its class. You want to classify this data accurately with a linear algorithm. To do so, you need to add a synthetic feature. What should that feature’s value be?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783786969594-rbm3cksy.jpg)

options.text: X2+Y2
X2
Y2
cos(X)

questions.explanation: The feature X² + Y² is the squared Euclidean distance from the origin. It converts concentric, center-versus-outer-region class structure into a one-dimensional threshold that a linear classifier can separate.

questions.question:
You have data shown in the graphic below. Its two dimensions are X and Y, and each dot’s shade indicates its class. You want to classify this data accurately with a linear algorithm. To do so, you need to add a synthetic feature. What should that feature’s value be?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783786969594-rbm3cksy.jpg)

options.text: Store and process the entire dataset in BigQuery.
Store and process the entire dataset in Bigtable.
Store the full dataset in BigQuery, and store a compressed copy of the data in a Cloud Storage bucket.
Store the warm data as files in Cloud Storage, and store the active data in BigQuery. Keep this ratio as 80% warm and 20% active.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery provides managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse analytics. Keeping a compressed copy in Cloud Storage exposes the data as portable files for batch tools, while BigQuery remains the analytics store. BigQuery supports exporting table data to Cloud Storage in file formats such as CSV, JSON, Avro, and Parquet.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to data export | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/export-intro) · [Export table data to Cloud Storage | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/exporting-data)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis

options.text: Use the Gemini 2.5 Pro model in Vertex AI to analyze the images and store the results in BigQuery.
Use the ML.UNDERSTAND_TEXT function along with object tables to analyze the images, and store the JSON output in a Cloud Storage bucket.
Use Vertex AI Vision API to analyze the images and store the results in BigQuery.
Use the ML.GENERATE_TEXT function along with object tables to analyze the images and store the JSON output in a BigQuery table.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery object tables provide SQL access to unstructured Cloud Storage objects, including images. `ML.GENERATE_TEXT` with a Gemini remote model can analyze that multimodal object-table data for classification and return generated JSON, which can be written directly into a BigQuery table for integration with other datasets. `ML.UNDERSTAND_TEXT` is designed for text analysis, not image-content analysis.

**Learn more:** [The ML.GENERATE_TEXT function](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-generate-text) · [Introduction to object tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/object-table-introduction)

You are part of the data governance team and are implementing security requirements. You must encrypt all data in BigQuery by using an encryption key managed by your team. You must implement a mechanism that generates and stores encryption material only on your on-premises hardware security module (HSM). You want to use Google-managed solutions. What should you do?

options.text: Create the encryption key in the on-premises HSM, and import it into a Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS) key. Associate the created Cloud KMS key while creating the BigQuery resources.
Create the encryption key in the on-premises HSM and link it to a Cloud External Key Manager (Cloud EKM) key. Associate the created Cloud KMS key while creating the BigQuery resources.
Create the encryption key in the on-premises HSM, and import it into Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud HSM) key. Associate the created Cloud HSM key while creating the BigQuery resources.
Create the encryption key in the on-premises HSM. Create BigQuery resources and encrypt data while ingesting them into BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
Cloud External Key Manager (Cloud EKM) enables a Cloud KMS external key to use cryptographic key material managed in an external key-management system; the material remains outside Google Cloud and is never sent to Google. BigQuery supports customer-managed encryption keys using Cloud EKM, so an on-premises HSM key can be linked to a Cloud EKM key and used to protect BigQuery data.

**Learn more:** [Cloud External Key Manager](https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/ekm) · [Compatible services for Cloud KMS](https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/compatible-services)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization stores highly personal data in BigQuery and must comply with strict data-privacy regulations. Sensitive data values must become unreadable whenever an employee leaves the organization. What should you do?

options.text: Use column-level access controls with policy tags and revoke viewer permissions when employees leave the organization.
Use dynamic data masking and revoke viewer permissions when employees leave the organization.
Use customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) and delete keys when employees leave the organization.
Use AEAD functions and delete keys when employees leave the organization.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery AEAD functions support encryption of individual values and crypto-deletion: deleting the encryption key renders all values encrypted with that key unreadable because they can no longer be decrypted. This enables encryption keys to be scoped to the data associated with each employee.

**Learn more:** [AEAD encryption concepts](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/aead-encryption-concepts) · [AEAD encryption functions](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/aead_encryption_functions)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Several Spark jobs run on a Cloud Dataproc cluster according to a schedule. Some jobs execute sequentially, while others execute concurrently. You need to automate this process. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Cloud Dataproc Workflow Template
Create an initialization action to execute the jobs
Create a Directed Acyclic Graph in Cloud Composer
Create a Bash script that uses the Cloud SDK to create a cluster, execute jobs, and then tear down the cluster

questions.explanation:
Cloud Composer DAGs define scheduled workflows and task dependencies. Dependent Spark job tasks run in sequence, while tasks without dependencies can run concurrently; Composer can orchestrate Dataproc jobs as part of that workflow.

**Learn more:** [Write Airflow DAGs | Cloud Composer](https://cloud.google.com/composer/docs/composer-2/write-dags) · [Dataproc WorkflowTemplates API reference](https://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.workflowTemplates)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing your application's architecture to store data in Cloud Storage. The application includes pipelines that read raw data from one Cloud Storage bucket and write the processed data to a second bucket.  
  
You want Cloud Storage resources that remain resilient during a Google Cloud regional failure. You also want to minimize the recovery point objective (RPO) if a failure occurs, with no effect on applications that use the stored data. What should you do?

options.text: Adopt multi-regional Cloud Storage buckets in your architecture.
Adopt two regional Cloud Storage buckets, and update your application to write the output on both buckets.
Adopt a dual-region Cloud Storage bucket, and enable turbo replication in your architecture.
Adopt two regional Cloud Storage buckets, and create a daily task to copy from one bucket to the other.

questions.explanation:
A dual-region Cloud Storage bucket maintains copies across two regions and transparently serves replicated data from the available region during a regional outage, allowing applications to continue using the same bucket path. Enabling turbo replication reduces the cross-region replication RPO to 15 minutes, minimizing potential data-loss exposure compared with default replication.

**Learn more:** [Data availability and durability | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/availability-durability) · [Managing turbo replication | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/managing-turbo-replication)

Your company processes data for several different clients. Each client prefers its own set of analytics tools, and some permit direct query access through Google BigQuery. You must secure the data so clients cannot view one another's data, while ensuring suitable access to it.  
  
Which three actions should you take? (Choose three.)

options.text: Load data into different partitions.
Load data into a different dataset for each client.
Put each client's BigQuery dataset into a different table.
Restrict a client's dataset to approved users.
Only allow a service account to access the datasets.
Use the appropriate identity and access management (IAM) roles for each client's users.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery datasets are top-level containers used to organize tables and views and to control access. Keeping each client's data in a separate dataset creates a clear tenant boundary; granting that dataset only to the client's approved users prevents cross-client access; and assigning appropriate least-privilege IAM roles determines the actions those users may perform. [Create datasets](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/datasets) and [Control access to resources with IAM](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/control-access-to-resources-iam) document dataset-level access control and role assignment.

**Learn more:** [Create datasets | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/datasets) · [Control access to resources with IAM | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/control-access-to-resources-iam)

You work for an economic consulting firm that helps companies identify economic trends as they occur. As part of your analysis, you use Google BigQuery to correlate customer data with the average prices of the 100 most common goods sold, including bread, gasoline, milk, and others. The average prices for these goods are updated every 30 minutes. You need to ensure that this data remains current so you can combine it with other BigQuery data as cost-effectively as possible.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Load the data every 30 minutes into a new partitioned table in BigQuery.
Store and update the data in a regional Google Cloud Storage bucket and create a federated data source in BigQuery
Store the data in Google Cloud Datastore. Use Google Cloud Dataflow to query BigQuery and combine the data programmatically with the data stored in Cloud Datastore
Store the data in a file in a regional Google Cloud Storage bucket. Use Cloud Dataflow to query BigQuery and combine the data programmatically with the data stored in Google Cloud Storage.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Storage-backed BigQuery external table (federated data source) lets BigQuery query the current data in Cloud Storage directly and join it with native BigQuery tables, without repeatedly loading data into BigQuery or building a Dataflow pipeline. This best fits frequently refreshed, small external data that must remain current with minimal operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to loading data | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data) · [Query Cloud Storage data in external tables | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/query-cloud-storage-data?hl=en)

You are preparing data that your machine learning team will use to train a model with BigQueryML. They want to predict the price per square foot of real estate. The training data contains a price column and a column for the number of square feet. Another feature column, `feature1`, has null values because of missing data. You want to replace the nulls with zeros so that more data points are retained. Which query should you use?

options.text: ![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785600349695-jmk0nu7a.png)
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785600352324-zmz0ub9b.png)
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785600354969-yjfo6kuc.png)
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785600357398-7ns5cqc2.png)

questions.explanation:
The training data must include a `price_per_sqft` value calculated as `price / square_feet` and a non-null version of `feature1` that uses `IFNULL(feature1, 0)`. Excluding the original input columns before adding these derived columns prevents duplicate or uncleaned versions from remaining in the output. `WHERE feature1 IS NOT NULL` would discard records rather than retain them.

**Learn more:** [GoogleSQL query syntax: SELECT * EXCEPT](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax) · [GoogleSQL conditional expressions: IFNULL](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/conditional_expressions)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are creating a model to predict whether it will rain on a particular day. You have thousands of input features and want to determine whether removing some can improve training speed with minimal effect on model accuracy. What can you do?

options.text: Eliminate features that are highly correlated to the output labels.
Combine highly co-dependent features into one representative feature.
Instead of feeding in each feature individually, average their values in batches of 3.
Remove the features that have null values for more than 50% of the training records.

questions.explanation:
Highly co-dependent features often encode overlapping information. Combining such a group into one representative feature reduces input dimensionality and training cost while retaining most of the shared predictive signal. Features highly correlated with the output label are ordinarily valuable predictors, whereas arbitrary averaging or dropping features solely because of a missing-value threshold can discard useful information.

**Learn more:** [Google ML: Regularization for simplicity—strongly correlated features](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/MCE/mc-il-regularization-simplicity-2-features) · [Google ML: Understand the problem—predictive power](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/problem-framing/problem)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have terabytes of customer behavioral data streaming daily from Google Analytics into BigQuery. Your customers’ information, including their preferences, is hosted in a Cloud SQL for MySQL database. Your CRM database runs on a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance. The marketing team wants to use customer information from both databases and the customer behavioral data to create marketing campaigns for yearly active customers.  
  
You need to ensure that the marketing team can run the campaigns more than 100 times per day on typical days and up to 300 times during sales. At the same time, you want to minimize the load on the Cloud SQL databases. What should you do?

options.text: Create BigQuery connections to both Cloud SQL databases. Use BigQuery federated queries on the two databases and the Google Analytics data on BigQuery to run these queries.
Create a job on Apache Spark with Dataproc Serverless to query both Cloud SQL databases and the Google Analytics data on BigQuery for these queries.
Create streams in Datastream to replicate the required tables from both Cloud SQL databases to BigQuery for these queries.
Create a Dataproc cluster with Trino to establish connections to both Cloud SQL databases and BigQuery, to execute the queries.

questions.explanation:
Datastream continuously replicates the required Cloud SQL MySQL and PostgreSQL tables into BigQuery using change data capture, so campaign queries can join replicated customer and CRM data with Google Analytics data entirely in BigQuery. This supports frequent analytical queries without repeatedly querying the operational Cloud SQL databases.

**Learn more:** [Configure a BigQuery destination | Datastream | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/configure-bigquery-destination) · [Introduction to federated queries | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/federated-queries-intro)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An external table has been created for Apache Hive-partitioned data stored in a Cloud Storage bucket that contains many files. Queries against this table are slow. What should you do to improve query performance?

options.text: Change the storage class of the Hive partitioned data objects from Coldline to Standard.
Create an individual external table for each Hive partition by using a common table name prefix. Use wildcard table queries to reference the partitioned data.
Upgrade the external table to a BigLake table. Enable metadata caching for the table.
Migrate the Hive partitioned data objects to a multi-region Cloud Storage bucket.

questions.explanation:
BigLake metadata caching stores metadata for files in Cloud Storage, avoiding repeated metadata retrieval during queries. Queries that involve many files and Hive partition filters benefit particularly from this cache, so upgrading the Cloud Storage external table to BigLake and enabling metadata caching improves performance.

**Learn more:** [Use metadata caching for external data sources](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/metadata-caching-external-tables) · [Create Cloud Storage BigLake tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/create-cloud-storage-table-biglake)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your infrastructure contains a set of YouTube channels. You are tasked with establishing a process to send YouTube channel data to Google Cloud for analysis. You want a solution that lets worldwide marketing teams perform ANSI SQL and other analyses on current YouTube channel log data. How should you configure the log-data transfer into Google Cloud?

options.text: Use Storage Transfer Service to transfer the offsite backup files to a Cloud Storage Multi-Regional storage bucket as a final destination.
Use Storage Transfer Service to transfer the offsite backup files to a Cloud Storage Regional bucket as a final destination.
Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to transfer the offsite backup files to a Cloud Storage Multi-Regional storage bucket as a final destination.
Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to transfer the offsite backup files to a Cloud Storage Regional storage bucket as a final destination.

questions.explanation:
Storage Transfer Service is intended to transfer files from offsite storage systems into Cloud Storage. A multi-regional Cloud Storage bucket is appropriate when data must be broadly available to globally distributed teams. BigQuery Data Transfer Service transfers YouTube Channel connector data into a BigQuery dataset rather than to a Cloud Storage bucket.

**Learn more:** [Storage Transfer Service overview](https://cloud.google.com/storage-transfer/docs/overview) · [Load YouTube Channel data into BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/youtube-channel-transfer)

You administer shared BigQuery datasets that include views used by several teams in your organization. The marketing team is concerned about fluctuations in its monthly BigQuery analytics costs under the on-demand billing model. You need to help the marketing team set a consistent monthly BigQuery analytics spend. What should you do?

options.text: Create a BigQuery Enterprise reservation with a baseline of 250 slots and autoscaling set to 500 for the marketing team, and bill them back accordingly.
Establish a BigQuery quota for the marketing team, and limit the maximum number of bytes scanned each day.
Create a BigQuery reservation with a baseline of 500 slots with no autoscaling for the marketing team, and bill them back accordingly.
Create a BigQuery Standard pay-as-you go reservation with a baseline of 0 slots and autoscaling set to 500 for the marketing team, and bill them back accordingly.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery capacity-based pricing uses slot reservations rather than charging query processing by bytes scanned. A fixed 500-slot reservation with no autoscaling is billed for the provisioned capacity, producing a consistent monthly compute spend for the assigned marketing workload. Autoscaling capacity can add variable charges, while a bytes-scanned quota only caps usage rather than setting a fixed monthly charge.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to workload management](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reservations-intro) · [Estimate and control costs](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-costs)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Flowlogistic plans to use Google BigQuery as its primary analytics system, but it still has Apache Hadoop and Spark workloads that cannot be migrated to BigQuery. Flowlogistic is unsure how to store data common to both workloads. What should it do?

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810368916-vs0jaglm.png)

options.text: Store the common data in BigQuery as partitioned tables.
Store the common data in BigQuery and expose authorized views.
Store the common data encoded as Avro in Google Cloud Storage.
Store he common data in the HDFS storage for a Google Cloud Dataproc cluster.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Storage provides a shared, durable storage layer for Dataproc Hadoop/Spark workloads and BigQuery. Avro is a schema-based format supported by BigQuery for Cloud Storage data, making it suitable for data used by both systems.

**Learn more:** [Create Cloud Storage external tables](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/external-data-cloud-storage) · [Load Avro data from Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data-cloud-storage-avro)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a new application from which you must collect data in a scalable manner. Data is continuously received from the application during the day, and by the end of the year you expect to produce approximately 150 GB of JSON data each day. Your requirements are:  
  
- Decouple the producer from the consumer.  
- Store raw ingested data indefinitely in a space- and cost-efficient form.  
- Support near-real-time SQL queries.  
- Retain at least 2 years of historical data that will be queried using SQL.  
  
Which pipeline should you use to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create an application that provides an API. Write a tool to poll the API and write data to Cloud Storage as gzipped JSON files.
Create an application that writes to a Cloud SQL database to store the data. Set up periodic exports of the database to write to Cloud Storage and load into BigQuery.
Create an application that publishes events to Cloud Pub/Sub, and create Spark jobs on Cloud Dataproc to convert the JSON data to Avro format, stored on HDFS on Persistent Disk.
Create an application that publishes events to Cloud Pub/Sub, and create a Cloud Dataflow pipeline that transforms the JSON event payloads to Avro, writing the data to Cloud Storage and BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Pub/Sub decouples event publishers from consumers through asynchronous message delivery. A streaming Cloud Dataflow pipeline can transform incoming JSON events continuously, write compact Avro files to durable Cloud Storage for indefinite low-cost raw retention, and write records to BigQuery for near-real-time SQL queries and long-term SQL-accessible history. Google documents Dataflow streaming pipelines from Pub/Sub to BigQuery, and documents Avro as a binary format that can be compressed and loaded efficiently from Cloud Storage into BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Stream from Pub/Sub to BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/tutorials/dataflow-stream-to-bigquery) · [Read from Pub/Sub to Dataflow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/streaming-with-cloud-pubsub)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: You are building a model to forecast housing prices. Because of budget limitations, it must run on one resource-constrained virtual machine. Which learning algorithm should you choose?

options.text: Linear regression
Logistic classification
Recurrent neural network
Feedforward neural network

questions.explanation: Linear regression is designed to predict continuous numerical outcomes such as housing prices and has low computational and memory requirements, making it suitable for a resource-constrained virtual machine.

questions.question: You are building a model to forecast housing prices. Because of budget limitations, it must run on one resource-constrained virtual machine. Which learning algorithm should you choose?

options.text: Use a fixed-time window with a duration of 60 minutes.
Use a sliding time window with a duration of 60 minutes.
Use a session window with a gap time duration of 60 minutes.
Use a global window with a time based trigger with a delay of 60 minutes.

questions.explanation:
A session window with a 60-minute gap groups each user’s activity into a browsing session and ends that session after one hour without interaction. The resulting session can be evaluated for a basket value above $30 and the absence of a completed transaction. Google Cloud Dataflow documents session windows as grouping elements within a gap duration and specifically notes their suitability for activity streams with idle periods.

**Learn more:** [Streaming pipelines — Cloud Dataflow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/streaming-pipelines)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates a hybrid GCP deployment in which analytics are conducted on anonymized customer data. The data are imported into Cloud Storage from your data center by using parallel uploads to a data-transfer server running on GCP. Management says that the daily transfers take too long and asks you to resolve the issue. You want to maximize transfer speeds. Which action should you take?

options.text: Increase the CPU size on your server.
Increase the size of the Google Persistent Disk on your server.
Increase your network bandwidth from your datacenter to GCP.
Increase your network bandwidth from Compute Engine to Cloud Storage.

questions.explanation:
Parallel Cloud Storage uploads can be substantially faster only when network and disk speed are not limiting factors. Because the data originates in the on-premises data center and is already sent through parallel uploads to a GCP transfer server, the data center-to-GCP connection is the throughput constraint to expand. Increasing that network bandwidth raises the maximum ingress transfer rate.

**Learn more:** [Parallel composite uploads | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/parallel-composite-uploads)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Each analytics team in your organization runs BigQuery jobs in its own project. You want to allow every team to monitor slot usage within its project.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a Cloud Monitoring dashboard based on the BigQuery metric query/scanned_bytes
Create a Cloud Monitoring dashboard based on the BigQuery metric slots/allocated_for_project
Create a log export for each project, capture the BigQuery job execution logs, create a custom metric based on the totalSlotMs, and create a Cloud Monitoring dashboard based on the custom metric

Create an aggregated log export at the organization level, capture the BigQuery job execution logs, create a custom metric based on the totalSlotMs, and create a Cloud Monitoring dashboard based on the custom metric

questions.explanation:
The BigQuery Cloud Monitoring metric `slots/allocated_for_project` reports the number of slots currently allocated to query jobs in a project. A dashboard based on this built-in project metric lets each team monitor its own slot usage directly.

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud metrics: A or B](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/metrics_gcp_a_b) · [Create dashboards, charts, and alerts | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/monitoring-dashboard)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a fault-tolerant architecture for storing data in a regional BigQuery dataset. You must ensure that your application can recover from a table-corruption event that occurred during the last seven days. You want to use managed services with the lowest RPO and the most cost-effective solution. What should you do?

options.text: Access historical data by using time travel in BigQuery.
Export the data from BigQuery into a new table that excludes the corrupted data
Create a BigQuery table snapshot on a daily basis.
Migrate your data to multi-region BigQuery buckets.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery time travel provides access to a table’s prior versions for changed or deleted data within the dataset’s time-travel window, which is seven days by default. This supports point-in-time recovery with a lower RPO than a daily snapshot schedule and does not require maintaining separate backup exports or snapshots.

**Learn more:** [Data retention with time travel and fail-safe | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/time-travel) · [Access historical data | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-historical-data)

questions.question: You are training a spam classifier and observe that it is overfitting the training data. Which three actions can you take to address this problem? (Choose three.)

options.text: Get more training examples
Reduce the number of training examples
Use a smaller set of features
Use a larger set of features
Increase the regularization parameters
Decrease the regularization parameters

questions.explanation: Overfitting can be mitigated by adding more training examples, reducing the feature set to lower model complexity, and increasing regularization to penalize overly complex parameter values.

questions.question: You are training a spam classifier and observe that it is overfitting the training data. Which three actions can you take to address this problem? (Choose three.)

options.text: Storage Transfer Service for the migration; Pub/Sub and Cloud Data Fusion for the real-time updates
BigQuery Data Transfer Service for the migration; Pub/Sub and Dataproc for the real-time updates
gsutil for the migration; Pub/Sub and Dataflow for the real-time updates
gsutil for both the migration and the real-time updates

questions.explanation:
gsutil is suitable for transferring a small number of very large files to Cloud Storage; Cloud Storage supports parallel composite uploads to improve large-file upload performance. Pub/Sub can ingest transactional events, and Dataflow provides a streaming pipeline that reads from Pub/Sub and writes to BigQuery, enabling continuous real-time warehouse updates.

**Learn more:** [Parallel composite uploads | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/parallel-composite-uploads) · [Stream from Pub/Sub to BigQuery | Cloud Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/tutorials/dataflow-stream-to-bigquery)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your software uses a simple JSON format for every message. These messages are published to Google Cloud Pub/Sub, then processed by Google Cloud Dataflow to create a real-time dashboard for the CFO. During testing, you notice that some messages are absent from the dashboard. You check the logs, and all messages are being published to Cloud Pub/Sub successfully. What should you do next?

options.text: Check the dashboard application to see if it is not displaying correctly.
Run a fixed dataset through the Cloud Dataflow pipeline and analyze the output.
Use Google Stackdriver Monitoring on Cloud Pub/Sub to find the missing messages.
Switch Cloud Dataflow to pull messages from Cloud Pub/Sub instead of Cloud Pub/Sub pushing messages to Cloud Dataflow.

questions.explanation:
A fixed, known dataset isolates the Dataflow pipeline from the live Pub/Sub input and makes it possible to compare expected and actual output. This identifies whether message parsing, transformations, windowing, aggregation, or sink processing is dropping records. Dataflow pipelines read Pub/Sub data by repeatedly requesting it from Pub/Sub, so switching from push to pull is not the relevant corrective action.

**Learn more:** [Develop and test Dataflow pipelines](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/develop-and-test-pipelines) · [Troubleshoot Dataflow errors](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/common-errors)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are migrating your on-premises data warehouse to BigQuery. One upstream data source is hosted on a MySQL database running in your on-premises data center and has no public IP addresses. You want to ensure that data ingestion into BigQuery is secure and does not traverse the public internet. What should you do?

options.text: Update your existing on-premises ETL tool to write to BigQuery by using the BigQuery Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) driver. Set up the proxy parameter in the simba.googlebigqueryodbc.ini file to point to your data center’s NAT gateway.

Use Datastream to replicate data from your on-premises MySQL database to BigQuery. Set up Cloud Interconnect between your on-premises data center and Google Cloud. Use Private connectivity as the connectivity method and allocate an IP address range within your VPC network to the Datastream connectivity configuration. Use Server-only as the encryption type when setting up the connection profile in Datastream.

Use Datastream to replicate data from your on-premises MySQL database to BigQuery. Use Forward-SSH tunnel as the connectivity method to establish a secure tunnel between Datastream and your on-premises MySQL database through a tunnel server in your on-premises data center. Use None as the encryption type when setting up the connection profile in Datastream.

Use Datastream to replicate data from your on-premises MySQL database to BigQuery. Gather Datastream public IP addresses of the Google Cloud region that will be used to set up the stream. Add those IP addresses to the firewall allowlist of your on-premises data center. Use IP Allowlisting as the connectivity method and Server-only as the encryption type when setting up the connection profile in Datastream.

questions.explanation:
Datastream private connectivity supports securely reaching an external source database through a private network connection such as Cloud Interconnect. Allocating private address space in the VPC for the Datastream private connectivity configuration permits Datastream to reach the on-premises MySQL database without exposing it through public IP addresses. Server-only encryption authenticates the source server and helps prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.

**Learn more:** [Datastream network connectivity methods](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/network-connectivity-options) · [Create Datastream connection profiles](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/create-connection-profiles)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis

options.text: Create two separate authorized datasets; one for the data analytics team and another for the consumer support team.
Ensure that the data analytics team members do not have the Data Catalog Fine-Grained Reader role for the policy tags.
Replace the authorized dataset with an authorized view. Use row-level security and apply filter_expression to limit data access.
Remove the bigquery.dataViewer role from the data analytics team on the authorized datasets.
Enforce access control in the policy tag taxonomy.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery column-level access control permits access to a policy-tagged column when a principal has dataset access and the Data Catalog Fine-Grained Reader role for the relevant policy tag. Removing that role from the data analytics team prevents access to the protected columns. Policy-tag access control must also be enforced in the taxonomy so that the associated data policy is applied. [Restrict access with column-level access control](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/column-level-security)

**Learn more:** [Restrict access with column-level access control](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/column-level-security) · [Authorized datasets](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/authorized-datasets)

A globally distributed auction application lets users bid on items. At times, users submit identical bids at nearly the same time, and separate application servers process those bids. Each bid event includes the item, amount, user, and timestamp. You need to collect these bid events in one location in real time to determine which user placed the first bid. What should you do?

options.text: Create a file on a shared file and have the application servers write all bid events to that file. Process the file with Apache Hadoop to identify which user bid first.
Have each application server write the bid events to Cloud Pub/Sub as they occur. Push the events from Cloud Pub/Sub to a custom endpoint that writes the bid event information into Cloud SQL.

Set up a MySQL database for each application server to write bid events into. Periodically query each of those distributed MySQL databases and update a master MySQL database with bid event information.

Have each application server write the bid events to Google Cloud Pub/Sub as they occur. Use a pull subscription to pull the bid events using Google Cloud Dataflow. Give the bid for each item to the user in the bid event that is processed first.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Pub/Sub provides a real-time event-ingestion layer, and a pull subscription consumed by a single Dataflow streaming pipeline centralizes event processing. The pipeline can consistently process bid events for each item as they arrive and assign the bid to the user whose event is processed first. Dataflow’s Pub/Sub connector is designed for low-latency streaming reads and supports event timestamps and watermarking.

**Learn more:** [Read from Pub/Sub to Dataflow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/streaming-with-cloud-pubsub) · [Order messages](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/ordering)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building an Apache Beam pipeline that uses JdbcIO to extract data from a Cloud SQL instance. You have two projects running in Google Cloud. The pipeline will be deployed and run on Dataflow in Project A. The Cloud SQL instance runs in Project B and has no public IP address. After deploying the pipeline, you notice that it fails to extract data from the Cloud SQL instance because of a connection failure. You verify that VPC Service Controls and shared VPC are not used in these projects. You want to resolve this error while ensuring the data does not traverse the public internet. What should you do?

options.text: Set up VPC Network Peering between Project A and Project B. Add a firewall rule to allow the peered subnet range to access all instances on the network.
Turn off the external IP addresses on the Dataflow worker. Enable Cloud NAT in Project A.
Add the external IP addresses of the Dataflow worker as authorized networks in the Cloud SQL instance.

Set up VPC Network Peering between Project A and Project B. Create a Compute Engine instance without external IP address in Project B on the peered subnet to serve as a proxy server to the Cloud SQL database.

questions.explanation:
Cloud SQL private IP connectivity is implemented through private services access, which uses VPC Network Peering and is not transitive. Consequently, peering Project A with Project B alone does not allow Dataflow workers in Project A to reach the Cloud SQL private IP through Project B. A private proxy VM in Project B can communicate directly with Cloud SQL, and the workers can communicate privately with that VM over the direct A–B VPC peering connection.

**Learn more:** [Learn about using private IP — Cloud SQL for MySQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/private-ip?hl=en) · [Set up and manage VPC Network Peering](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/using-vpc-peering)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are preparing a dataset for use across the organization. You must preprocess customer data stored in a restricted Cloud Storage bucket. The data will support consumer analyses. You need to meet data-privacy requirements, including protecting certain sensitive data elements, while retaining all data for possible future use cases. What should you do?

options.text: Use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API and Dataflow to detect and remove sensitive fields from the data in Cloud Storage. Write the filtered data in BigQuery.
Use customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) to directly encrypt the data in Cloud Storage. Use federated queries from BigQuery. Share the encryption key by following the principle of least privilege.
Use Dataflow and the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API to mask sensitive data. Write the processed data in BigQuery.
Use Dataflow and Cloud KMS to encrypt sensitive fields and write the encrypted data in BigQuery. Share the encryption key by following the principle of least privilege.

questions.explanation:
Masking de-identifies sensitive values without dropping the associated fields, preserving the dataset for analysis and future use while reducing exposure of protected data. Dataflow can apply this transformation at scale to Cloud Storage input, and the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API provides sensitive-data detection and de-identification techniques such as masking before the processed data is written to BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Data Masking/Tokenization from Cloud Storage to BigQuery (using Cloud DLP)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/templates/provided/dlp-text-to-bigquery) · [De-identifying sensitive data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/deidentify-sensitive-data)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization manages a Google BigQuery dataset containing tables with user-level data. It wants to expose aggregates from that data to other Google Cloud projects while retaining control over access to the user-level data. It also needs to minimize overall storage costs and ensure that analysis costs for other projects are charged to those projects. What should it do?

options.text: Create and share an authorized view that provides the aggregate results.
Create and share a new dataset and view that provides the aggregate results.
Create and share a new dataset and table that contains the aggregate results.
Create dataViewer Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles on the dataset to enable sharing.

questions.explanation:
An authorized view exposes only the view-defined aggregate results while keeping the underlying user-level tables inaccessible to view users. Because it is a logical view rather than a copied aggregate table, it adds no duplicate table storage. Queries against the view are billed to the project that runs them, allowing consuming projects to bear their own analysis costs.

**Learn more:** [Authorized views | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/authorized-views)

You have a table containing millions of rows of sales data that is partitioned by date. Multiple applications and users query this data many times per minute. The query aggregates values using `AVG`, `MAX`, and `SUM` and does not need to join any other tables. The required aggregations are computed only across the past year of data, although you must retain the complete historical data in the base tables.  
  
You want query results to always include the most recent table data while reducing computation cost, maintenance overhead, and duration. What should you do?

options.text: Create a materialized view to aggregate the base table data. Include a filter clause to specify the last one year of partitions.
Create a materialized view to aggregate the base table data. Configure a partition expiration on the base table to retain only the last one year of partitions.
Create a view to aggregate the base table data. Include a filter clause to specify the last year of partitions.
Create a new table that aggregates the base table data. Include a filter clause to specify the last year of partitions. Set up a scheduled query to recreate the new table every hour.

questions.explanation:
A materialized view precomputes and maintains the supported aggregates, reducing repeated scan and aggregation work for frequent queries. Filtering its definition to the most recent year limits the materialized data while preserving all historical partitions in the base table. BigQuery materialized-view queries are consistent with base-table changes, combining cached materialized data with necessary base-table changes when needed.

**Learn more:** [Use materialized views | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/materialized-views-use) · [Create materialized views | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/materialized-views-create)

You have a Google Cloud Dataflow streaming pipeline that uses a Google Cloud Pub/Sub subscription as its source. You need to update the code in a way that makes the new Cloud Dataflow pipeline incompatible with the current version. You do not want to lose any data while making this update. What should you do?

options.text: Update the current pipeline and use the drain flag.
Update the current pipeline and provide the transform mapping JSON object.
Create a new pipeline that has the same Cloud Pub/Sub subscription and cancel the old pipeline.
Create a new pipeline that has a new Cloud Pub/Sub subscription and cancel the old pipeline.

questions.explanation:
For an incompatible streaming-pipeline change, drain the existing Dataflow job before replacement so it finishes processing in-flight data. A transform mapping is intended to help compatible replacement jobs transfer state, not to support genuinely incompatible changes. Cancelling immediately can lose in-flight data, while a different Pub/Sub subscription does not retain the current subscription’s pending messages and delivery state. Google Cloud recommends draining rather than cancelling when data loss must be avoided.

**Learn more:** [Upgrade a streaming pipeline](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/upgrade-guide) · [Update an existing pipeline](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/updating-a-pipeline)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are operating a streaming pipeline with Dataflow and using hopping windows to group data as it arrives. You noticed that some data arrives late but is not marked as late data, resulting in inaccurate downstream aggregations. You need to identify a solution that lets you capture late data in the appropriate window. What should you do?

options.text: Use watermarks to define the expected data arrival window. Allow late data as it arrives.
Change your windowing function to tumbling windows to avoid overlapping window periods.
Change your windowing function to session windows to define your windows based on certain activity.
Expand your hopping window so that the late data has more time to arrive within the grouping.

questions.explanation:
In Dataflow, a watermark indicates when all data for a window is expected to have arrived. Data that arrives with a timestamp in a window after that watermark passes is late data, and configuring allowed lateness enables the pipeline to accept and process it for that window. [Google Cloud Dataflow: Streaming pipelines](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/streaming-pipelines)

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud Dataflow: Streaming pipelines](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/streaming-pipelines)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is choosing a system to centralize data ingestion and delivery. You are evaluating messaging and data-integration systems to meet these key requirements:  
  
- The ability to seek to a specific offset in a topic, potentially back to the beginning of all data ever captured  
- Support for publish/subscribe semantics across hundreds of topics  
- Retain per-key ordering  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810991180-h65pj72y.png)  
  
Which system should you select?

options.text: Apache Kafka
Cloud Storage
Dataflow
Firebase Cloud Messaging

questions.explanation:
Apache Kafka provides durable topic logs with consumer offset control, including seeking to a specified offset or the earliest retained offset. It supports publish/subscribe across many topics, and records with the same key are routed to the same partition, where their order is retained. [Apache Kafka Consumer API](https://kafka.apache.org/42/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/consumer/KafkaConsumer.html)

**Learn more:** [Apache Kafka Consumer API](https://kafka.apache.org/42/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/consumer/KafkaConsumer.html)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An online retailer has built its current application on Google App Engine. A new company initiative requires extending the application so customers can transact directly through it. The retailer needs to manage shopping transactions and analyze combined data from multiple datasets with a business intelligence (BI) tool. They want to use only one database for this purpose. Which Google Cloud database should they select?

options.text: BigQuery
Cloud SQL
Cloud BigTable
Cloud Datastore

questions.explanation:
Cloud SQL is a fully managed relational database service that supports SQL-based online transaction processing for shopping activity and can be used by App Engine applications. Its relational model also supports combining datasets with SQL for analysis by BI tools. BigQuery is primarily optimized for online analytical processing rather than frequent single-row transactional operations.

**Learn more:** [Cloud SQL overview](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/introduction) · [Optimize query computation in BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-performance-compute)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a car manufacturer and have configured a data pipeline with Google Cloud Pub/Sub to capture anomalous sensor events. You use a Cloud Pub/Sub push subscription that invokes a custom HTTPS endpoint you created to act on these anomalous events as they occur. Your custom HTTPS endpoint continues to receive an excessive number of duplicate messages. What is the most likely reason for these duplicate messages?

options.text: The message body for the sensor event is too large.
Your custom endpoint has an out-of-date SSL certificate.
The Cloud Pub/Sub topic has too many messages published to it.
Your custom endpoint is not acknowledging messages within the acknowledgement deadline.

questions.explanation:
For a Pub/Sub push subscription, the HTTPS endpoint acknowledges delivery by returning a successful HTTP status code. If Pub/Sub does not receive that acknowledgment before the acknowledgment deadline expires, it redelivers the unacknowledged message, which causes duplicate deliveries.

**Learn more:** [Push subscriptions | Pub/Sub | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/push) · [Subscription properties | Pub/Sub | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscription-properties)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to build a near-real-time inventory dashboard that reads the primary inventory tables in your BigQuery data warehouse. Historical inventory data is stored as inventory balances by item and location. You receive several thousand inventory updates every hour. You want to maximize dashboard performance while ensuring the data is accurate. What should you do?

options.text: Leverage BigQuery UPDATE statements to update the inventory balances as they are changing.
Partition the inventory balance table by item to reduce the amount of data scanned with each inventory update.

Use the BigQuery streaming the stream changes into a daily inventory movement table. Calculate balances in a view that joins it to the historical inventory balance table. Update the inventory balance table nightly.

Use the BigQuery bulk loader to batch load inventory changes into a daily inventory movement table. Calculate balances in a view that joins it to the historical inventory balance table. Update the inventory balance table nightly.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery is optimized for analytical workloads and recommends avoiding frequent individual row updates; streaming is appropriate when frequent inserts must be available with minimal latency. Streaming inventory movements into an append-oriented daily table makes recent changes available to the dashboard promptly, while a view can combine those movements with the historical balance table to calculate accurate current balances. Consolidating the balance-table update nightly avoids continual mutations of the main inventory balance table.

**Learn more:** [Optimize query computation | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-performance-compute) · [Stream data using the Storage Write API | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/write-api-streaming)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are setting up networking for a Dataflow job. The data pipeline uses custom container images with the libraries needed for transformation logic already installed. The data pipeline reads data from Cloud Storage and writes it to BigQuery. You need to provide cost-effective, secure communication between the pipeline and Google APIs and services. What should you do?

options.text: Disable external IP addresses from worker VMs and enable Private Google Access.
Leave external IP addresses assigned to worker VMs while enforcing firewall rules.
Disable external IP addresses and establish a Private Service Connect endpoint IP address.
Enable Cloud NAT to provide outbound internet connectivity while enforcing firewall rules.

questions.explanation:
Dataflow workers that only require Google Cloud services such as Cloud Storage and BigQuery can run without external IP addresses when Private Google Access is enabled on their subnet. Preinstalled container dependencies eliminate the need for outbound internet access at runtime, while disabling external IPs reduces the public attack surface and avoids requiring Cloud NAT.

**Learn more:** [Configure internet access and firewall rules for Dataflow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/routes-firewall) · [Plan your Dataflow pipeline](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/plan-pipelines)

You must store and analyze social-media posts in Google BigQuery at a rate of 10,000 messages per minute, with near-real-time availability. The application is initially designed to use streaming inserts for individual posts. It also runs data aggregations immediately after the streaming inserts.  
  
You find that queries following streaming inserts do not provide strong consistency, so query reports can omit in-flight data. How should you change the application design?

options.text: Re-write the application to load accumulated data every 2 minutes.
Convert the streaming insert code to batch load for individual messages.
Load the original message to Google Cloud SQL, and export the table every hour to BigQuery via streaming inserts.
Estimate the average latency for data availability after streaming inserts, and always run queries after waiting twice as long.

questions.explanation:
Accumulating messages and loading them in two-minute batches creates completed load-job boundaries, so aggregation queries run against committed data rather than relying on data that may still be in a streaming buffer. This maintains near-real-time analysis while avoiding the consistency issue of immediate streaming-insert queries.

**Learn more:** [Use the legacy streaming API](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/streaming-data-into-bigquery)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a BigQuery data warehouse to analyze sales data for a telecommunications service provider. You need to create a data model for customers, products, and subscriptions. All customers, products, and subscriptions can be updated monthly, but you must retain a historical record of all data.  
  
You plan to use the visualization layer for current and historical reporting. You need to ensure the data model is simple, easy to use, and cost-effective. What should you do?

options.text: Create a normalized model with tables for each entity. Use snapshots before updates to track historical data.
Create a normalized model with tables for each entity. Keep all input files in a Cloud Storage bucket to track historical data.
Create a denormalized model with nested and repeated fields. Update the table and use snapshots to track historical data.
Create a denormalized, append-only model with nested and repeated fields. Use the ingestion timestamp to track historical data.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery recommends denormalizing hierarchical data with nested and repeated fields to reduce joins and improve query performance. An append-only design retains every monthly version without replacing prior data, while an ingestion timestamp provides a simple versioning attribute for selecting either the latest records or records from a historical point in time. This supports current and historical reporting without maintaining separate snapshot tables.

**Learn more:** [Use nested and repeated fields](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-performance-nested) · [Specify nested and repeated columns in table schemas](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/nested-repeated)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a model that provides clothing recommendations. Because a user's fashion preferences are likely to evolve over time, you create a data pipeline that streams new data back to the model as it becomes available. How should this data be used to train the model?

options.text: Continuously retrain the model on just the new data.
Continuously retrain the model on a combination of existing data and the new data.
Train on the existing data while using the new data as your test set.
Train on the new data while using the existing data as your test set.

questions.explanation:
Recommendation models whose inputs reflect changing consumer preferences need frequent retraining with up-to-date data. Combining historical training data with newly arrived data lets the model adapt to recent preferences while retaining useful established patterns; evaluation data should be held out from training.

**Learn more:** [ML pipelines | Google for Developers](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/managing-ml-projects/pipelines) · [Production ML systems: Static versus dynamic training | Google for Developers](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/production-ml-systems/static-vs-dynamic-training)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are modifying code for a subscriber to a Pub/Sub feed. You are worried that, during deployment, the subscriber could mistakenly acknowledge messages and cause message loss. The subscriber is not configured to retain acknowledged messages. What should you do to ensure you can recover from errors after deployment?

options.text: Set up the Pub/Sub emulator on your local machine. Validate the behavior of your new subscriber logic before deploying it to production.
Create a Pub/Sub snapshot before deploying new subscriber code. Use a Seek operation to re-deliver messages that became available after the snapshot was created.
Use Cloud Build for your deployment. If an error occurs after deployment, use a Seek operation to locate a timestamp logged by Cloud Build at the start of the deployment.
Enable dead-lettering on the Pub/Sub topic to capture messages that aren't successfully acknowledged. If an error occurs after deployment, re-deliver any messages captured by the dead-letter queue.

questions.explanation:
A Pub/Sub snapshot captures a subscription’s acknowledgment state. Seeking the subscription to that snapshot restores the captured state, so messages that were acknowledged after the snapshot can be redelivered. This supplies a recovery point even when acknowledged messages are not otherwise retained by the subscription.

**Learn more:** [Replay and purge messages with seek](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/replay-overview) · [Method: projects.subscriptions.seek](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.subscriptions/seek)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a data-transformation solution for BigQuery. Your developers are skilled in SQL and want to use the ELT development approach. Additionally, they require an intuitive coding environment and the ability to manage SQL as code. You need to identify a solution that lets your developers build these pipelines. What should you do?

options.text: Use Dataform to build, manage, and schedule SQL pipelines.
Use Dataflow jobs to read data from Pub/Sub, transform the data, and load the data to BigQuery.
Use Data Fusion to build and execute ETL pipelines.
Use Cloud Composer to load data and run SQL pipelines by using the BigQuery job operators.

questions.explanation:
Dataform is a BigQuery-native ELT service for developing, testing, version-controlling, and scheduling SQL transformation workflows. It provides a web development environment, stores SQL-based workflow code in repositories, integrates with Git, and executes the resulting SQL in BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Dataform overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataform/docs/overview) · [Overview of workflows](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataform/docs/sql-workflows)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work at a global shipping company and want to train a model on 40 TB of data to predict which ships in each geographic region are likely to cause delivery delays on a given day. The model will use multiple attributes gathered from multiple sources. Telemetry data, including location in GeoJSON format, will be retrieved from each ship and loaded hourly. You need a dashboard that shows the number and identity of ships likely to cause delays within a region. You want a storage solution with native prediction and geospatial-processing functionality. Which storage solution should you use?

options.text: BigQuery
Cloud Bigtable
Cloud Datastore
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL

questions.explanation:
BigQuery provides BigQuery ML for building and running prediction models directly on warehouse data, plus geospatial analytics through the `GEOGRAPHY` type and GoogleSQL geography functions. It can load GeoJSON as geographic data, enabling scalable regional analysis of hourly ship telemetry alongside the attributes used for delay predictions.

**Learn more:** [Working with geospatial data | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/geospatial-data) · [Supported input feature types | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/input-feature-types)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to build a data pipeline that copies time-series transaction data so your data science team can query it in BigQuery for analysis.  
  
Every hour, thousands of transactions receive a new status. The initial dataset is 1.5 PB and will increase by 3 TB per day. The data is highly structured, and your data science team will build machine learning models from it. You want to maximize performance and usability for the data science team. Which two strategies should you adopt? (Choose two.)

options.text: Denormalize the data as must as possible.
Preserve the structure of the data as much as possible.
Use BigQuery UPDATE to further reduce the size of the dataset.
Develop a data pipeline where status updates are appended to BigQuery instead of updated.
Copy a daily snapshot of transaction data to Cloud Storage and store it as an Avro file. Use BigQuery's support for external data sources to query.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery performs best with denormalized data, preferably using nested and repeated fields where appropriate, because this reduces joins and the associated data shuffling. For a very large time-series dataset with frequent status changes, appending time-stamped status-change records avoids continual bulk rewrites from `UPDATE` operations, retains the history needed for analysis and machine learning, and suits BigQuery’s analytical workload model.

**Learn more:** [Use nested and repeated fields](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-performance-nested?hl=en) · [Optimize query computation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-performance-compute?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to encrypt customer data kept in BigQuery. You must implement per-user crypto-deletion for data stored in your tables, while adopting native Google Cloud features to avoid custom solutions. What should you do?

options.text: Implement Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) BigQuery functions while storing your data in BigQuery.
Create a customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) in Cloud KMS. Associate the key to the table while creating the table.
Create a customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) in Cloud KMS. Use the key to encrypt data before storing in BigQuery.
Encrypt your data during ingestion by using a cryptographic library supported by your ETL pipeline.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery AEAD functions support encryption of individual values and can use a separate keyset for each customer. Deleting a customer’s key/keyset renders the data encrypted with it unreadable, which provides per-user crypto-deletion. A table-level CMEK does not provide this per-user granularity.

**Learn more:** [AEAD encryption concepts | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/aead-encryption-concepts?hl=en) · [Encryption at rest | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/encryption-at-rest)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to migrate an Apache Spark 3 batch job from on-premises to Google Cloud. You need to make minimal changes so the job reads from Cloud Storage and writes its results to BigQuery. The job is tuned for Spark with each executor using 8 vCPU and 16 GB of memory, and you want to select comparable settings. You also want to minimize the installation and management effort required to run the job. What should you do?

options.text: Execute the job as part of a deployment in a new Google Kubernetes Engine cluster.
Execute the job from a new Compute Engine VM.
Execute the job in a new Dataproc cluster.
Execute as a Dataproc Serverless job.

questions.explanation:
Dataproc Serverless runs Apache Spark batch workloads on Google-managed infrastructure, eliminating the need to provision and manage a Spark or Dataproc cluster. It supports Spark job submission and Spark property configuration, so the workload can retain comparable executor resource tuning while using Cloud Storage and BigQuery connectors.

**Learn more:** [Serverless for Apache Spark overview](https://cloud.google.com/dataproc-serverless/docs/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must configure BigQuery access for different departments in your company. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Each department can access only its own data.  
- Each department has one or more leads who must be able to create and update tables and make them available to their team.  
- Each department includes data analysts who must be able to query data but not modify it.  
  
How should access to the BigQuery data be configured?

options.text: Create a dataset for each department. Assign the department leads the role of OWNER, and assign the data analysts the role of WRITER on their dataset.
Create a dataset for each department. Assign the department leads the role of WRITER, and assign the data analysts the role of READER on their dataset.
Create a table for each department. Assign the department leads the role of Owner, and assign the data analysts the role of Editor on the project the table is in.
Create a table for each department. Assign the department leads the role of Editor, and assign the data analysts the role of Viewer on the project the table is in.

questions.explanation:
Separate datasets provide department-level data isolation. The BigQuery dataset-level WRITER role permits data modification for department leads, while the READER role permits analysts to read and query tables without modifying them. OWNER would grant unnecessary dataset-management privileges, and project-level roles or per-table organization do not provide the required least-privilege departmental boundary.

**Learn more:** [Basic roles and permissions | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control-basic-roles) · [Control access to resources with IAM | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/control-access-to-resources-iam)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],As the organization increases its use of GCP, many teams have begun creating their own projects. Projects are further proliferated to support different deployment stages and target audiences. Each project needs distinct access-control configurations, while the central IT team must be able to access every project.  
  
Additionally, data in Cloud Storage buckets and BigQuery datasets must be shared ad hoc for use by other projects. You want to simplify access-control management by minimizing the number of policies. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Cloud Deployment Manager to automate access provision.
Introduce resource hierarchy to leverage access control policy inheritance.
Create distinct groups for various teams, and specify groups in Cloud IAM policies.
Only use service accounts when sharing data for Cloud Storage buckets and BigQuery datasets.

For each Cloud Storage bucket or BigQuery dataset, decide which projects need access. Find all the active members who have access to these projects, and create a Cloud IAM policy to grant access to all these users.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud IAM allow policies applied at an organization or folder are inherited by descendant projects and resources, allowing central IT access to be managed with higher-level bindings. Granting roles to team groups rather than individual users centralizes membership management and avoids repeatedly updating IAM policies as team members change.

**Learn more:** [Using resource hierarchy for access control](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/resource-hierarchy-access-control) · [IAM overview](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is migrating its on-premises data-warehouse solutions to BigQuery. The current data warehouse uses trigger-based change data capture (CDC) to apply daily updates from multiple transactional database sources. With BigQuery, the company wants to improve its CDC handling so that source-system changes can be queried in BigQuery in near real time through log-based CDC streams, while also optimizing the performance of applying changes to the data warehouse.  
  
Which two steps should the company take to make changes available in the BigQuery reporting table with minimal latency while reducing compute overhead? (Choose two.)

options.text: Perform a DML INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE to replicate each individual CDC record in real time directly on the reporting table.
Insert each new CDC record and corresponding operation type to a staging table in real time.
Periodically DELETE outdated records from the reporting table.
Periodically use a DML MERGE to perform several DML INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations at the same time on the reporting table.
Insert each new CDC record and corresponding operation type in real time to the reporting table, and use a materialized view to expose only the newest version of each unique record.

questions.explanation:
Streaming each CDC record and its operation type to a staging table provides low-latency ingestion of the change stream. Periodically performing a set-based DML `MERGE` on the reporting table batches inserts, updates, and deletes, reducing the compute overhead of applying each change individually. Google Cloud’s Datastream-to-BigQuery guidance supports configuring merge frequency for replica tables and notes that a staging-and-replica view can expose the freshest data when merges are less frequent.

**Learn more:** [Use Datastream and Dataflow to stream data into BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/best-practices-stream-data)

options.text: Use Storage Transfer Service to move files into Cloud Storage.
Use Cloud Data Fusion to move files into Cloud Storage.
Use Dataflow to move files into Cloud Storage.
Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to move files into BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Data Fusion provides a graphical Pipeline Studio for building data pipelines and includes Cloud Storage sink plugins. It supports Cloud KMS customer-managed encryption keys for data written by its pipelines, including data written through supported Cloud Storage sinks.

**Learn more:** [Use customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) | Cloud Data Fusion](https://cloud.google.com/data-fusion/docs/how-to/customer-managed-encryption-keys) · [Introduction to Cloud Data Fusion: Console](https://cloud.google.com/data-fusion/docs/concepts/console-overview)

Your retail company is concerned about its BigQuery analytics spending. The company runs several queries that require the same aggregation of store ID and real-time sales volume. You need to implement the optimal solution to minimize analytics costs and return results faster. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new table from a CSV file with the repeated aggregation for the other queries to reference for faster processing.
Create a materialized view to minimize repetitive computations.
Use join acceleration with primary and foreign keys to increase query joining to live data.
Leverage partitioning to minimize the number of bytes read.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery materialized views precompute and store aggregate query results, reducing repetitive computation, data processing, and query latency for recurring aggregate workloads. They are automatically maintained as base-table data changes and can provide up-to-date results by using the materialized data together with necessary base-table changes.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to materialized views | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/materialized-views-intro) · [Use materialized views | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/materialized-views-use)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A shipping company has live package-tracking data sent to an Apache Kafka stream in real time. The data is then loaded into BigQuery. Analysts at your company want to query the tracking data in BigQuery to analyze geospatial trends throughout a package’s lifecycle. The table was originally created using ingest-date partitioning. Over time, query processing time has increased. You need to copy all data into a new clustered table. What should you do?

options.text: Re-create the table using data partitioning on the package delivery date.
Implement clustering in BigQuery on the package-tracking ID column.
Implement clustering in BigQuery on the ingest date column.
Tier older data onto Cloud Storage files and create a BigQuery table using Cloud Storage as an external data source.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery clustering sorts and colocates rows by the clustering column, allowing block pruning when queries filter or aggregate on that column. A package-tracking ID is a high-cardinality key that associates all events in an individual package lifecycle, so clustering by it improves targeted lifecycle queries. The existing ingest-date partitioning already limits data by ingestion date; clustering on that same date adds little selective benefit.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to clustered tables | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/clustered-tables) · [Create clustered tables | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/creating-clustered-tables)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You used Dataprep to create a recipe from a sample of data in a BigQuery table. You want to reuse this recipe for a daily data upload with the same schema, once the load job—whose execution time varies—has completed. What should you do?

options.text: Create a cron schedule in Dataprep.
Create an App Engine cron job to schedule the execution of the Dataprep job.
Export the recipe as a Dataprep template, and create a job in Cloud Scheduler.
Export the Dataprep job as a Dataflow template, and incorporate it into a Composer job.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Composer orchestrates dependency-aware data pipelines, so it can wait for the BigQuery load job to complete before starting the downstream Dataflow template. BigQuery jobs run asynchronously and can have variable completion times; a cron-based schedule alone cannot reliably enforce this completion dependency.

**Learn more:** [Manage BigQuery jobs](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-jobs) · [Choose Workflows or Cloud Composer for service orchestration](https://cloud.google.com/workflows/docs/choose-orchestration)
