lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company receives both batch- and stream-based event data. You want to process this data with Google Cloud Dataflow during a predictable time period.  
  
However, you realize that data can sometimes arrive late or out of order. How should you design your Cloud Dataflow pipeline to handle late or out-of-order data?

options.text: Set a single global window to capture all the data.
Set sliding windows to capture all the lagged data.
Use watermarks and timestamps to capture the lagged data.
Ensure every datasource type (stream or batch) has a timestamp, and use the timestamps to define the logic for lagged data.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Dataflow uses each event’s timestamp and a watermark to reason about event time when records arrive late or out of order. The watermark estimates when data for a time window should have arrived, so the pipeline can identify and handle late data according to its configured windowing and triggering behavior.

**Learn more:** [Streaming pipelines | Cloud Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/streaming-pipelines) · [Programming model for Apache Beam | Cloud Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/beam-programming-model)

MJTelco Case Study  
  
Company Overview  
  
MJTelco is a startup planning to build networks in rapidly expanding, underserved markets worldwide. The company holds patents for innovative optical-communications hardware. Using these patents, it can create many reliable, high-speed backbone links with inexpensive hardware.  
  
Company Background  
  
Founded by experienced telecom executives, MJTelco uses technologies originally developed to solve communications challenges in space. Central to its operations, it must build a distributed data infrastructure that enables real-time analysis and uses machine learning to continually optimize its topologies. Because its hardware is inexpensive, it plans to overdeploy the network, enabling it to account for the effects of dynamic regional politics on location availability and cost.  
  
Its management and operations teams are located around the globe, creating many-to-many relationships between data consumers and providers in the system. After careful evaluation, they chose public cloud as the ideal environment to support their needs.  
  
Solution Concept  
  
MJTelco is running a successful proof-of-concept (PoC) project in its labs. It has two primary needs:  
  
- Scale and harden the PoC to support substantially more data flows generated when it expands to more than 50,000 installations.  
- Refine its machine-learning cycles to validate and improve the dynamic models used to control topology definition.  
  
MJTelco will also use three distinct operating environments—development/test, staging, and production—to support experiments, deployment of new features, and production customers.  
  
Business Requirements  
  
- Scale the production environment at minimal cost, instantiating resources when and where required for an unpredictable, distributed telecom user community.  
- Ensure the security of proprietary data to protect its leading-edge machine learning and analysis.  
- Provide reliable, timely access to data for analysis by distributed research workers.  
- Maintain isolated environments that enable rapid iteration of machine-learning models without impacting customers.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783787334106-trg90c3u.png)  
  
Technical Requirements  
  
- Ensure secure, efficient transport and storage of telemetry data.  
- Rapidly scale instances to support between 10,000 and 100,000 data providers, each with multiple flows.  
- Enable analysis and presentation against data tables that track up to 2 years of data, storing approximately 100m records/day.  
- Support rapid iteration of monitoring infrastructure focused on awareness of data-pipeline problems in both telemetry flows and production learning cycles.  
  
CEO Statement  
  
Our business model depends on our patents, analytics, and dynamic machine learning. Our inexpensive hardware is organized for high reliability, giving us cost advantages. We must rapidly stabilize our large distributed data pipelines to meet our reliability and capacity commitments.  
  
CTO Statement  
  
Our public-cloud services must function as advertised. We need resources that scale and keep our data secure. We also need environments in which our data scientists can carefully examine and rapidly adapt our models. Because we depend on automation to process data, our development and test environments must also work as we iterate.  
  
CFO Statement  
  
The project is too large for us to maintain the required data and analysis hardware and software. We also cannot afford to staff an operations team to monitor so many data feeds, so we will depend on automation and infrastructure. Google Cloud's machine learning will enable our quantitative researchers to work on high-value problems rather than data-pipeline problems.  
  
You must create visualizations for operations teams that meet these requirements:  
  
- The report must include telemetry data from all 50,000 installations for the most recent 6 weeks, sampled once per minute.  
- The report must be no more than 3 hours behind live data.  
- The actionable report must display only suboptimal links.  
- Most suboptimal links must be sorted to the top.  
- Suboptimal links must be groupable and filterable by regional geography.  
- User response time to load the report must be <5 seconds.  
  
Which approach satisfies the requirements?

options.text: Load the data into Google Sheets, use formulas to calculate a metric, and use filters/sorting to show only suboptimal links in a table.
Load the data into Google BigQuery tables, write Google Apps Script that queries the data, calculates the metric, and shows only suboptimal rows in a table in Google Sheets.

Load the data into Google Cloud Datastore tables, write a Google App Engine Application that queries all rows, applies a function to derive the metric, and then renders results in a table using the Google charts and visualization API.

Load the data into Google BigQuery tables, write a Google Data Studio 360 report that connects to your data, calculates a metric, and then uses a filter expression to show only suboptimal rows in a table.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery is a fully managed, scalable analytics platform suited to multi-billion-row telemetry datasets and continuous ingestion. A Data Studio 360 report (now Looker Studio) can use BigQuery as its data source, define calculated metrics, filter to suboptimal links, sort by the derived metric, and apply geographic controls. This avoids querying all raw rows in an application or trying to use a spreadsheet as the analytical data store; BigQuery BI Engine can further accelerate Looker Studio report performance when needed.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery overview](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/introduction) · [BigQuery integrations | Looker Studio](https://cloud.google.com/looker/docs/studio/bigquery-integrations)

A Cloud Storage data lake stores raw, processed, and historical data in separate buckets. Data more than two years old is rarely accessed, and all data must be retained for no more than seven years. You are concerned about increasing storage costs. How should costs be controlled for the historical-data bucket?

options.text: Write a script on a Compute Engine instance, triggered daily by Cloud Scheduler, to scan all objects and delete any older than seven years.
Configure an Object Lifecycle Management rule to transition objects older than two years to the Archive storage class and eventually delete them after seven years.
Enable the Autoclass feature on your Cloud Storage buckets and select Opt-in to object transitions to Coldline and Archive storage classes.
Replicate the buckets to a different region with lower storage costs and configure an Object Lifecycle Management rule to delete objects after seven years.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management can automatically use an age condition to change objects to the Archive storage class and separately delete them once they reach the seven-year retention limit. Archive is intended for rarely accessed data, and lifecycle rules provide server-side, age-based storage-class transitions and deletion.

**Learn more:** [Object Lifecycle Management | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/lifecycle) · [Cloud Storage storage classes](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-classes)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a financial institution that allows customers to register online. As customers register, their user data is sent to Pub/Sub before it is ingested into BigQuery. For security reasons, you want to redact customers’ Government issued Identification Number while still allowing customer service representatives to view the original values when needed. What should you do?

options.text: Use BigQuery's built-in AEAD encryption to encrypt the SSN column. Save the keys to a new table that is only viewable by permissioned users.
Use BigQuery column-level security. Set the table permissions so that only members of the Customer Service user group can see the SSN column.
Before loading the data into BigQuery, use Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to replace input values with a cryptographic hash.
Before loading the data into BigQuery, use Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to replace input values with a cryptographic format-preserving encryption token.

questions.explanation:
Sensitive Data Protection format-preserving encryption de-identifies an identifier by replacing it with an encrypted token before BigQuery ingestion. It is reversible with the cryptographic key used for de-identification, allowing authorized personnel or services to re-identify original values when necessary. Cryptographic hashes cannot be re-identified.

**Learn more:** [Pseudonymization | Sensitive Data Protection | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/pseudonymization) · [De-identifying sensitive data | Sensitive Data Protection | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/deidentify-sensitive-data)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are creating an Apache Beam pipeline that enriches data from Cloud Pub/Sub using static reference data in BigQuery. The reference data is small enough to fit in a single worker’s memory. The pipeline must write enriched results to BigQuery for analysis. Which job type and transforms should this pipeline use?

options.text: Batch job, PubSubIO, side-inputs
Streaming job, PubSubIO, JdbcIO, side-outputs
Streaming job, PubSubIO, BigQueryIO, side-inputs
Streaming job, PubSubIO, BigQueryIO, side-outputs

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Pub/Sub source is unbounded, which requires a streaming pipeline. PubSubIO reads Pub/Sub messages, and BigQueryIO provides the BigQuery read and write integration. A small static reference dataset can be materialized as a side input and accessed while each streaming element is enriched. Side outputs are intended for separate output collections rather than reference-data lookups.

**Learn more:** [Apache Beam Programming Guide — Side inputs](https://beam.apache.org/documentation/programming-guide/) · [Apache Beam Google BigQuery I/O connector](https://beam.apache.org/documentation/io/built-in/google-bigquery/)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],BigQuery is used as the centralized analytics platform. New data is loaded daily, and an ETL pipeline modifies the source data and prepares it for end users. This ETL pipeline is changed regularly and may introduce errors, which are sometimes not detected until 2 weeks later. You need a way to recover from these errors while optimizing backup storage costs. How should data be organized in BigQuery and backups stored?

options.text: Organize your data in a single table, export, and compress and store the BigQuery data in Cloud Storage.
Organize your data in separate tables for each month, and export, compress, and store the data in Cloud Storage.
Organize your data in separate tables for each month, and duplicate your data on a separate dataset in BigQuery.
Organize your data in separate tables for each month, and use snapshot decorators to restore the table to a time prior to the corruption.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery time travel, including the functionality formerly called snapshot decorators, retains recoverable historical data for no more than seven days, so it cannot reliably recover corruption found after two weeks. Exporting monthly tables as compressed files to Cloud Storage provides durable, lower-cost archival backups without keeping a full duplicate in BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Data retention with time travel and fail-safe | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/time-travel) · [Estimate and control costs | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-costs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your car factory publishes machine measurements as messages to a Pub/Sub topic in your Google Cloud project. A Dataflow streaming job that you created with the Apache Beam SDK reads the messages, acknowledges them to Pub/Sub, applies custom business logic in a `DoFn` instance, and writes the results to BigQuery.  
  
You need to ensure that, when the business logic fails for a message, that message is sent to a Pub/Sub topic you can monitor for alerting. What should you do?

options.text: Enable retaining of acknowledged messages in your Pub/Sub pull subscription. Use Cloud Monitoring to monitor the subscription/num_retained_acked_messages metric on this subscription.

Use an exception handling block in your Dataflow’s DoFn code to push the messages that failed to be transformed through a side output and to a new Pub/Sub topic. Use Cloud Monitoring to monitor the topic/num_unacked_messages_by_region metric on this new topic.

Enable dead lettering in your Pub/Sub pull subscription, and specify a new Pub/Sub topic as the dead letter topic. Use Cloud Monitoring to monitor the subscription/dead_letter_message_count metric on your pull subscription.
Create a snapshot of your Pub/Sub pull subscription. Use Cloud Monitoring to monitor the snapshot/num_messages metric on this snapshot.

questions.explanation:
For Dataflow pipelines that read from Pub/Sub, Pub/Sub dead-letter topics do not reliably capture failures in downstream pipeline code because Dataflow can acknowledge a message after the first fused stage, before a later `DoFn` failure occurs. Failed transformations should be handled explicitly in the pipeline: catch the exception, emit the failed message through a side output, and write that output to a separate Pub/Sub topic for monitoring.

**Learn more:** [Read from Pub/Sub to Dataflow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/streaming-with-cloud-pubsub)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an application that shares financial market data with consumers, who will receive data feeds. Data is gathered from the markets in real time.  
  
Consumers will receive the data in these ways:  
  
- A real-time event stream  
- ANSI SQL access to the real-time stream and historical data  
- Batch historical exports  
  
Which solution should you use?

options.text: Cloud Dataflow, Cloud SQL, Cloud Spanner
Cloud Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, BigQuery
Cloud Dataproc, Cloud Dataflow, BigQuery
Cloud Pub/Sub, Cloud Dataproc, Cloud SQL

questions.explanation:
Cloud Pub/Sub provides the scalable real-time event stream. BigQuery supports SQL analytics over streaming and historical data, and Cloud Storage is suitable for batch file exports of historical data. Pub/Sub supports export subscriptions to BigQuery tables and Cloud Storage buckets, supporting this architecture.

**Learn more:** [Choose a subscription type | Pub/Sub](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscriber) · [Export statements in GoogleSQL | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/export-statements)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a linear regression model in BigQuery ML to predict a customer's likelihood of purchasing your company's products. The model uses a city-name variable as a key predictive component. To train and serve the model, your data must be arranged in columns. You want to prepare the data with the least amount of coding while retaining the predictive variables. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new view with BigQuery that does not include a column with city information.
Use SQL in BigQuery to transform the state column using a one-hot encoding method, and make each city a column with binary values.
Use TensorFlow to create a categorical variable with a vocabulary list. Create the vocabulary file and upload that as part of your model to BigQuery ML.
Use Cloud Data Fusion to assign each city to a region that is labeled as 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5, and then use that number to represent the city in the model.

questions.explanation:
City names are nominal categorical values, so they should be represented as binary indicator features rather than as arbitrary numeric region labels, which would imply a false ordering. One-hot encoding creates one binary feature per city and retains the predictive information for a linear regression model. BigQuery ML supports one-hot encoding for nonnumeric features, and BigQuery SQL can perform the transformation.

**Learn more:** [Automatic feature preprocessing | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/auto-preprocessing) · [ML.ONE_HOT_ENCODER function | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-one-hot-encoder)

You work for a shipping company with distribution centers where packages travel along delivery lines for proper routing. The company wants to install cameras on the delivery lines to detect and track any visible damage to packages while they are in transit. You need to create a way to automatically detect damaged packages and flag them for human review in real time as the packages move through transit. Which solution should you choose?

options.text: Use BigQuery machine learning to be able to train the model at scale, so you can analyze the packages in batches.
Train an AutoML model on your corpus of images, and build an API around that model to integrate with the package tracking applications.
Use the Cloud Vision API to detect for damage, and raise an alert through Cloud Functions. Integrate the package tracking applications with this function.
Use TensorFlow to create a model that is trained on your corpus of images. Create a Python notebook in Cloud Datalab that uses this model so you can analyze for damaged packages.

questions.explanation:
A custom AutoML vision model trained on labeled images of the company’s packages can learn the organization-specific visual patterns of damage. Serving that model through an API enables synchronous, real-time predictions that package-tracking applications can use to flag items for human review. Vertex AI supports training AutoML image-classification models and obtaining online predictions from deployed endpoints.

**Learn more:** [Train an image classification model | Vertex AI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/image-data/classification/train-model) · [Get online inferences from a custom trained model | Vertex AI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/get-online-predictions)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate a large on-premises data warehouse to BigQuery. The data is presently stored in a proprietary, vendor-specific format. A batch migration of this data to BigQuery is required. What should be done?

options.text: Use the bq command-line tool to load the data directly from the on-premises data warehouse.
Export the data to CSV files, upload the files to Cloud Storage, then load the files into BigQuery.
Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service.
Use Datastream to replicate the data in real time.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery batch load jobs support files in Cloud Storage, including CSV. Data in a proprietary warehouse format must first be exported to a supported format, then staged in Cloud Storage and loaded into BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Loading CSV data from Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data-cloud-storage-csv) · [Introduction to loading data](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Flowlogistic’s CEO wants rapid insight into the customer base so that the sales team can be better informed in the field. The team is not highly technical, so it purchased a visualization tool to simplify creating BigQuery reports. However, the team is overwhelmed by the data in the table and is spending substantial money on queries while trying to locate the needed data. What should you do to solve this problem most cost-effectively?

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783787332071-3udiwzv1.png)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783787336743-khwpbry2.png)

options.text: Export the data into a Google Sheet for virtualization.
Create an additional table with only the necessary columns.
Create a view on the table to present to the virtualization tool.
Create identity and access management (IAM) roles on the appropriate columns, so only they appear in a query.

questions.explanation:
A BigQuery view can present only the columns required by the visualization tool while avoiding a duplicate physical table. Because BigQuery query costs depend on the data processed in selected columns, limiting the view’s projection reduces unnecessary data scans and makes reporting simpler for nontechnical users.

**Learn more:** [Optimize query computation | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-performance-compute?hl=en) · [Introduction to logical views | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/views-intro)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company keeps critical operational sales data in a BigQuery dataset in `us-central1`. The company needs a disaster-recovery plan that can restore this data to `us-east1` with a recovery point objective (RPO) of 24 hours and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 4 hours if `us-central1` has an outage. You need to implement this disaster-recovery plan while minimizing cost and complexity. What should you do?

options.text: Set up continuous queries and Pub/Sub to stream data changes from BigQuery tables in us-central1 to us-east1.
Manually export data to a CSV file in a multi-regional Cloud Storage bucket daily and use bq load to restore to us-east1.
Configure BigQuery cross-region dataset replication from ns-central1 to us-east1.
Take daily BigQuery table snapshots in us-central1.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery cross-region dataset replication automatically creates and asynchronously maintains a secondary replica in another region. The secondary replica can be promoted to become writable after an outage, providing a low-operational-overhead recovery approach that readily meets a 24-hour RPO and 4-hour RTO.

**Learn more:** [Cross-region dataset replication | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/data-replication)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates a large on-premises cluster running Spark, Hive, and HDFS in a colocation facility. The cluster is sized for peak system use; however, many jobs are batch-oriented, and cluster utilization fluctuates substantially.  
  
The company wants to move to the cloud to reduce the overhead of on-premises infrastructure and maintenance and to gain cost savings. It also wants to modernize its current infrastructure with more serverless offerings to benefit from the cloud. Because the colocation-facility contract is due for renewal, the company has only 2 months for its initial migration.  
  
How should you recommend approaching the upcoming migration strategy to maximize cloud cost savings while still completing the migration on time?

options.text: Migrate the workloads to Dataproc plus HDFS; modernize later.
Migrate the workloads to Dataproc plus Cloud Storage; modernize later.
Migrate the Spark workload to Dataproc plus HDFS, and modernize the Hive workload for BigQuery.
Modernize the Spark workload for Dataflow and the Hive workload for BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
Dataproc provides managed support for Apache Spark, Hive, and Hadoop workloads, enabling a fast initial migration with minimal application change. Cloud Storage is HDFS-compatible through Dataproc’s installed connector and persists independently after clusters are shut down, unlike cluster HDFS. This separation lets batch compute be transient or right-sized for fluctuating demand while retaining durable data, reducing always-on cluster cost and infrastructure management. The serverless redesign of individual workloads can be deferred until after the time-constrained migration.

**Learn more:** [Dataproc FAQ](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/resources/faq) · [Migrating Apache Hadoop to Dataproc: A decision tree](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/migrating-apache-hadoop-dataproc-decision-tree)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work at a large real estate company and are preparing 6 TB of home-sales data for machine learning. You will use SQL to transform the data and BigQuery ML to build a machine learning model. You intend to use the model for predictions on a raw dataset that has not been transformed. How should you configure your workflow to prevent skew at prediction time?

options.text: When creating your model, use BigQuery's TRANSFORM clause to define preprocessing steps. At prediction time, use BigQuery's ML.EVALUATE clause without specifying any transformations on the raw input data.
When creating your model, use BigQuery's TRANSFORM clause to define preprocessing steps. Before requesting predictions, use a saved query to transform your raw input data, and then use ML.EVALUATE.

Use a BigQuery view to define your preprocessing logic. When creating your model, use the view as your model training data. At prediction time, use BigQuery's ML.EVALUATE clause without specifying any transformations on the raw input data.
Preprocess all data using Dataflow. At prediction time, use BigQuery's ML.EVALUATE clause without specifying any further transformations on the input data.

questions.explanation:
A BigQuery ML model created with a `TRANSFORM` clause retains its preprocessing logic. BigQuery ML automatically applies those transformations, including training-derived transformation statistics, to the raw feature columns supplied during prediction or evaluation. This ensures training and serving use identical feature processing and prevents training-serving skew.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery ML CREATE MODEL statement](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create) · [Perform feature engineering with the TRANSFORM clause](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/bigqueryml-transform)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a healthcare organization in which data is organized and managed by its respective data owners across various storage services. Because of this decentralized ecosystem, data discovery and management have become challenging. You need to rapidly identify and implement a cost-optimized solution to help your organization with the following:  
  
- Data management and discovery  
- Data lineage tracking  
- Data quality validation  
  
How should you build this solution?

options.text: Use BigLake to convert the current solution into a data lake architecture.
Build a new data discovery tool on Google Kubernetes Engine that helps with new source onboarding and data lineage tracking.
Use BigQuery to track data lineage, and use Dataprep to manage data and perform data quality validation.
Use Dataplex to manage data, track data lineage, and perform data quality validation.

questions.explanation:
Dataplex provides a centralized data-governance and discovery layer for distributed data assets. Its catalog capabilities support finding and managing metadata, its lineage integration supports tracking data movement and transformations, and its data-quality capabilities support automated validation such as completeness, validity, consistency, and custom rules.

**Learn more:** [Use auto data quality](https://cloud.google.com/dataplex/docs/use-auto-data-quality) · [About data lineage](https://cloud.google.com/dataplex/docs/about-data-lineage)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization stores data assets in BigQuery, Pub/Sub, and a PostgreSQL instance that runs on Compute Engine. Because multiple domains and varied teams use the data, teams across the organization cannot discover existing data assets.  
  
You need to design a solution that improves data discoverability while minimizing development and configuration effort. What should you do?

options.text: Use Data Catalog to automatically catalog BigQuery datasets. Use Data Catalog APIs to manually catalog Pub/Sub topics and PostgreSQL tables.
Use Data Catalog to automatically catalog BigQuery datasets and Pub/Sub topics. Use Data Catalog APIs to manually catalog PostgreSQL tables.
Use Data Catalog to automatically catalog BigQuery datasets and Pub/Sub topics. Use custom connectors to manually catalog PostgreSQL tables.
Use customer connectors to manually catalog BigQuery datasets, Pub/Sub topics, and PostgreSQL tables.

questions.explanation:
Data Catalog automatically catalogs metadata for BigQuery resources and Pub/Sub topics. PostgreSQL is an external RDBMS source for Data Catalog, so using the available PostgreSQL connector to ingest its table metadata provides discoverability with less custom development than manually creating entries through the Data Catalog APIs.

**Learn more:** [Data Catalog entry groups reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-catalog/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.entryGroups/create) · [Integrate data sources with Data Catalog](https://cloud.google.com/data-catalog/docs/integrate-data-sources?hl=pt-br)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your analytics team wants to create a simple statistical model to identify which customers are most likely to work with your company again, based on several metrics. They plan to run the model on Apache Spark using data stored in Google Cloud Storage, and you have recommended Google Cloud Dataproc to execute the job.  
  
Testing shows that this workload can complete in approximately 30 minutes on a 15-node cluster, with results written to Google BigQuery. The workload is planned to run weekly. How should you optimize the cluster for cost?

options.text: Migrate the workload to Google Cloud Dataflow
Use pre-emptible virtual machines (VMs) for the cluster
Use a higher-memory node so that the job runs faster
Use SSDs on the worker nodes so that the job can run faster

questions.explanation:
Preemptible VMs provide significantly discounted compute capacity and suit short, fault-tolerant batch workloads such as a weekly 30-minute Spark job. A preemptible VM can be terminated and has a 24-hour maximum runtime, neither of which prevents using it for this brief, restartable processing workload.

**Learn more:** [Preemptible VM instances](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/preemptible) · [Dataproc best practices](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/dataproc-best-practices-guide)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a stateful data-processing pipeline that reads data from a Cloud Storage bucket and writes transformed data to a BigQuery table. The pipeline must be highly available and resilient to zonal failures in the `us-central1` region. You need to configure a Dataflow pipeline with minimal disruption during a zonal outage. What should you do?

options.text: Launch the Dataflow job with the --region=us-central1 parameter.
Deploy the Dataflow job to a single zone within us-central1 and configure it to use a regional persistent disk to store its state.
Deploy the Dataflow job to a single zone within us-central1 and use a multi-regional Cloud Storage bucket to store its state.
Launch the Dataflow job with the --zone=us-central1a parameter.

questions.explanation:
Configuring the job with `--region=us-central1` allows Dataflow to manage worker placement across the available zones in that region. Regional placement improves resilience to zonal failures because workers can be recreated in another available zone; pinning a job to one zone does not provide that protection.

**Learn more:** [Dataflow regions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/regional-endpoints) · [Design Dataflow pipeline workflows](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/pipeline-workflows)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates in a highly regulated industry. A requirement is to ensure that individual users can access only the minimum information needed to perform their jobs. You want to enforce this requirement by using Google BigQuery. Which three approaches can you use? (Choose three.)

options.text: Disable writes to certain tables.
Restrict access to tables by role.
Ensure that the data is encrypted at all times.
Restrict BigQuery API access to approved users.
Segregate data across multiple tables or databases.
Use Google Stackdriver Audit Logging to determine policy violations.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery supports least-privilege access through IAM roles granted at granular scopes, including individual tables and datasets. Access can be limited to approved users or principals for BigQuery API operations, and sensitive data can be separated into different tables or datasets so that distinct IAM policies can be applied. Encryption, write restrictions, and audit logging do not independently limit users to only the data they need.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to security and access controls in BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control-intro) · [Control access to resources with IAM](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/control-access-to-resources-iam)

questions.question: You need to create a new Cloud Spanner transaction table to store product-sales data. You are deciding which primary key to use. From a performance standpoint, which strategy should you select?

options.text: The current epoch time
A concatenation of the product name and the current epoch time
A random universally unique identifier number (version 4 UUID)
The original order identification number from the sales system, which is a monotonically increasing integer

questions.explanation:
Cloud Spanner range-shards data by primary key, so monotonically increasing timestamps and integer order IDs direct new writes to the same key range and can create a write hotspot. A version 4 UUID uses random values that distribute rows across the key space, avoiding that hotspot pattern.\
\
**Learn more:** [Schema design best practices | Spanner | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/schema-design?hl=en)

Run the Dataproc cluster in a zone in the us-central1 region, reading from the bucket in the us-south1 region.4. 1. Create a dual-region Cloud Storage bucket in the us-central1 and us-south1 regions.2. Enable turbo replication.3. Run the Dataproc cluster in a zone in the us-central1 region, reading from the bucket in the same region.4. In case of a regional failure, redeploy the Dataproc clusters to the us-south1 region and read from the same bucket.

questions.explanation:
A dual-region Cloud Storage bucket with turbo replication replicates objects between its two regions within a 15-minute RPO. When a workload accesses a dual-region bucket from one of its constituent regions, Cloud Storage routes the request to that same region for optimal performance. Keeping Dataproc in `us-central1` during normal operation and redeploying it to `us-south1` after a regional failure preserves local-region reads while using the same replicated bucket.

**Learn more:** [Bucket locations | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-locations) · [Data availability and durability | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/availability-durability)

The marketing team at your organization regularly supplies updates for a segment of your customer dataset. The team has provided a CSV containing 1 million records that must be updated in BigQuery. When you run an `UPDATE` statement in BigQuery, you receive a `quotaExceeded` error. What should you do?

options.text: Reduce the number of records updated each day to stay within the BigQuery UPDATE DML statement limit.
Increase the BigQuery UPDATE DML statement limit in the Quota management section of the Google Cloud Platform Console.
Split the source CSV file into smaller CSV files in Cloud Storage to reduce the number of BigQuery UPDATE DML statements per BigQuery job.
Import the new records from the CSV file into a new BigQuery table. Create a BigQuery job that merges the new records with the existing records and writes the results to a new BigQuery table.

questions.explanation:
For a large batch refresh, load the CSV data into a staging table and use a query to combine the incoming rows with the existing data into a new table. This set-based replacement pattern avoids depending on mutating `UPDATE` DML capacity for a million-record update; BigQuery applies dedicated concurrency and rate limits to mutating DML statements such as `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, and `MERGE`.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery quotas and limits](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/quotas) · [Transform data with data manipulation language (DML)](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/data-manipulation-language)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses a proprietary system to transmit inventory data every 6 hours to a cloud-based data-ingestion service. The transmitted data contains a payload with several fields and the transmission timestamp. When there are concerns about a transmission, the system retransmits the data.  
  
How should the data be deduplicated most efficiently?

options.text: Assign global unique identifiers (GUID) to each data entry.
Compute the hash value of each data entry, and compare it with all historical data.
Store each data entry as the primary key in a separate database and apply an index.
Maintain a database table to store the hash value and other metadata for each data entry.

questions.explanation:
Use a deterministic hash of the relevant data entry as an idempotency key and persist it with processing metadata. Each retransmission can then be checked with a direct lookup instead of scanning historical entries, while the metadata supports processing status and retention decisions. AWS guidance describes idempotency keys as hashes of an event or selected fields that are stored in a persistence layer for duplicate detection.

**Learn more:** [Idempotency - Powertools for AWS Lambda (Python)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/powertools/python/2.39.1/utilities/idempotency/)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your startup has a web application that currently serves customers from a single region in Asia. You are seeking funding that will enable the startup to serve customers globally. Your current objective is to optimize for cost, while your post-funding objective is to optimize for global presence and performance. You must use a native JDBC driver. What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Spanner to configure a single region instance initially, and then configure multi-region Cloud Spanner instances after securing funding.
Use a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL highly available instance first, and Bigtable with US, Europe, and Asia replication after securing funding.
Use a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL zonal instance first, and Bigtable with US, Europe, and Asia after securing funding.
Use a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL zonal instance first, and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with highly available configuration after securing funding.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Spanner supports JDBC and can begin with a regional configuration, whose resources remain in one region and which has a lower cost profile than multi-region configurations. The instance can subsequently be moved to a multi-region configuration without downtime. Multi-region Spanner distributes data across multiple regions, improving global availability and enabling lower-latency reads from multiple geographic locations.

**Learn more:** [Regional, dual-region, and multi-region configurations | Spanner](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/instance-configurations) · [Getting started with Spanner in JDBC](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/getting-started/jdbc)

questions.question: You are designing a Dataflow pipeline for a batch-processing job. You want to mitigate multiple zonal failures when submitting the job. What should you do?

options.text: Submit duplicate pipelines in two different zones by using the --zone flag.
Set the pipeline staging location as a regional Cloud Storage bucket.
Specify a worker region by using the --region flag.
Create an Eventarc trigger to resubmit the job in case of zonal failure when submitting the job.

questions.explanation:
Specifying a worker region with `--region` lets Dataflow choose the best available zone within that region, providing additional fault tolerance for zonal resource failures at job submission. Explicitly selecting a zone removes that placement flexibility.\
\
**Learn more:** [Design Dataflow pipeline workflows](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/pipeline-workflows)

questions.question: You are designing a Dataflow pipeline for a batch-processing job. You want to mitigate multiple zonal failures when submitting the job. What should you do?

options.text: Configure your Dataflow pipeline to use local execution
Increase the maximum number of Dataflow workers by setting maxNumWorkers in PipelineOptions
Increase the number of nodes in the Bigtable cluster
Modify your Dataflow pipeline to use the Flatten transform before writing to Bigtable
Modify your Dataflow pipeline to use the CoGroupByKey transform before writing to Bigtable

questions.explanation:
Increasing the Dataflow job’s `maxNumWorkers` allows the job to scale out with more worker instances, raising pipeline processing and write parallelism. Increasing the number of Bigtable cluster nodes raises the cluster’s scalable read and write capacity, which reduces write pressure and supports more concurrent dashboard requests.

**Learn more:** [Pipeline options | Cloud Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/pipeline-options) · [Understand performance | Bigtable](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/performance)

You are preparing to migrate an existing on-premises Apache Hadoop deployment to the cloud. You must make the deployment as fault-tolerant and cost-effective as possible for long-running batch jobs, using a managed service. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy a Dataproc cluster. Use a standard persistent disk and 50% preemptible workers. Store data in Cloud Storage, and change references in scripts from hdfs:// to gs://
Deploy a Dataproc cluster. Use an SSD persistent disk and 50% preemptible workers. Store data in Cloud Storage, and change references in scripts from hdfs:// to gs://

Install Hadoop and Spark on a 10-node Compute Engine instance group with standard instances. Install the Cloud Storage connector, and store the data in Cloud Storage. Change references in scripts from hdfs:// to gs://
Install Hadoop and Spark on a 10-node Compute Engine instance group with preemptible instances. Store data in HDFS. Change references in scripts from hdfs:// to gs://

questions.explanation:
Dataproc is a managed Hadoop and Spark service. Keeping persistent data in Cloud Storage and using `gs://` makes the data durable independently of cluster workers, while fault-tolerant batch workloads can reduce compute cost with preemptible workers. Standard Persistent Disk is appropriate for large data-processing workloads dominated by sequential I/O; SSD Persistent Disk is warranted when lower latency and higher IOPS are required, which is not a stated need.

**Learn more:** [Dataproc FAQ](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/resources/faq) · [Preemptible VM instances](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/preemptible?hl=en)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Business users need a way to clean and prepare data before they use it for analysis. These users are less technically savvy and prefer graphical user interfaces for defining transformations. After the data is transformed, they want to perform their analysis directly in a spreadsheet. You need to recommend a solution they can use. What should you do?

options.text: Use Dataprep to clean the data, and write the results to BigQuery. Analyze the data by using Connected Sheets.
Use Dataprep to clean the data, and write the results to BigQuery. Analyze the data by using Looker Studio.
Use Dataflow to clean the data, and write the results to BigQuery. Analyze the data by using Connected Sheets.
Use Dataflow to clean the data, and write the results to BigQuery. Analyze the data by using Looker Studio.

questions.explanation:
Dataprep provides a graphical, no-code interface for visually exploring, cleaning, and preparing data, and it can write cleaned data to BigQuery. Connected Sheets brings BigQuery data into the familiar Google Sheets interface for spreadsheet-based analysis, including formulas, pivot tables, and charts.

**Learn more:** [Using Connected Sheets](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/connected-sheets?hl=en) · [Introducing BigQuery pushdown for Dataprep](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/introducing-dataprep-bigquery-pushdown)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The data analyst team at your company uses BigQuery for ad-hoc queries and scheduled SQL pipelines in a Google Cloud project that has a slot reservation of 2000 slots. However, following the recent addition of hundreds of new non-time-sensitive SQL pipelines, the team is experiencing frequent quota errors. You review the logs and find that approximately 1500 queries are triggered concurrently during peak time. You need to resolve the concurrency issue. What should you do?

options.text: Increase the slot capacity of the project with baseline as 0 and maximum reservation size as 3000.
Update SQL pipelines to run as a batch query, and run ad-hoc queries as interactive query jobs.
Increase the slot capacity of the project with baseline as 2000 and maximum reservation size as 3000.
Update SQL pipelines and ad-hoc queries to run as interactive query jobs.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery gives batch queries lower priority than interactive queries and is more likely to queue them when reservation capacity is fully used. A project assigned to a reservation can queue up to 1,000 interactive queries but up to 20,000 batch queries; therefore, assigning non-time-sensitive pipelines to batch priority avoids the interactive-query queue limit while retaining interactive priority for ad-hoc work.

**Learn more:** [Use query queues | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/query-queues) · [Overview of BigQuery analytics | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/query-overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to archive data in Cloud Storage. Since some of the data is highly sensitive, you want to apply the `Trust No One` (TNO) approach to encrypt it so that cloud-provider staff cannot decrypt it. What should you do?

options.text: Use gcloud kms keys create to create a symmetric key. Then use gcloud kms encrypt to encrypt each archival file with the key and unique additional authenticated data (AAD). Use gsutil cp to upload each encrypted file to the Cloud Storage bucket, and keep the AAD outside of Google Cloud.

Use gcloud kms keys create to create a symmetric key. Then use gcloud kms encrypt to encrypt each archival file with the key. Use gsutil cp to upload each encrypted file to the Cloud Storage bucket. Manually destroy the key previously used for encryption, and rotate the key once.

Specify customer-supplied encryption key (CSEK) in the .boto configuration file. Use gsutil cp to upload each archival file to the Cloud Storage bucket. Save the CSEK in Cloud Memorystore as permanent storage of the secret.

Specify customer-supplied encryption key (CSEK) in the .boto configuration file. Use gsutil cp to upload each archival file to the Cloud Storage bucket. Save the CSEK in a different project that only the security team can access.

questions.explanation:
Customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK) add an encryption layer for Cloud Storage objects while Cloud Storage does not permanently store or manage the supplied key; it is provided for each applicable operation. The CSEK must be kept securely and separately from the archived data. Restricting it to a separate project accessible only by the security team provides the required separation of key access from the storage workload.

**Learn more:** [Customer-supplied encryption keys | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/customer-supplied-keys) · [Data encryption options | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing storage for two relational tables within a 10-TB database on Google Cloud. You need to support horizontally scalable transactions.  
  
You also need to optimize the data for range queries on non-key columns. What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud SQL for storage. Add secondary indexes to support query patterns.
Use Cloud SQL for storage. Use Cloud Dataflow to transform data to support query patterns.
Use Cloud Spanner for storage. Add secondary indexes to support query patterns.
Use Cloud Spanner for storage. Use Cloud Dataflow to transform data to support query patterns.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Spanner is a horizontally scalable relational database with transactional support. Secondary indexes make lookups and scans on non-primary-key columns more efficient, including range queries, avoiding full table scans.

**Learn more:** [Secondary indexes | Spanner | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/secondary-indexes) · [Getting started with Spanner using REST | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/getting-started/rest)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a new report for your large team in Google Data Studio 360, using Google BigQuery as its data source. Company policy requires that employees view only data associated with their own region, so you create and populate one table for each region. You need to enforce the regional data-access policy.  
  
Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783787336234-zwx5vcx6.png)

options.text: Ensure all the tables are included in global dataset.
Ensure each table is included in a dataset for a region.
Adjust the settings for each table to allow a related region-based security group view access.
Adjust the settings for each view to allow a related region-based security group view access.
Adjust the settings for each dataset to allow a related region-based security group view access.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery datasets are containers used to organize tables and control access to them. Storing each region’s table in that region’s dataset and granting the corresponding regional security group dataset-level viewer access enforces isolation: the group can query the tables in its assigned dataset but has no access granted to other regions’ datasets.

**Learn more:** [Control access to resources with IAM](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/control-access-to-resources-iam) · [Introduction to datasets](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/datasets-intro)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You want to use Google Stackdriver Logging to monitor Google BigQuery usage. You need an immediate notification sent to your monitoring tool when new data is appended to a specific table by using an insert job, but you do not want notifications for other tables. What should you do?

options.text: Make a call to the Stackdriver API to list all logs, and apply an advanced filter.
In the Stackdriver logging admin interface, and enable a log sink export to BigQuery.
In the Stackdriver logging admin interface, enable a log sink export to Google Cloud Pub/Sub, and subscribe to the topic from your monitoring tool.
Using the Stackdriver API, create a project sink with advanced log filter to export to Pub/Sub, and subscribe to the topic from your monitoring tool.

questions.explanation:
A project log sink with an advanced inclusion filter can select only the BigQuery audit-log entries for insert jobs that append data to the designated table. Routing the matching entries to a Pub/Sub topic lets a monitoring tool receive them in near real time, while excluding events for other tables.

**Learn more:** [Route log entries | Cloud Logging](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/routing/overview) · [View logs routed to Pub/Sub | Cloud Logging](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/pubsub)

You use Google BigQuery as your data warehouse. Users report that this simple query runs very slowly regardless of when it is executed:  
  
```sql  
SELECT country, state, city FROM [myproject:mydataset.mytable] GROUP BY country  
```  
  
You review the query plan and see the following output in the **Read** section of **Stage:1**:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783787339516-qrn3b6vi.jpg)  
  
What is the most likely cause of the delay in this query?

options.text: Users are running too many concurrent queries in the system
The [myproject:mydataset.mytable] table has too many partitions
Either the state or the city columns in the [myproject:mydataset.mytable] table have too many NULL values
Most rows in the [myproject:mydataset.mytable] table have the same value in the country column, causing data skew

questions.explanation:
Grouping distributes rows by the `country` key. When most rows share one country value, one worker must process a disproportionately large share of the data while other workers finish sooner, creating a data-skew bottleneck. BigQuery’s query-plan guidance identifies a large maximum-versus-average worker time as an indication of skewed data and recommends checking data distribution for aggregation stages.

**Learn more:** [Query plan and timeline | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/query-plan-explanation)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization follows a multi-cloud data storage strategy, storing data in Cloud Storage and in Amazon Web Services (AWS) S3 storage buckets. All data is located in US regions. You want to query current data with BigQuery, regardless of the cloud in which it is stored. You must let users query the tables from BigQuery without granting direct access to the data in the storage buckets. What should you do?

options.text: Setup a BigQuery Omni connection to the AWS S3 bucket data. Create BigLake tables over the Cloud Storage and S3 data and query the data using BigQuery directly.
Set up a BigQuery Omni connection to the AWS S3 bucket data. Create external tables over the Cloud Storage and S3 data and query the data using BigQuery directly.
Use the Storage Transfer Service to copy data from the AWS S3 buckets to Cloud Storage buckets. Create BigLake tables over the Cloud Storage data and query the data using BigQuery directly.
Use the Storage Transfer Service to copy data from the AWS S3 buckets to Cloud Storage buckets. Create external tables over the Cloud Storage data and query the data using BigQuery directly.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery Omni provides the connection required to query Amazon S3 data without copying it to Google Cloud. BigLake tables support Cloud Storage and Amazon S3 and use access delegation: the connection service account accesses the underlying objects, while users are granted access to the BigLake tables. This preserves up-to-date queries and avoids granting users direct bucket access.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to BigLake tables](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/biglake-intro) · [Introduction to BigQuery Omni](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/omni-introduction)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a single BigQuery dataset that contains customers’ street addresses. You need to retrieve every occurrence of street addresses from the dataset. What should you do?

options.text: Write a SQL query in BigQuery by using REGEXP_CONTAINS on all tables in your dataset to find rows where the word “street” appears.
Create a deep inspection job on each table in your dataset with Cloud Data Loss Prevention and create an inspection template that includes the STREET_ADDRESS infoType.
Create a discovery scan configuration on your organization with Cloud Data Loss Prevention and create an inspection template that includes the STREET_ADDRESS infoType.
Create a de-identification job in Cloud Data Loss Prevention and use the masking transformation.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Data Loss Prevention inspection job can inspect BigQuery tables using the built-in `STREET_ADDRESS` infoType and produce findings for detected address values. Configuring that inspection for each table in the dataset targets all of the dataset’s tables and supports retrieving the detected occurrences.

**Learn more:** [Inspect Google Cloud storage and databases for sensitive data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/inspecting-storage) · [Jobs and job triggers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/concepts-job-triggers)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a system that processes financial transactions. The system must support high throughput for concurrent user operations, and every operation requires low-latency reads and writes to individual records. You need to identify a storage solution that guarantees ACID compliance for the processed transactions. You want a managed Google Cloud service. What should you do?

options.text: Select Bigtable.
Select BigQuery.
Select Cloud Storage.
Select Spanner.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Spanner is a fully managed Google Cloud database built for highly concurrent transactional workloads at scale. Its read-write transactions provide ACID guarantees, including serializable isolation and external consistency, while supporting low-latency reads and writes to individual records.

**Learn more:** [Transactions overview | Spanner | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/transactions) · [Spanner documentation | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Banking-industry government regulations require protection of clients’ personally identifiable information (PII). Your company requires PII to be access-controlled, encrypted, and compliant with major data-protection standards. Along with using Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP), you want to follow Google-recommended practices and use service accounts to control access to PII. What should you do?

options.text: Assign the required Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles to every employee, and create a single service account to access project resources.
Use one service account to access a Cloud SQL database, and use separate service accounts for each human user.
Use Cloud Storage to comply with major data protection standards. Use one service account shared by all users.
Use Cloud Storage to comply with major data protection standards. Use multiple service accounts attached to IAM groups to grant the appropriate access to each group.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage supports IAM-based access control and encryption configurations that can help meet compliance requirements. Sensitive data should receive least-privilege access, and Google recommends dedicated, single-purpose service accounts instead of sharing one service account across multiple users or applications. Using multiple service accounts with IAM groups permits role-based, appropriately scoped access to PII.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for using service accounts securely](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/best-practices-service-accounts) · [Overview of access control for Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to connect multiple applications that have dynamic public IP addresses to a Cloud SQL instance. You configured users with strong passwords and enforced SSL connections to the Cloud SQL instance. You want to use the Cloud SQL public IP while ensuring the connections are secure. What should you do?

options.text: Add CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 network to Authorized Network. Use Identity and Access Management (IAM) to add users.
Add all application networks to Authorized Network and regularly update them.
Leave the Authorized Network empty. Use Cloud SQL Auth proxy on all applications.
Add CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 network to Authorized Network. Use Cloud SQL Auth proxy on all applications.

questions.explanation:
The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy authorizes application access with IAM credentials and automatically encrypts traffic with TLS. It avoids the need to maintain authorized-network IP allowlists, which is appropriate when client public IP addresses change dynamically. With the proxy, a Cloud SQL instance using public IP does not need an authorized network entry for those clients.

**Learn more:** [About the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/sql-proxy) · [Choose how to connect to Cloud SQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connection-options)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your weather app queries a database every 15 minutes to retrieve the current temperature. The frontend is powered by Google App Engine and serves millions of users. How should you design the frontend to respond to a database failure?

options.text: Issue a command to restart the database servers.
Retry the query with exponential backoff, up to a cap of 15 minutes.
Retry the query every second until it comes back online to minimize staleness of data.
Reduce the query frequency to once every hour until the database comes back online.

questions.explanation:
Exponential backoff progressively increases the delay between retry attempts, reducing pressure on an unavailable or overloaded database. A 15-minute cap preserves alignment with the application’s normal temperature-refresh interval, while immediate repeated retries from a frontend serving millions of users could create a thundering-herd retry storm.

**Learn more:** [Retry failed requests | Google Cloud IAM documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/retry-strategy)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are applying security best practices to your data pipeline. At present, you manually run jobs as the Project Owner. You want to automate these jobs by taking nightly batch files that contain non-public information from Google Cloud Storage, processing them with a Spark Scala job on a Google Cloud Dataproc cluster, and writing the results to Google BigQuery.  
  
How should you run this workload securely?

options.text: Restrict the Google Cloud Storage bucket so only you can see the files
Grant the Project Owner role to a service account, and run the job with it
Use a service account with the ability to read the batch files and to write to BigQuery
Use a user account with the Project Viewer role on the Cloud Dataproc cluster to read the batch files and write to BigQuery

questions.explanation:
A dedicated service account should run the automated workload with only the permissions it needs: read access to the Cloud Storage batch files and write access to BigQuery. This follows least privilege and avoids using a human identity or granting the broad Project Owner role. Google Cloud recommends service-account credentials for workloads running on Google Cloud resources and advises against granting basic Owner, Editor, or Viewer roles in production.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate to BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/authentication) · [Introduction to security and access controls in BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control-intro?hl=en)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],MJTelco needs to create a schema in Google Bigtable to enable historical analysis of the last 2 years of records. Each record arrives every 15 minutes and contains a unique device identifier and a data record. The most common query retrieves all data for a particular device for a particular day.  
  
Which schema should be used?

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783786950218-8pqpcc1g.png)

options.text: Rowkey: date#device_id Column data: data_point
Rowkey: date Column data: device_id, data_point
Rowkey: device_id Column data: date, data_point
Rowkey: data_point Column data: device_id, date
Rowkey: date#data_point Column data: device_id

questions.explanation:
Bigtable row keys should be based on the primary query pattern, and time-series schemas should avoid using a timestamp or date as the row-key prefix because it can create write hotspots. A `device_id` row key groups a device’s historical telemetry together, with the date and data point distinguishing that device’s records. This best supports device-and-day retrieval among the available schemas.

**Learn more:** [Schema design best practices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design?hl=en) · [Schema design for time series data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design-time-series)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use Bigtable for a real-time application with a heavy mixed read/write load. You have recently identified an additional use case that requires an hourly analytical job to calculate certain statistics across the entire database. You must ensure the reliability of both your production application and the analytical workload.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Export Bigtable dump to GCS and run your analytical job on top of the exported files.
Add a second cluster to an existing instance with a multi-cluster routing, use live-traffic app profile for your regular workload and batch-analytics profile for the analytics workload.
Add a second cluster to an existing instance with a single-cluster routing, use live-traffic app profile for your regular workload and batch-analytics profile for the analytics workload.
Increase the size of your existing cluster twice and execute your analytics workload on your new resized cluster.

questions.explanation:
Bigtable replication can isolate a read-only batch analytics workload from a production workload that mixes reads and writes by routing each through a separate app profile with single-cluster routing to different clusters. This prevents the large analytical reads from competing with production traffic for the same cluster’s resources. Multi-cluster routing is for availability/failover rather than dedicated workload isolation.

**Learn more:** [Examples of replication configurations | Bigtable](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/replication-settings) · [Replication overview | Bigtable](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/replication-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company based in the United States has developed an application that evaluates and responds to user actions. The data volume in its primary table increases by 250,000 records per second. Many third parties use the application's APIs to incorporate its functionality into their own frontend applications.  
  
The application's APIs must meet these requirements:  
  
- A single global endpoint  
- ANSI SQL support  
- Consistent access to the latest data  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Implement BigQuery with no region selected for storage or processing.
Implement Cloud Spanner with the leader in North America and read-only replicas in Asia and Europe.
Implement Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with the master in North America and read replicas in Asia and Europe.
Implement Bigtable with the primary cluster in North America and secondary clusters in Asia and Europe.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Spanner provides a globally distributed relational database with GoogleSQL support based on ANSI SQL, synchronous replication, and external consistency, so all clients can access current committed data through a global service. A multi-region configuration can designate a North American leader region and use read-only replicas in Asia and Europe for geographically distributed reads.

**Learn more:** [Spanner documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs) · [Regional, dual-region, and multi-region configurations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/instance-configurations)

questions.question: You work for a mid-sized enterprise that must migrate its operational-system transaction data from an on-premises database to GCP. The database is approximately 20 TB. Which database should you select?

options.text: Cloud SQL
Cloud Bigtable
Cloud Spanner
Cloud Datastore

questions.explanation:
Cloud Spanner is a fully managed, horizontally scalable database that provides strong ACID transactional consistency at large scale, making it appropriate for a 20 TB operational transaction database.\
\

questions.question: You are administering a Cloud Dataproc cluster. You need to speed up a job while minimizing costs and without losing work in progress on the clusters. What should you do?

options.text: Increase the cluster size with more non-preemptible workers.
Increase the cluster size with preemptible worker nodes, and configure them to forcefully decommission.
Increase the cluster size with preemptible worker nodes, and use Cloud Stackdriver to trigger a script to preserve work.
Increase the cluster size with preemptible worker nodes, and configure them to use graceful decommissioning.

questions.explanation:
Preemptible worker nodes provide lower-cost additional processing capacity. Graceful decommissioning removes workers without interrupting jobs in progress by allowing work to finish before the nodes are removed.\
\

questions.question: You are administering a Cloud Dataproc cluster. You need to speed up a job while minimizing costs and without losing work in progress on the clusters. What should you do?

options.text: Automate the 10 intents that cover 70% of the requests so that live agents can handle more complicated requests.
Automate the more complicated requests first because those require more of the agents' time.
Automate a blend of the shortest and longest intents to be representative of all intents.
Automate intents in places where common words such as 'payment' appear only once so the software isn't confused.

questions.explanation:
Automating the 10 simple, high-volume intents first addresses 70% of requests immediately and reserves live-agent capacity for the longer, more complex inquiries. Dialogflow recommends building large or complex agents iteratively by starting with dialogs that address top-level requests.

questions.question: Your team is addressing a binary-classification problem. You trained a support vector machine (SVM) classifier with default parameters and obtained an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.87 on the validation set. You want to improve the model's AUC. What should you do?

options.text: Perform hyperparameter tuning
Train a classifier with deep neural networks, because neural networks would always beat SVMs
Deploy the model and measure the real-world AUC; it's always higher because of generalization
Scale predictions you get out of the model (tune a scaling factor as a hyperparameter) in order to get the highest AUC

questions.explanation: Hyperparameter tuning can identify SVM settings better suited to the data, such as the regularization strength and kernel-related parameters, which can improve the model’s ranking performance and AUC. You must copy millions of sensitive patient records from a relational database into BigQuery. The database has a total size of 10 TB. You need to design a solution that is secure and efficient in time. What should you do?

options.text: Export the records from the database as an Avro file. Upload the file to GCS using gsutil, and then load the Avro file into BigQuery using the BigQuery web UI in the GCP Console.

Export the records from the database as an Avro file. Copy the file onto a Transfer Appliance and send it to Google, and then load the Avro file into BigQuery using the BigQuery web UI in the GCP Console.

Export the records from the database into a CSV file. Create a public URL for the CSV file, and then use Storage Transfer Service to move the file to Cloud Storage. Load the CSV file into BigQuery using the BigQuery web UI in the GCP Console.

Export the records from the database as an Avro file. Create a public URL for the Avro file, and then use Storage Transfer Service to move the file to Cloud Storage. Load the Avro file into BigQuery using the BigQuery web UI in the GCP Console.

questions.explanation:
Transfer Appliance securely moves a large on-premises data set to Cloud Storage using encrypted, tamper-resistant hardware, avoiding the time required for a potentially bandwidth-constrained 10 TB network upload. Avro is a preferred BigQuery load format because it embeds the schema and can be loaded in parallel. Publicly exposing the source file is not appropriate for sensitive patient records.

**Learn more:** [Transfer Appliance overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/transfer-appliance/docs/4.0/overview) · [Load Avro data from Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data-cloud-storage-avro)
