You operate an on-premises Apache Kafka cluster whose topics contain web-application logs. You need to replicate the data to Google Cloud for analysis in BigQuery and Cloud Storage. The preferred replication approach is mirroring, to avoid deploying Kafka Connect plugins.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Deploy a Kafka cluster on GCE VM Instances. Configure your on-prem cluster to mirror your topics to the cluster running in GCE. Use a Dataproc cluster or Dataflow job to read from Kafka and write to GCS.
Deploy a Kafka cluster on GCE VM Instances with the Pub/Sub Kafka connector configured as a Sink connector. Use a Dataproc cluster or Dataflow job to read from Kafka and write to GCS.
Deploy the Pub/Sub Kafka connector to your on-prem Kafka cluster and configure Pub/Sub as a Source connector. Use a Dataflow job to read from Pub/Sub and write to GCS.
Deploy the Pub/Sub Kafka connector to your on-prem Kafka cluster and configure Pub/Sub as a Sink connector. Use a Dataflow job to read from Pub/Sub and write to GCS.

questions.explanation:
Kafka mirroring replicates topics and records from a source Kafka cluster to a target Kafka cluster. Deploying a Kafka cluster on GCE provides the Google Cloud target for the on-premises topics; Dataproc or Dataflow can then consume the replicated Kafka data and write it to Cloud Storage for downstream analytics. The Pub/Sub Kafka connector requires Kafka Connect, so it does not meet the constraint to avoid Kafka Connect plugins. [Google Cloud documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/managed-service-for-apache-kafka/docs/connect-cluster/create-mirrormaker-connector?hl=en)

**Learn more:** [Create a MirrorMaker 2.0 connector](https://docs.cloud.google.com/managed-service-for-apache-kafka/docs/connect-cluster/create-mirrormaker-connector?hl=en) · [Connect Pub/Sub to Apache Kafka](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/connect_kafka)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You operate a network of 1000 sensors. The sensors produce time-series data: one metric per sensor each second, together with a timestamp. You already have 1 TB of data and anticipate that it will grow by 1 GB per day.  
  
You must access this data in two ways. The first access pattern requires retrieving the metric for one specific sensor at a specific timestamp, with median single-digit millisecond latency. The second access pattern requires running complex analytic queries on the data, including joins, once per day. How should you store this data?

options.text: Store your data in BigQuery. Concatenate the sensor ID and timestamp, and use it as the primary key.
Store your data in Bigtable. Concatenate the sensor ID and timestamp and use it as the row key. Perform an export to BigQuery every day.
Store your data in Bigtable. Concatenate the sensor ID and metric, and use it as the row key. Perform an export to BigQuery every day.
Store your data in BigQuery. Use the metric as a primary key.

questions.explanation:
Bigtable is suited to low-latency, single-keyed time-series data. A row key composed of the sensor ID and timestamp uniquely and directly addresses the measurement needed for the point read. Bigtable does not support joins, so exporting the data to BigQuery daily provides the analytical warehouse needed for complex queries and joins.

**Learn more:** [Bigtable overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/overview) · [Schema design for time series data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/schema-design-time-series)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying MariaDB SQL databases on GCE VM instances and must configure monitoring and alerting. You want to gather MariaDB metrics, including network connections, disk I/O, and replication status, with minimal development effort, and use Stackdriver for dashboards and alerts.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Install the OpenCensus Agent and create a custom metric collection application with a StackDriver exporter.
Place the MariaDB instances in an Instance Group with a Health Check.
Install the StackDriver Logging Agent and configure fluentd in_tail plugin to read MariaDB logs.
Install the StackDriver Agent and configure the MySQL plugin.

questions.explanation:
The Stackdriver Monitoring Agent's MySQL plugin collects database performance metrics for MySQL-compatible MariaDB instances and sends them to Cloud Monitoring, where they can be used in dashboards and alerting policies. Google Cloud's MariaDB integration likewise uses a `mysql` metrics receiver for MariaDB telemetry.

**Learn more:** [MySQL plugin | Cloud Monitoring](https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/agent/plugins/mysql) · [MariaDB | Cloud Monitoring](https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/agent/ops-agent/third-party/mariadb)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You currently store transactional data on premises in a PostgreSQL database. To modernize your data environment, you want to run transactional workloads and meet analytics requirements with one database. You must move to Google Cloud without changing database management systems while minimizing cost and complexity. What should you do?

options.text: Migrate and modernize your database with Cloud Spanner.
Migrate your workloads to AlloyDB for PostgreSQL.
Migrate to BigQuery to optimize analytics.
Migrate your PostgreSQL database to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL.

questions.explanation:
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL retains PostgreSQL compatibility while supporting hybrid transactional and analytical processing (HTAP), so complex analytics can run on live transactional data in the same managed database. Its built-in capabilities reduce operational and data-movement complexity compared with separating transactional and analytics systems.

**Learn more:** [AlloyDB overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs/overview?hl=en) · [AlloyDB for PostgreSQL](https://cloud.google.com/products/alloydb?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a messaging system using Pub/Sub to process clickstream data with an event-driven consumer app that depends on a push subscription. You need to configure a messaging system reliable enough to handle temporary downtime of the consumer app. You also need the system to store input messages that the subscriber cannot consume. The system must retry failed messages gradually, without overloading the consumer app, and store failed messages in a topic after a maximum of 10 retries. How should you configure the Pub/Sub subscription?

options.text: Increase the acknowledgement deadline to 10 minutes.
Use immediate redelivery as the subscription retry policy, and configure dead lettering to a different topic with maximum delivery attempts set to 10.
Use exponential backoff as the subscription retry policy, and configure dead lettering to the same source topic with maximum delivery attempts set to 10.
Use exponential backoff as the subscription retry policy, and configure dead lettering to a different topic with maximum delivery attempts set to 10.

questions.explanation:
Pub/Sub exponential backoff adds progressively longer delays between delivery attempts, which helps avoid overloading a consumer application during temporary failures. A dead-letter policy can forward messages that remain unacknowledged after a configured maximum number of delivery attempts; 10 is a supported value. The dead-letter topic must be a different topic from the source topic attached to the subscription.

**Learn more:** [Subscription retry policy | Pub/Sub | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscription-retry-policy) · [Dead-letter topics | Pub/Sub | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/handling-failures)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use a BigQuery dataset for analysis. You want to give third-party companies access to that same dataset. You need to keep data-sharing costs low and ensure the data remains current. Which solution should you choose?

options.text: Use Analytics Hub to control data access, and provide third party companies with access to the dataset.
Use Cloud Scheduler to export the data on a regular basis to Cloud Storage, and provide third-party companies with access to the bucket.
Create a separate dataset in BigQuery that contains the relevant data to share, and provide third-party companies with access to the new dataset.
Create a Dataflow job that reads the data in frequent time intervals, and writes it to the relevant BigQuery dataset or Cloud Storage bucket for third-party companies to use.

questions.explanation:
Analytics Hub, now called BigQuery sharing, enables zero-copy sharing of BigQuery datasets across organizational boundaries. Third-party subscribers can query a linked dataset that reflects the shared source data, avoiding replicated exports or scheduled copy pipelines. Google Cloud does not charge an additional fee to manage data exchanges or listings; subscribers pay for queries they run against the shared data.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to BigQuery sharing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/analytics-hub-introduction?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to rebuild your batch pipeline for structured data on Google Cloud. You use PySpark to perform data transformations at scale, but the pipelines take more than twelve hours to run. To speed up development and pipeline execution, you want a serverless tool and SOL syntax. You have already moved the raw data to Cloud Storage. How should you build the pipeline on Google Cloud while satisfying the speed and processing requirements?

options.text: Convert your PySpark commands into SparkSQL queries to transform the data, and then run your pipeline on Dataproc to write the data into BigQuery.
Ingest your data into Cloud SQL, convert your PySpark commands into SparkSQL queries to transform the data, and then use federated quenes from BigQuery for machine learning.
Ingest your data into BigQuery from Cloud Storage, convert your PySpark commands into BigQuery SQL queries to transform the data, and then write the transformations to a new table.
Use Apache Beam Python SDK to build the transformation pipelines, and write the data into BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery provides a serverless, distributed analytics platform that can batch-load structured data from Cloud Storage and execute scalable GoogleSQL transformations. Loading the raw data into BigQuery and writing the transformed results to a new table implements an ELT pipeline without managing Spark clusters, while retaining SQL-based development. [BigQuery overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/introduction?hl=en) and [Introduction to loading, transforming, and exporting data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/load-transform-export-intro?hl=en) describe this pattern.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/introduction?hl=en) · [Introduction to loading, transforming, and exporting data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/load-transform-export-intro?hl=en)

questions.question: Your company is pursuing a hybrid-cloud initiative. You have a complex data pipeline that transfers data between cloud-provider services and uses services from each cloud provider. Which cloud-native service should you use to orchestrate the entire pipeline?

options.text: Cloud Dataflow
Cloud Composer
Cloud Dataprep
Cloud Dataproc

questions.explanation:
Cloud Composer provides managed Apache Airflow workflow orchestration for authoring, scheduling, and monitoring data pipelines that span hybrid and multi-cloud environments, including workflows that coordinate services across cloud providers.\
\
**Learn more:** [Managed Service for Apache Airflow (formerly Cloud Composer)](https://cloud.google.com/products/managed-service-for-apache-airflow)

questions.question: Your company is pursuing a hybrid-cloud initiative. You have a complex data pipeline that transfers data between cloud-provider services and uses services from each cloud provider. Which cloud-native service should you use to orchestrate the entire pipeline?

options.text: Create a Cloud Composer environment and run the logic in Cloud Composer.
Create a Dataproc cluster, and use PySpark to apply the logic on your JSON file.
Invoke a Cloud Function instance that uses Python to apply the logic on your JSON file.
Invoke a subworkflow in Workflows to apply the logic on your JSON file.

questions.explanation:
A Python Cloud Function can encapsulate business logic that is unsupported by Workflows and be invoked synchronously over HTTP, allowing the workflow to continue to the Cloud Storage-to-BigQuery load only after the function returns. This is a lightweight fit for a 1KB response and avoids the unnecessary cluster or environment overhead of Dataproc and Cloud Composer. Workflows subworkflows remain limited to the Workflows language and standard library.

**Learn more:** [Workflows overview](https://cloud.google.com/workflows/docs/overview) · [Invoke Cloud Run functions or Cloud Run from Workflows](https://cloud.google.com/workflows/docs/calling-run-functions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying a new storage system for your media-streaming mobile application and determine that Google Cloud Datastore is the best fit. Your entities have multiple properties, with some able to hold multiple values. For example, in the `Movie` entity, the `actors` and `tags` properties have multiple values, but `date released` does not.  
  
Typical queries request all movies with `actor=<actorname>` ordered by `date_released`, or all movies with `tag=Comedy` ordered by `date_released`. How can you avoid a combinatorial explosion in the number of indexes?

options.text: ![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810397928-0trzy0jn.png)
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810401231-t1l50cxg.png)
Set the following in your entity options: exclude_from_indexes = 'actors, tags'
Set the following in your entity options: exclude_from_indexes = 'date_published'

questions.explanation:
Separate composite indexes for `actors` plus `date_released` and for `tags` plus `date_released` support the two independent query patterns. A composite index containing both multi-valued properties would create an entry for every combination of actor and tag values, causing combinatorial index growth.

**Learn more:** [Indexes | Datastore | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastore/docs/concepts/indexes)

questions.question: Your company is importing comma-separated values (CSV) files into Google BigQuery. The data imports successfully in full; however, the imported data does not match the source file byte-for-byte. What is the most likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The CSV data loaded in BigQuery is not flagged as CSV.
The CSV data has invalid rows that were skipped on import.
The CSV data loaded in BigQuery is not using BigQuery's default encoding.
The CSV data has not gone through an ETL phase before loading into BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery uses UTF-8 as the default CSV input encoding. If the source CSV uses a different encoding but the load uses the UTF-8 default, BigQuery attempts to convert the data to UTF-8, so the load can succeed even though the resulting values no longer match the source bytes exactly.\
\
**Learn more:** [BigQuery Job resource reference](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You created a patient-records database as a pilot project for a few hundred patients across three clinics. The design used one database table to represent all patients and their visits, with self-joins used to produce reports. Server resource utilization was 50%.  
  
Since then, the project scope has grown. The database must now store 100 times as many patient records. Reports can no longer be run because they either take too long or fail with insufficient compute resources. How should the database design be adjusted?

options.text: Add capacity (memory and disk space) to the database server by the order of 200.
Shard the tables into smaller ones based on date ranges, and only generate reports with prespecified date ranges.
Normalize the master patient-record table into the patient table and the visits table, and create other necessary tables to avoid self-join.
Partition the table into smaller tables, with one for each clinic. Run queries against the smaller table pairs, and use unions for consolidated reports.

questions.explanation: Normalizing the data model separates patient entities from visit entities and links them through appropriate keys. This eliminates duplicated patient attributes and avoids the inefficient self-joins caused by storing both entity types in one table, improving query efficiency and scalability as record volume grows.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have spent several days loading data from comma-separated values (CSV) files into the Google BigQuery table `CLICK_STREAM`. The `DT` column contains the epoch time of click events. For convenience, you selected a simple schema in which every field is of type `STRING`.  
  
Now you want to calculate web session durations for users visiting your site and change its data type to `TIMESTAMP`. You want to minimize migration effort without making future queries computationally expensive. What should you do?

options.text: Delete the table CLICK_STREAM, and then re-create it such that the column DT is of the TIMESTAMP type. Reload the data.
Add a column TS of the TIMESTAMP type to the table CLICK_STREAM, and populate the numeric values from the column TS for each row. Reference the column TS instead of the column DT from now on.
Create a view CLICK_STREAM_V, where strings from the column DT are cast into TIMESTAMP values. Reference the view CLICK_STREAM_V instead of the table CLICK_STREAM from now on.

Add two columns to the table CLICK STREAM: TS of the TIMESTAMP type and IS_NEW of the BOOLEAN type. Reload all data in append mode. For each appended row, set the value of IS_NEW to true. For future queries, reference the column TS instead of the column DT, with the WHERE clause ensuring that the value of IS_NEW must be true.

Construct a query to return every row of the table CLICK_STREAM, while using the built-in function to cast strings from the column DT into TIMESTAMP values. Run the query into a destination table NEW_CLICK_STREAM, in which the column TS is the TIMESTAMP type. Reference the table NEW_CLICK_STREAM instead of the table CLICK_STREAM from now on. In the future, new data is loaded into the table NEW_CLICK_STREAM.

questions.explanation:
Epoch values stored as strings should be converted once into a `TIMESTAMP` column and materialized in a replacement table. BigQuery provides timestamp conversion functions such as `TIMESTAMP_SECONDS` for epoch seconds; writing the converted result to a destination table prevents every future query from repeatedly converting the original string values. Subsequent loads can use the correct `TIMESTAMP` schema directly.

**Learn more:** [Timestamp functions | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/timestamp_functions) · [Conversion functions | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/conversion_functions)

questions.question: You are developing an ELT solution in BigQuery using Dataform. You need to run uniqueness and null-value checks on your final tables. What should you do to efficiently incorporate these checks into your pipeline?

options.text: Build BigQuery user-defined functions (UDFs).
Create Dataplex data quality tasks.
Build Dataform assertions into your code.
Write a Spark-based stored procedure.

questions.explanation:
Dataform assertions are native data-quality tests that can be defined in a final table’s configuration. The built-in `uniqueKey` or `uniqueKeys` assertions validate uniqueness, and `nonNull` validates that specified columns contain no null values; Dataform runs them with the workflow.\
\
**Learn more:** [Test data quality — Dataform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataform/docs/assertions)

questions.question: You are developing an ELT solution in BigQuery using Dataform. You need to run uniqueness and null-value checks on your final tables. What should you do to efficiently incorporate these checks into your pipeline?

options.text: Create a Standard Tier Memorystore for Redis instance in the development environment. Initiate a manual failover by using the limited-data-loss data protection mode.
Create a Standard Tier Memorystore for Redis instance in a development environment. Initiate a manual failover by using the force-data-loss data protection mode.
Increase one replica to Redis instance in production environment. Initiate a manual failover by using the force-data-loss data protection mode.
Initiate a manual failover by using the limited-data-loss data protection mode to the Memorystore for Redis instance in the production environment.

questions.explanation:
A separate Standard Tier development instance isolates the test from production data. The `force-data-loss` protection mode performs failover without data-loss control, making it suitable for an aggressive simulation of a disaster scenario in which the primary may be unhealthy or replication is not fully synchronized. In contrast, `limited-data-loss` can block failover to minimize data loss.

**Learn more:** [About manual failover | Memorystore for Redis](https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/about-manual-failover) · [High availability for Memorystore for Redis](https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/high-availability-for-memorystore-for-redis)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have multiple unstructured data sources in both your on-premises data center and the cloud. The data uses different formats, including Apache Parquet and CSV. You want to centralize this data in Cloud Storage.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are creating a data pipeline on Google Cloud. Use Cloud Dataprep to find null values in sample source data. Convert all nulls to 0 using a Cloud Dataprep job.
Use Cloud Dataflow to find null values in sample source data. Convert all nulls to 'none' using a Cloud Dataprep job.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are preparing a dataset for use across the organization. You must preprocess customer data that is stored in a restricted Cloud Storage bucket. The data will be used to produce consumer analyses, and you must comply with data privacy requirements.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use Dataflow and the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API to mask sensitive data. Write the processed data in BigQuery.
Use customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) to directly encrypt the data in Cloud Storage. Use federated queries from BigQuery. Share the encryption key by following the principle of least privilege.
Use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API and Dataflow to detect and remove sensitive fields from the data in Cloud Storage. Write the filtered data in BigQuery.
Use Dataflow and Cloud KMS to encrypt sensitive fields and write the encrypted data in BigQuery. Share the encryption key by following the principle of least privilege.

questions.explanation:
Dataflow can process the Cloud Storage data and invoke the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API to de-identify sensitive customer values through masking before loading the resulting dataset into BigQuery. This reduces exposure of sensitive data while retaining data utility for consumer analysis. Google’s Dataflow template for this workflow reads from Cloud Storage, uses Cloud DLP for de-identification, and writes de-identified data to BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Data Masking/Tokenization from Cloud Storage to BigQuery (using Cloud DLP)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/templates/provided/dlp-text-to-bigquery) · [De-identifying sensitive data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/deidentify-sensitive-data)

You are building a new Google Cloud pipeline that streams IoT data from Cloud Pub/Sub through Cloud Dataflow to BigQuery. While previewing the data, you find that approximately 2% of it appears to be corrupt. You need to update the Cloud Dataflow pipeline to filter out the corrupt data. What should you do?

options.text: Add a SideInput that returns a Boolean if the element is corrupt.
Add a ParDo transform in Cloud Dataflow to discard corrupt elements.
Add a Partition transform in Cloud Dataflow to separate valid data from corrupt data.
Add a GroupByKey transform in Cloud Dataflow to group all of the valid data together and discard the rest.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Dataflow ParDo applies custom logic to each element and can emit zero outputs for elements that fail validation. A DoFn that emits only valid records therefore discards corrupt records before they reach BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Apache Beam ParDo documentation](https://beam.apache.org/documentation/transforms/java/elementwise/pardo/)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization has two Google Cloud projects, project A and project B. Project A contains a Pub/Sub topic that receives data from confidential sources. Only resources in project A must be able to access the data in that topic. You need to ensure that project B, and any future project, cannot access data in the project A topic. What should you do?

options.text: Add firewall rules in project A so only traffic from the VPC in project A is permitted.
Configure VPC Service Controls in the organization with a perimeter around project A.
Use Identity and Access Management conditions to ensure that only users and service accounts in project A. can access resources in project A.
Configure VPC Service Controls in the organization with a perimeter around the VPC of project A.

questions.explanation:
An enforced VPC Service Controls perimeter around project A creates a boundary for restricted Google Cloud services, blocking cross-perimeter access unless explicitly allowed by ingress or egress rules. Pub/Sub is supported, and its protection covers administrator, publisher, and subscriber operations. This isolates the confidential topic from project B and future projects placed outside the perimeter.

**Learn more:** [Overview of VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview) · [Supported products and limitations — Pub/Sub](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/supported-products)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing storage for extremely large text files in a Google Cloud data pipeline. You need support for ANSI SQL queries, as well as compression and parallel loading from the input locations in accordance with Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Transform text files to compressed Avro using Cloud Dataflow. Use BigQuery for storage and query.
Transform text files to compressed Avro using Cloud Dataflow. Use Cloud Storage and BigQuery permanent linked tables for query.
Compress text files to gzip using the Grid Computing Tools. Use BigQuery for storage and query.
Compress text files to gzip using the Grid Computing Tools. Use Cloud Storage, and then import into Cloud Bigtable for query.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery provides SQL querying and managed analytical storage. For loading data, compressed Avro is the preferred format because its compressed blocks can still be read in parallel; this avoids the non-parallel behavior associated with gzip-compressed text input. Cloud Dataflow can transform the text files into compressed Avro before loading them into BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Load Avro data from Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data-cloud-storage-avro) · [Batch loading data](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/batch-loading-data)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are operating a Dataflow streaming pipeline with Streaming Engine and Horizontal Autoscaling enabled. You set the maximum worker count to 1000. The pipeline input consists of Pub/Sub messages containing notifications from Cloud Storage. One pipeline transform reads CSV files and emits one element for each CSV line. Job performance is poor, the pipeline is using only 10 workers, and the autoscaler is not adding more workers. What should you do to improve performance?

options.text: Enable Vertical Autoscaling to let the pipeline use larger workers.
Change the pipeline code, and introduce a Reshuffle step to prevent fusion.
Update the job to increase the maximum number of workers.
Use Dataflow Prime, and enable Right Fitting to increase the worker resources.

questions.explanation:
Dataflow Horizontal Autoscaling does not scale up when pipeline parallelism is limited, because additional workers cannot efficiently distribute the work. A Reshuffle transform creates a redistribution boundary that prevents the relevant transforms from being fused, allowing the CSV-line processing to run with greater parallelism. The maximum worker setting is already 1000, which is the supported maximum for this streaming autoscaling configuration.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot Dataflow autoscaling](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/troubleshoot-autoscaling) · [Horizontal Autoscaling](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/horizontal-autoscaling)

You administer a BigQuery on-demand environment. Your business intelligence tool submits hundreds of queries each day that aggregate a large (50 TB) sales-history fact table at the day and month levels. These queries have slow response times and exceed cost expectations. You need to reduce response time, lower query costs, and minimize maintenance. What should you do?

options.text: Build authorized views on top of the sales table to aggregate data at the day and month level.
Enable BI Engine and add your sales table as a preferred table.
Build materialized views on top of the sales table to aggregate data at the day and month level.
Create a scheduled query to build sales day and sales month aggregate tables on an hourly basis.

questions.explanation:
Materialized views precompute and periodically cache frequently used aggregate results. For repeated day- and month-level aggregations over a large fact table, BigQuery can use the cached results or automatically rewrite eligible base-table queries to use them, reducing data processed, latency, and cost. Automatic refresh minimizes the maintenance required.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to materialized views](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/materialized-views-intro) · [Use materialized views](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/materialized-views-use)

Your financial services company is adopting cloud technology and needs to store 50 TB of financial time-series data in the cloud. The data is updated frequently, with new data continuously streaming in. The company also wants to migrate its existing Apache Hadoop jobs to the cloud to gain insights from this data.  
  
Which product should it use to store the data?

options.text: Cloud Bigtable
Google BigQuery
Google Cloud Storage
Google Cloud Datastore

questions.explanation:
Cloud Bigtable is a scalable wide-column NoSQL database designed for high-throughput, low-latency workloads at terabyte-to-petabyte scale. It is appropriate for continuously ingested financial time-series data and supports Apache Hadoop MapReduce jobs that read from and write to Bigtable.\
\
**Learn more:** [Bigtable overview](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/overview) · [Integrations with Bigtable](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/integrations)

questions.question:
Your financial services company is adopting cloud technology and needs to store 50 TB of financial time-series data in the cloud. The data is updated frequently, with new data continuously streaming in. The company also wants to migrate its existing Apache Hadoop jobs to the cloud to gain insights from this data.  
  
Which product should it use to store the data?

options.text: Create a table called tracking_table and include a DATE column.
Create a partitioned table called tracking_table and include a TIMESTAMP column.
Create sharded tables for each day following the pattern tracking_table_YYYYMMDD.
Create a table called tracking_table with a TIMESTAMP column to represent the day.

questions.explanation:
A BigQuery table partitioned by a `TIMESTAMP` column supports streaming ingestion and lets daily queries filter on the partitioning column. BigQuery can prune partitions that do not match the day being analyzed, reducing the bytes scanned and therefore query cost. Date-sharded tables add schema and metadata overhead and are not recommended over time-partitioned tables.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to partitioned tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/partitioned-tables) · [Use the legacy streaming API](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/streaming-data-into-bigquery)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a production streaming pipeline that ingests data from Pub/Sub. You must update this streaming pipeline with improved business logic. Ensure that the updated pipeline reprocesses Pub/Sub messages delivered during the preceding two days. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use the Pub/Sub subscription clear-retry-policy flag
Use Pub/Sub Snapshot capture two days before the deployment.
Create a new Pub/Sub subscription two days before the deployment.
Use the Pub/Sub subscription retain-acked-messages flag.
Use Pub/Sub Seek with a timestamp.

questions.explanation:
A subscription must retain acknowledged messages so that previously delivered and acknowledged messages remain available for replay. Seeking that subscription to a timestamp two days in the past marks the retained messages after that timestamp as unacknowledged, causing them to be redelivered and reprocessed.

**Learn more:** [Replay and purge messages with seek | Pub/Sub | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/replay-overview) · [Replay a message in Pub/Sub by seeking to a snapshot or timestamp | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/replay-message)

options.text: Configure the data source system to pre-validate data before sending it to Dataflow and use the BigQuery ML.GENERATE_TEXT command to assign a sentiment score.
Use Dataflow to load all data into BigQuery and execute a SQL MERGE statement to flag invalid records and BigQuery ML to assign sentiment scores.
After the Dataflow load completes, execute a Cloud Run function to scan for invalid entries and call Vertex AI to assign sentiment scores.
Apply a ParDo transform in Dataflow to validate each element, use a RunInference transform to assign sentiment scores, and use side outputs to route valid/invalid records.

questions.explanation:
A `ParDo` transform applies custom validation independently to each record, making it appropriate for email-address validation. Its side outputs can split valid records from invalid records so the latter are sent to a manual-review path. Dataflow ML integrates Apache Beam’s `RunInference` API into the pipeline, enabling sentiment inference before the valid records are written to the data warehouse.

**Learn more:** [Programming model for Apache Beam](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/beam-programming-model) · [About Dataflow ML](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/machine-learning/ml-about)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Flowlogistic Case Study  
  
Company Overview  
  
Flowlogistic is a leading logistics and supply-chain provider. It helps businesses around the world manage their resources and transport them to their final destination. The company has grown rapidly, expanding its offerings to include rail, truck, aircraft, and oceanic shipping.  
  
Company Background  
  
The company began as a regional trucking company and later expanded into other logistics markets. Because it has not updated its infrastructure, managing and tracking orders and shipments has become a bottleneck. To improve operations, Flowlogistic developed proprietary technology to track shipments in real time at the parcel level. However, it cannot deploy this technology because its Apache Kafka-based technology stack cannot support the processing volume. In addition, Flowlogistic wants to further analyze its orders and shipments to determine the best way to deploy resources.  
  
Solution Concept  
  
Flowlogistic wants to implement two cloud-based concepts:  
  
- Use its proprietary technology in a real-time inventory-tracking system that shows the location of its loads.  
- Perform analytics on all orders and shipment logs, which include both structured and unstructured data, to determine how best to deploy resources and which markets to expand into. It also wants to use predictive analytics to identify shipment delays earlier.  
  
Existing Technical Environment  
  
Flowlogistic's architecture is in a single data center:  
  
- Databases  
  - 8 physical servers in 2 clusters  
  - SQL Server — user data, inventory, static data  
  - 3 physical servers  
  - Cassandra — metadata, tracking messages  
  - 10 Kafka servers — tracking-message aggregation and batch insert  
- Application servers — customer front end, middleware for order/customs  
  - 60 virtual machines across 20 physical servers  
  - Tomcat — Java services  
  - Nginx — static content  
  - Batch servers  
- Storage appliances  
  - iSCSI for virtual machine (VM) hosts  
  - Fibre Channel storage area network (FC SAN) — SQL Server storage  
  - Network-attached storage (NAS) — image storage, logs, backups  
- 10 Apache Hadoop/Spark servers  
  - Core Data Lake  
  - Data-analysis workloads  
- 20 miscellaneous servers  
  - Jenkins, monitoring, bastion hosts  
  
Business Requirements  
  
- Build a reliable and reproducible environment with scaled panty of production.  
- Aggregate data in a centralized Data Lake for analysis.  
- Use historical data to perform predictive analytics on future shipments.  
- Accurately track every shipment worldwide using proprietary technology.  
- Improve business agility and speed of innovation through rapid provisioning of new resources.  
- Analyze and optimize the architecture for cloud performance.  
- Migrate fully to the cloud if all other requirements are met.  
  
Technical Requirements  
  
- Handle both streaming and batch data.  
- Migrate existing Hadoop workloads.  
- Ensure the architecture is scalable and elastic to meet the company's changing demands.  
- Use managed services whenever possible.  
- Encrypt data in flight and at rest.  
- Connect a VPN between the production data center and cloud environment.  
  
SEO Statement  
  
We have grown so quickly that our inability to upgrade our infrastructure is really hampering further growth and efficiency. We are efficient at moving shipments around the world, but we are inefficient at moving data around.  
  
We need to organize our information so we can more easily understand where our customers are and what they are shipping.  
  
CTO Statement  
  
IT has never been a priority for us, so as our data has grown, we have not invested enough in our technology. I have a good staff to manage IT, but they are so busy managing our infrastructure that I cannot get them to do the things that really matter, such as organizing our data, building the analytics, and figuring out how to implement the CFO's tracking technology.  
  
CFO Statement  
  
Part of our competitive advantage is that we penalize ourselves for late shipments and deliveries. Knowing where our shipments are at all times has a direct correlation to our bottom line and profitability. Additionally, I do not want to commit capital to building out a server environment.  
  
Flowlogistic is rolling out its real-time inventory-tracking system. The tracking devices will all send package-tracking messages, which will now go to a single Google Cloud Pub/Sub topic instead of the Apache Kafka cluster. A subscriber application will process the messages for real-time reporting and store them in Google BigQuery for historical analysis. You want to ensure that the package data can be analyzed over time.  
  
Which approach should you use?

options.text: Attach the timestamp on each message in the Cloud Pub/Sub subscriber application as they are received.
Attach the timestamp and Package ID on the outbound message from each publisher device as they are sent to Clod Pub/Sub.
Use the NOW () function in BigQuery to record the event's time.
Use the automatically generated timestamp from Cloud Pub/Sub to order the data.

questions.explanation:
A publisher device should include both the package ID and the timestamp at which it generated the tracking event. This preserves the event-time history for each package even when messages are delayed, retried, or processed out of order. Pub/Sub-generated `publishTime` records only when the Pub/Sub service receives the message, while subscriber receipt time and BigQuery `NOW()` record later processing times.

**Learn more:** [Publish message overview — Pub/Sub](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/publish-message-overview) · [PubsubMessage REST reference — Pub/Sub](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/reference/rest/v1/PubsubMessage)

A new customer has asked for daily reports showing their net consumption of Google Cloud compute resources and the users of those resources. You need to generate these daily reports quickly and efficiently. What should you do?

options.text: Do daily exports of Cloud Logging data to BigQuery. Create views filtering by project, log type, resource, and user.
Filter data in Cloud Logging by project, resource, and user; then export the data in CSV format.
Filter data in Cloud Logging by project, log type, resource, and user, then import the data into BigQuery.
Export Cloud Logging data to Cloud Storage in CSV format. Cleanse the data using Dataprep, filtering by project, resource, and user.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Logging can route log entries to BigQuery through a sink, allowing the data to be queried without a load job. BigQuery views provide reusable SQL definitions that can filter the exported logs by project, log type, resource, and user, which supports efficient recurring daily reporting.

**Learn more:** [View logs routed to BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/bigquery) · [Route logs to supported destinations](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/configure_export_v2)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You uploaded 5 years of log data to Cloud Storage. A user reports that some log-data points fall outside their expected ranges, indicating errors. You need to resolve this issue and be able to run the process again in the future while retaining the original data for compliance reasons. What should you do?

options.text: Import the data from Cloud Storage into BigQuery. Create a new BigQuery table, and skip the rows with errors.
Create a Compute Engine instance and create a new copy of the data in Cloud Storage. Skip the rows with errors.

Create a Dataflow workflow that reads the data from Cloud Storage, checks for values outside the expected range, sets the value to an appropriate default, and writes the updated records to a new dataset in Cloud Storage.

Create a Dataflow workflow that reads the data from Cloud Storage, checks for values outside the expected range, sets the value to an appropriate default, and writes the updated records to the same dataset in Cloud Storage.

questions.explanation:
Dataflow supports reusable batch data-processing pipelines that read from Cloud Storage, transform records, and write results to an output destination. Replacing invalid values during the transformation retains each record, while writing the cleaned records to a separate Cloud Storage dataset preserves the original source data for compliance and enables repeatable processing.

**Learn more:** [Dataflow overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/overview) · [Read from Cloud Storage to Dataflow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/read-from-cloud-storage)

questions.question: You are building a new real-time data warehouse for your company and will use Google BigQuery streaming inserts. There is no guarantee that data will be sent only once, but you have a unique ID for each data row and an event timestamp. You want to ensure that duplicates are excluded while querying data interactively. Which query type should you use?

options.text: Include ORDER BY DESK on timestamp column and LIMIT to 1.
Use GROUP BY on the unique ID column and timestamp column and SUM on the values.
Use the LAG window function with PARTITION by unique ID along with WHERE LAG IS NOT NULL.
Use the ROW_NUMBER window function with PARTITION by unique ID along with WHERE row equals 1.

questions.explanation: `ROW_NUMBER()` partitioned by the unique ID assigns an ordinal to rows sharing that ID, allowing the query to retain only one row (`row = 1`) for each ID and thereby exclude duplicates from the interactive result.

questions.question: You are building a new real-time data warehouse for your company and will use Google BigQuery streaming inserts. There is no guarantee that data will be sent only once, but you have a unique ID for each data row and an event timestamp. You want to ensure that duplicates are excluded while querying data interactively. Which query type should you use?

options.text: Use Cloud Storage as a data warehouse, shell scripts for processing, and BigQuery to create views for desired datasets.
Use Dataflow to identify longtail and outlier data points programmatically, with BigQuery as a sink.
Use BigQuery to ingest, prepare, and then analyze the data, and then run queries to create views.
Use Cloud Composer to identify longtail and outlier data points, and then output a usable dataset to BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
Dataflow provides managed low-latency streaming data processing, allowing custom programmatic transforms to detect long-tail and outlier records and cleanse data before downstream AI use. It can write the processed output to BigQuery, which serves as the historical analytics warehouse.

**Learn more:** [Dataflow overview](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/overview) · [Dataflow managed I/O for BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/managed-io-bigquery)

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You want to use a database containing information about tissue samples to classify future tissue samples as either normal or mutated. You are assessing an unsupervised anomaly-detection method for classifying the tissue samples. Which two characteristics support this method? (Choose two.)

options.text: There are very few occurrences of mutations relative to normal samples.
There are roughly equal occurrences of both normal and mutated samples in the database.
You expect future mutations to have different features from the mutated samples in the database.
You expect future mutations to have similar features to the mutated samples in the database.
You already have labels for which samples are mutated and which are normal in the database.

questions.explanation:
Unsupervised anomaly detection establishes the normal pattern in predominantly normal data and identifies samples that diverge from that pattern. It is therefore well suited when mutated samples are rare and when future mutations may exhibit new, different features. Amazon SageMaker Random Cut Forest, an unsupervised anomaly-detection algorithm, detects data points that diverge from otherwise well-structured or patterned data.

**Learn more:** [How RCF Works - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/rcf_how-it-works.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You want to build a managed Hadoop system for your data lake. The data-transformation process consists of a sequence of Hadoop jobs that run in order.  
  
To implement a design that separates storage from compute, you decided to use the Cloud Storage connector for all input, output, and intermediate data. However, you found that one Hadoop job runs very slowly on Cloud Dataproc compared with the on-premises bare-metal Hadoop environment (8-core nodes with 100-GB RAM). Analysis shows that this particular Hadoop job is disk-I/O intensive. You want to resolve the issue. What should you do?

options.text: Allocate sufficient memory to the Hadoop cluster, so that the intermediary data of that particular Hadoop job can be held in memory
Allocate sufficient persistent disk space to the Hadoop cluster, and store the intermediate data of that particular Hadoop job on native HDFS
Allocate more CPU cores of the virtual machine instances of the Hadoop cluster so that the networking bandwidth for each instance can scale up
Allocate additional network interface card (NIC), and configure link aggregation in the operating system to use the combined throughput when working with Cloud Storage

questions.explanation:
For I/O-intensive Hadoop processing, intermediate data should be stored on the cluster’s native HDFS, backed by provisioned persistent disks, while durable source and final datasets can remain in Cloud Storage. This avoids the higher latency of repeatedly reading and writing intermediate data through Cloud Storage and preserves the separation of persistent storage from compute for the data lake.

**Learn more:** [Dataproc Hadoop data storage](https://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/concepts/dataproc-hdfs) · [Dataproc best practices](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/dataproc-best-practices-guide)

questions.question: Your company has developed a TensorFlow neural-network model with many neurons and layers. The model fits the training data well; however, it performs poorly when tested on new data. What method can you use to address this?

options.text: Threading
Serialization
Dropout Methods
Dimensionality Reduction

questions.explanation: Strong performance on training data coupled with poor performance on unseen data indicates overfitting. Dropout regularizes a neural network by randomly omitting units during training, which reduces reliance on particular neurons and improves generalization to new data.

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: Your company has developed a TensorFlow neural-network model with many neurons and layers. The model fits the training data well; however, it performs poorly when tested on new data. What method can you use to address this?

options.text: Run the gsutil utility to transfer all ORC files from the Cloud Storage bucket to HDFS. Mount the Hive tables locally.
Run the gsutil utility to transfer all ORC files from the Cloud Storage bucket to any node of the Dataproc cluster. Mount the Hive tables locally.

Run the gsutil utility to transfer all ORC files from the Cloud Storage bucket to the master node of the Dataproc cluster. Then run the Hadoop utility to copy them do HDFS. Mount the Hive tables from HDFS.
Leverage Cloud Storage connector for Hadoop to mount the ORC files as external Hive tables. Replicate external Hive tables to the native ones.
Load the ORC files into BigQuery. Leverage BigQuery connector for Hadoop to mount the BigQuery tables as external Hive tables. Replicate external Hive tables to the native ones.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Dataproc installs an HDFS-compatible Cloud Storage connector, allowing Hive external tables to reference ORC files directly at `gs://` locations; their data can then be written into native Hive tables. To populate local HDFS, objects can be copied from Cloud Storage to the master node’s local filesystem with `gsutil` and then copied into HDFS with Hadoop. `gsutil` itself does not directly transfer data into HDFS.

**Learn more:** [Dataproc FAQ](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/resources/faq) · [gcloud dataproc jobs submit hive reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/dataproc/jobs/submit/hive)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are working on a regression task in a natural-language-processing domain and have 100M labeled examples in the dataset. You randomly shuffled the data and split it into training and test samples at a 90/10 ratio. After training the neural network and evaluating it on the test set, you find that the model’s root-mean-squared error (RMSE) is twice as high on the training set as on the test set. How should you improve the model’s performance?

options.text: Increase the share of the test sample in the train-test split.
Try to collect more data and increase the size of your dataset.
Try out regularization techniques (e.g., dropout of batch normalization) to avoid overfitting.
Increase the complexity of your model by, e.g., introducing an additional layer or increase sizing the size of vocabularies or n-grams used.

questions.explanation: A model whose training error is unusually high relative to its test error is not displaying the usual overfitting pattern; it lacks sufficient ability to fit the training data. Increasing model capacity, such as by adding a layer or expanding relevant feature representations such as vocabularies or n-grams, addresses underfitting.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to migrate a Redis database from an on-premises data center to a Memorystore for Redis instance. You want to follow Google-recommended practices and complete the migration with minimal cost, time, and effort. What should you do?

options.text: Make an RDB backup of the Redis database, use the gsutil utility to copy the RDB file into a Cloud Storage bucket, and then import the RDB file into the Memorystore for Redis instance.
Make a secondary instance of the Redis database on a Compute Engine instance and then perform a live cutover.
Create a Dataflow job to read the Redis database from the on-premises data center and write the data to a Memorystore for Redis instance.
Write a shell script to migrate the Redis data and create a new Memorystore for Redis instance.

questions.explanation:
Memorystore for Redis can import a native Redis RDB backup from a Cloud Storage bucket. This provides the managed, supported migration path and avoids the additional infrastructure and custom development required by a live replica, Dataflow pipeline, or shell-script migration.

**Learn more:** [Import data to a Redis instance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/import-data?hl=en) · [About importing and exporting data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/about-importing-exporting)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s `customer_order` table in BigQuery holds the order history for 10 million customers and has a table size of 10 PB. You need to build a dashboard for the support team to view order history. The dashboard includes two filters: `country_name` and `username`. Both are STRING data types in the BigQuery table. When a filter is applied, the dashboard retrieves order history from the table and displays the query results. However, applying the filters to the following query makes the dashboard slow to display results:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783859960056-7i7x65z3.png)  
  
How should the BigQuery table be redesigned to enable faster access?

options.text: Cluster the table by country and username fields.
Cluster the table by country field, and partition by username field.
Partition the table by country and username fields.
Partition the table by _PARTITIONTIME.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery clustering supports STRING columns and organizes storage blocks by the ordered clustering columns. Clustering first by country and then by username lets queries filtering on those columns prune irrelevant blocks, reducing the data scanned. BigQuery partitioning cannot use multiple columns, and these STRING fields are not valid time-unit or integer-range partitioning columns.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to clustered tables | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/clustered-tables) · [Introduction to partitioned tables | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/partitioned-tables)

questions.question: You are responsible for creating your company’s ETL pipelines to run on an Apache Hadoop cluster. The pipeline will need checkpointing and pipeline splitting. Which method should you use to write the pipelines?

options.text: PigLatin using Pig
HiveQL using Hive
Java using MapReduce
Python using MapReduce

questions.explanation:
Pig Latin provides dataflow operators suited to Hadoop ETL pipelines. Its `SPLIT` operator partitions one relation into multiple relations, and `STORE` persists results to the filesystem, supporting intermediate checkpoint outputs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Apache Pig Latin Basics](https://pig.apache.org/docs/r0.16.0/basic.html)

options.text: Use Dataflow for your workflow pipelines. Use Cloud Run triggers for scheduling.
Use Dataflow for your workflow pipelines. Use shell scripts to schedule workflows.
Use Cloud Composer in a Shared VPC configuration. Place the Cloud Composer resources in the host project.
Use Cloud Composer in a Shared VPC configuration. Place the Cloud Composer resources in the service project.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Composer is Google’s managed Apache Airflow service for authoring, scheduling, and monitoring workflows. In a Shared VPC configuration, the Cloud Composer environment is located in the service project, while the host project contains the Shared VPC network and subnetworks.

**Learn more:** [Configure Shared VPC networking | Managed Service for Apache Airflow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/composer/docs/composer-3/configure-shared-vpc)

You are designing a data mesh on Google Cloud, using Dataplex to manage data in BigQuery and Cloud Storage. You want to simplify permissions for data assets. You are creating a customer virtual lake with two user groups:  
  
- Data engineers, who need full access to the data lake  
- Analytic users, who need access to curated data  
  
You need to assign access rights to these two groups. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Grant the dataplex.dataOwner role to the data engineer group on the customer data lake.2. Grant the dataplex.dataReader role to the analytic user group on the customer curated zone.
1. Grant the dataplex.dataReader role to the data engineer group on the customer data lake.2. Grant the dataplex.dataOwner to the analytic user group on the customer curated zone.

1. Grant the bigquery.dataOwner role on BigQuery datasets and the storage.objectCreator role on Cloud Storage buckets to data engineers.2. Grant the bigquery.dataViewer role on BigQuery datasets and the storage.objectViewer role on Cloud Storage buckets to analytic users.

1. Grant the bigquery.dataViewer role on BigQuery datasets and the storage.objectViewer role on Cloud Storage buckets to data engineers.2. Grant the bigquery.dataOwner role on BigQuery datasets and the storage.objectEditor role on Cloud Storage buckets to analytic users.

questions.explanation:
The Dataplex Data Owner role provides full access to a managed resource and all of its child resources, making it appropriate at the lake level for data engineers. The Dataplex Data Reader role provides read access to data and metadata, making it appropriate on the curated zone for analytic users. Dataplex can apply these roles to the managed BigQuery and Cloud Storage resources, avoiding separate service-level permissions.

**Learn more:** [Knowledge Catalog IAM roles](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataplex/docs/iam-roles?hl=en)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You keep historic data in Cloud Storage. You need to run analytics on that historic data. You want a solution that detects invalid data entries and performs data transformations without requiring programming or SQL knowledge.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Dataflow with Beam to detect errors and perform transformations.
Use Cloud Dataprep with recipes to detect errors and perform transformations.
Use Cloud Dataproc with a Hadoop job to detect errors and perform transformations.
Use federated tables in BigQuery with queries to detect errors and perform transformations.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Dataprep provides a visual, no-code interface for exploring, profiling, cleaning, and transforming data. It detects data-quality issues such as missing or mismatched values and uses recipes to define repeatable transformations. [Google Cloud: Easy data preparation with Cloud Dataprep](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/gcp/google-cloud-platform-adds-new-tools-for-easy-data-preparation-and-integration)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a pipeline that publishes application events to a Pub/Sub topic. Although message ordering does not matter, you must be able to aggregate events across disjoint hourly intervals before loading the results into BigQuery for analysis. Which technology should you use to process and load this data to BigQuery while ensuring that it scales for large event volumes?

options.text: Create a Cloud Function to perform the necessary data processing that executes using the Pub/Sub trigger every time a new message is published to the topic.
Schedule a Cloud Function to run hourly, pulling all available messages from the Pub/Sub topic and performing the necessary aggregations.
Schedule a batch Dataflow job to run hourly, pulling all available messages from the Pub/Sub topic and performing the necessary aggregations.
Create a streaming Dataflow job that reads continually from the Pub/Sub topic and performs the necessary aggregations using tumbling windows.

questions.explanation:
A streaming Dataflow pipeline is designed to read the unbounded event stream from Pub/Sub and perform stateful aggregations by using windows. Tumbling windows are fixed, non-overlapping intervals, so hourly tumbling windows produce one aggregation per disjoint hour before the results are written to BigQuery. Dataflow supports scalable streaming Pub/Sub-to-BigQuery pipelines, including windowed aggregations.

**Learn more:** [Streaming pipelines | Cloud Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/streaming-pipelines) · [Performance characteristics of Pub/Sub to BigQuery pipelines | Cloud Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/pubsub-bigquery-performance)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Data Analysts at your company are assigned the Cloud IAM Owner role in their projects so they can work with multiple GCP products in those projects. Your organization requires that all BigQuery data access logs be retained for 6 months. You need to ensure that only audit personnel at your company can access the data access logs for every project. What should you do?

options.text: Enable data access logs in each Data Analyst's project. Restrict access to Stackdriver Logging via Cloud IAM roles.
Export the data access logs via a project-level export sink to a Cloud Storage bucket in the Data Analysts' projects. Restrict access to the Cloud Storage bucket.
Export the data access logs via a project-level export sink to a Cloud Storage bucket in a newly created projects for audit logs. Restrict access to the project with the exported logs.
Export the data access logs via an aggregated export sink to a Cloud Storage bucket in a newly created project for audit logs. Restrict access to the project that contains the exported logs.

questions.explanation:
An organization-level aggregated sink routes matching log entries from the organization and all child projects to a centralized destination. Exporting BigQuery Data Access audit logs to a Cloud Storage bucket in a separate audit project allows retention for at least six months and lets IAM access to that project be limited to audit personnel. Owners of the source projects do not automatically receive access to the separate destination project.

**Learn more:** [Collate and route organization- and folder-level logs to supported destinations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/aggregated_sinks) · [Aggregated sinks overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/aggregated_sinks_overview)

Restrict access to the project that contains the exported logs."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"An organization-level aggregated sink routes matching log entries from the organization and all child projects to a centralized destination. Exporting BigQuery Data Access audit logs to a Cloud Storage bucket in a separate audit project allows retention for at least six months and lets IAM access to that project be limited to audit personnel. Owners of the source projects do not automatically receive access to the separate destination project.

You are developing a new data pipeline to share data between two different application types: job generators and job runners. Your solution must scale as usage increases and support adding new applications without adversely affecting the performance of existing applications. What should you do?

options.text: Create an API using App Engine to receive and send messages to the applications
Use a Cloud Pub/Sub topic to publish jobs, and use subscriptions to execute them
Create a table on Cloud SQL, and insert and delete rows with the job information
Create a table on Cloud Spanner, and insert and delete rows with the job information

questions.explanation:
Cloud Pub/Sub provides asynchronous, scalable messaging that decouples applications producing jobs from applications processing them. Job generators publish jobs to a topic, while job runners consume them through subscriptions. New consumers can be added through subscriptions without requiring generators or existing runners to change or directly interact, preserving their independence and performance.

**Learn more:** [What is Pub/Sub and Pub/Sub Lite?](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/pubsub_overview) · [Publish message overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/publish-message-overview)

You have chosen to use Cloud Datastore to ingest vehicle telemetry data in real time. You want to build a storage system that accommodates long-term data growth while keeping costs low. You also want to periodically create data snapshots so that you can perform point-in-time (PIT) recovery or clone data for Cloud Datastore in another environment. You want to retain these snapshots for a long time. Which two methods can achieve this?  
  
(Choose two.)

options.text: Use managed export, and store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket using Nearline or Coldline class.
Use managed export, and then import to Cloud Datastore in a separate project under a unique namespace reserved for that export.
Use managed export, and then import the data into a BigQuery table created just for that export, and delete temporary export files.

Write an application that uses Cloud Datastore client libraries to read all the entities. Treat each entity as a BigQuery table row via BigQuery streaming insert. Assign an export timestamp for each export, and attach it as an extra column for each row. Make sure that the BigQuery table is partitioned using the export timestamp column.

Write an application that uses Cloud Datastore client libraries to read all the entities. Format the exported data into a JSON file. Apply compression before storing the data in Cloud Source Repositories.

questions.explanation:
Managed export creates Cloud Storage export files that can be retained as recoverable copies; Nearline and Coldline provide lower-cost storage for infrequently accessed data. Managed export files can also be imported into another Datastore mode database, including one in a different project, which supports creating a separate-environment clone. BigQuery copies and custom streaming exports do not preserve a Datastore importable backup, and Cloud Source Repositories is not suited to long-term telemetry archives.

**Learn more:** [Exporting and Importing Entities | Datastore | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastore/docs/export-import-entities?hl=en) · [Storage classes | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-classes)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have migrated your on-premises Apache Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) data lake to Cloud Storage. The data-science team must process the data using Apache Spark and SQL. Security policies must be enforced at the column level. You need a cost-effective solution that can scale to a data mesh. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Deploy a long-living Dataproc cluster with Apache Hive and Ranger enabled.2. Configure Ranger for column level security.3. Process with Dataproc Spark or Hive SQL.
1. Define a BigLake table.2. Create a taxonomy of policy tags in Data Catalog.3. Add policy tags to columns.4. Process with the Spark-BigQuery connector or BigQuery SQL.
1. Load the data to BigQuery tables.2. Create a taxonomy of policy tags in Data Catalog.3. Add policy tags to columns.4. Process with the Spark-BigQuery connector or BigQuery SQL.

1. Apply an Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy at the file level in Cloud Storage.2. Define a BigQuery external table for SQL processing.3. Use Dataproc Spark to process the Cloud Storage files.

questions.explanation:
BigLake exposes Cloud Storage data through a governed table layer without requiring it to be loaded into BigQuery. Policy tags applied to BigLake table columns provide column-level access control, and the BigQuery Storage API enforces those policies for BigQuery SQL and supported connectors such as Apache Spark. This supports a scalable, centrally governed data-mesh approach while avoiding a continuously running cluster.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to BigLake tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/biglake-intro) · [Introduction to column-level access control](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/column-level-security-intro)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your chemical company must manually review documentation for a customer order. You use a Pub/Sub pull subscription so sales agents receive the order details. You need to ensure that orders are not processed twice by different sales agents and that this workflow does not gain additional complexity. What should you do?

options.text: Use a Deduplicate PTransform in Dataflow before sending the messages to the sales agents.
Create a transactional database that monitors the pending messages.
Use Pub/Sub exactly-once delivery in your pull subscription.
Create a new Pub/Sub push subscription to monitor the orders processed in the agent's system.

questions.explanation:
Pub/Sub exactly-once delivery is supported for pull subscriptions and prevents duplicate message deliveries after a successful acknowledgment. It therefore helps ensure that a single order is not processed more than once without adding separate processing or monitoring components.

**Learn more:** [Exactly-once delivery | Pub/Sub | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/exactly-once-delivery)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have developed three data-processing jobs. One runs a Cloud Dataflow pipeline that transforms data uploaded to Cloud Storage and writes the results to BigQuery. The second ingests data from on-premises servers and uploads it to Cloud Storage. The third is a Cloud Dataflow pipeline that retrieves information from third-party data providers and uploads that information to Cloud Storage.  
  
You need to schedule and monitor execution of these three workflows, and manually run them when necessary. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Direct Acyclic Graph in Cloud Composer to schedule and monitor the jobs.
Use Stackdriver Monitoring and set up an alert with a Webhook notification to trigger the jobs.
Develop an App Engine application to schedule and request the status of the jobs using GCP API calls.
Set up cron jobs in a Compute Engine instance to schedule and monitor the pipelines using GCP API calls.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Composer provides managed Apache Airflow orchestration through DAGs. DAGs can schedule dependent workflow tasks, expose run status and logs for monitoring, and be triggered manually through the Google Cloud console or Airflow UI. This directly supports coordinating the Dataflow and Cloud Storage jobs without building custom scheduling and monitoring infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Managed Service for Apache Airflow documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/composer/docs) · [Schedule and trigger Airflow DAGs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/composer/docs/composer-3/schedule-and-trigger-dags)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company’s data platform receives CSV dumps of booking and user-profile data from upstream sources into Cloud Storage. The data analyst team needs to join these datasets using the email field present in both datasets for analysis. However, personally identifiable information (PII) must not be accessible to the analysts. You need to de-identify the email field in both datasets before loading them into BigQuery for the analysts. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Create a pipeline to de-identify the email field by using recordTransformations in Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP) with masking as the de-identification transformations type.2. Load the booking and user profile data into a BigQuery table.

1. Create a pipeline to de-identify the email field by using recordTransformations in Cloud DLP with format-preserving encryption with FFX as the de-identification transformation type.2. Load the booking and user profile data into a BigQuery table.

1. Load the CSV files from Cloud Storage into a BigQuery table, and enable dynamic data masking.2. Create a policy tag with the email mask as the data masking rule.3. Assign the policy to the email field in both tables. A4. Assign the Identity and Access Management bigquerydatapolicy.maskedReader role for the BigQuery tables to the analysts.

1. Load the CSV files from Cloud Storage into a BigQuery table, and enable dynamic data masking.2. Create a policy tag with the default masking value as the data masking rule.3. Assign the policy to the email field in both tables.4. Assign the Identity and Access Management bigquerydatapolicy.maskedReader role for the BigQuery tables to the analysts

questions.explanation:
Cloud DLP record transformations can de-identify tabular fields before they are loaded into BigQuery. FFX format-preserving encryption replaces each email with a cryptographically protected token; using the same key and configuration for both datasets yields the same token for the same email, so analysts can join on the protected field without accessing the original PII. Simple masking and default dynamic masking do not provide a reliable, shared join key across the datasets.

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud Sensitive Data Protection: Transformation reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/transformations-reference) · [Google Cloud Sensitive Data Protection: De-identifying sensitive data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/deidentify-sensitive-data)

questions.question: You need to automate execution of a multi-step data pipeline on Google Cloud. The pipeline contains Dataproc and Dataflow jobs with multiple interdependencies. You want to use managed services where possible, and the pipeline must run daily. Which tool should you use?

options.text: cron
Cloud Composer
Cloud Scheduler
Workflow Templates on Dataproc

questions.explanation:
Cloud Composer is a fully managed Apache Airflow service for authoring, scheduling, and monitoring DAG-based data pipelines. Its DAGs express dependencies among tasks and can orchestrate Google Cloud services such as Dataproc and Dataflow on a recurring daily schedule.\
\
**Learn more:** [Choose Workflows or Cloud Composer for service orchestration](https://cloud.google.com/workflows/docs/choose-orchestration) · [Run a Hadoop wordcount job on a Cloud Dataproc cluster](https://docs.cloud.google.com/composer/docs/composer-3/run-hadoop-wordcount-job)

questions.question: You need to automate execution of a multi-step data pipeline on Google Cloud. The pipeline contains Dataproc and Dataflow jobs with multiple interdependencies. You want to use managed services where possible, and the pipeline must run daily. Which tool should you use?

options.text: Assign a function with notification logic to the on_retry_callback parameter for the operator responsible for the task at risk.
Configure a Cloud Monitoring alert on the sla_missed metric associated with the task at risk to trigger a notification.
Assign a function with notification logic to the on_failure_callback parameter tor the operator responsible for the task at risk.
Assign a function with notification logic to the sla_miss_callback parameter for the operator responsible for the task at risk.

questions.explanation:
An operator-level `on_failure_callback` is invoked when its task instance fails, allowing task-specific notification logic to run. A retry callback applies only when a retry occurs, and SLA-miss mechanisms report missed execution-time objectives rather than task failure.

**Learn more:** [Apache Airflow hierarchy and alerting options with Cloud Composer](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/apache-airflow-hierarchy-and-alerting-options-with-cloud-composer)
