questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a cloud-native historical-data processing system that must meet the following conditions:  
  
- The data being analyzed is in CSV, Avro, and PDF formats and will be accessed by multiple analysis tools, including Dataproc, BigQuery, and Compute Engine.  
- A batch pipeline transfers data daily.  
- Performance is not a consideration for the solution.  
- The solution design must maximize availability.  
  
How should you design the data storage for this solution?

options.text: Create a Dataproc cluster with high availability. Store the data in HDFS, and perform analysis as needed.
Store the data in BigQuery. Access the data using the BigQuery Connector on Dataproc and Compute Engine.
Store the data in a regional Cloud Storage bucket. Access the bucket directly using Dataproc, BigQuery, and Compute Engine.
Store the data in a multi-regional Cloud Storage bucket. Access the data directly using Dataproc, BigQuery, and Compute Engine.

questions.explanation:
A multi-regional Cloud Storage bucket provides shared object storage that Dataproc, BigQuery, and Compute Engine can access directly, while accommodating the CSV, Avro, and PDF source files. Multi-region buckets provide cross-region redundancy and higher availability than regional buckets; their potentially variable performance is acceptable when performance is not a factor.

**Learn more:** [Bucket locations | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-locations) · [Data availability and durability | Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/availability-durability)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a real-time prediction engine that streams files, which might contain PII (personal identifiable information) data, into Cloud Storage and ultimately into BigQuery. You need to ensure that sensitive data is masked while retaining referential integrity, since names and email addresses are frequently used as join keys.  
  
How should you use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API (DLP API) to ensure the PII data is inaccessible to unauthorized individuals?

options.text: Create a pseudonym by replacing the PII data with cryptogenic tokens, and store the non-tokenized data in a locked-down button.
Redact all PII data, and store a version of the unredacted data in a locked-down bucket.
Scan every table in BigQuery, and mask the data it finds that has PII.
Create a pseudonym by replacing PII data with a cryptographic format-preserving token.

questions.explanation:
Cloud DLP format-preserving encryption pseudonymizes detected PII by replacing it with cryptographic tokens. With the same cryptographic key, the same input consistently produces the same token, preserving referential integrity for joins while concealing the original names and email addresses.

**Learn more:** [Transformation reference — Sensitive Data Protection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/transformations-reference?hl=en) · [Pseudonymization — Sensitive Data Protection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/pseudonymization)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization keeps customer data in an on-premises Apache Hadoop cluster in Apache Parquet format. Apache Spark jobs running on that cluster process the data daily.  
  
You are migrating both the Spark jobs and Parquet data to Google Cloud. BigQuery will be used for future transformation pipelines, so the data must be available in BigQuery. You want to use managed services while minimizing ETL processing changes and operational costs. What should you do?

options.text: Migrate your data to Cloud Storage and migrate the metadata to Dataproc Metastore (DPMS). Refactor Spark pipelines to write and read data on Cloud Storage, and run them on Dataproc Serverless.
Migrate your data to Cloud Storage and register the bucket as a Dataplex asset. Refactor Spark pipelines to write and read data on Cloud Storage, and run them on Dataproc Serverless.
Migrate your data to BigQuery. Refactor Spark pipelines to write and read data on BigQuery, and run them on Dataproc Serverless.
Migrate your data to BigLake. Refactor Spark pipelines to write and read data on Cloud Storage, and run them on Dataproc on Compute Engine.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Storage bucket registered as a Dataplex asset can be discovered and cataloged for BigQuery, including BigLake tables over Parquet files. Keeping the data in Cloud Storage preserves the existing file-based Spark pattern, and Dataproc Serverless runs Spark without managing clusters. This minimizes both pipeline refactoring and operational overhead while making the data accessible in BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Discover and catalog Cloud Storage data](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/automatic-discovery) · [Introduction to BigLake tables](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/biglake-intro)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a large bank with locations across North America. You are configuring a data-storage system to process bank-account transactions. You need ACID compliance and SQL data access. Which solution is suitable?

options.text: Store transaction data in Cloud Spanner. Enable stale reads to reduce latency.
Store transaction in Cloud Spanner. Use locking read-write transactions.
Store transaction data in BigQuery. Disabled the query cache to ensure consistency.
Store transaction data in Cloud SQL. Use a federated query BigQuery for analysis.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Spanner supports SQL and ACID-compliant read-write transactions. Its locking read-write transactions atomically read, modify, and commit data with strong transactional consistency, making them appropriate for bank-account transaction processing across distributed locations.

**Learn more:** [Transactions overview | Spanner | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/transactions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must modernize the existing on-premises data strategy. Your organization currently uses:  
  
- Apache Hadoop clusters to process multiple large data sets, including an on-premises Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) for data replication.  
- Apache Airflow to orchestrate hundreds of ETL pipelines containing thousands of job steps.  
  
You need to establish a new Google Cloud architecture that supports the Hadoop workloads while requiring minimal changes to the existing orchestration processes. What should you do?

options.text: Use Bigtable for your large workloads, with connections to Cloud Storage to handle any HDFS use cases. Orchestrate your pipelines with Cloud Composer.
Use Dataproc to migrate Hadoop clusters to Google Cloud, and Cloud Storage to handle any HDFS use cases. Orchestrate your pipelines with Cloud Composer.
Use Dataproc to migrate Hadoop clusters to Google Cloud, and Cloud Storage to handle any HDFS use cases. Convert your ETL pipelines to Dataflow.
Use Dataproc to migrate your Hadoop clusters to Google Cloud, and Cloud Storage to handle any HDFS use cases. Use Cloud Data Fusion to visually design and deploy your ETL pipelines.

questions.explanation:
Dataproc is a managed Google Cloud service for running Apache Hadoop and related ecosystem workloads. Dataproc includes an HDFS-compatible Cloud Storage connector, allowing Cloud Storage to serve HDFS-oriented storage use cases. Cloud Composer is Google Cloud’s managed Apache Airflow service, so existing Airflow DAG-based ETL orchestration can be retained with minimal change.

**Learn more:** [Dataproc FAQ](https://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/resources/faq) · [Managed Airflow overview](https://cloud.google.com/composer/docs/composer-2/composer-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are loading CSV files from Cloud Storage into BigQuery. The files have known data-quality issues, including mismatched data types—for example, STRINGs and INT64s in the same column—and inconsistent formatting of values such as phone numbers or addresses.  
  
You need to build the data pipeline to preserve data quality and perform the necessary cleansing and transformation. What should you do?

options.text: Use Data Fusion to transform the data before loading it into BigQuery.
Use Data Fusion to convert the CSV files to a self-describing data format, such as AVRO, before loading the data to BigQuery.
Load the CSV files into a staging table with the desired schema, perform the transformations with SQL, and then write the results to the final destination table.
Create a table with the desired schema, load the CSV files into the table, and perform the transformations in place using SQL.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Data Fusion can implement an ETL pipeline that cleanses and standardizes inconsistent CSV values and converts mixed field types before the data is loaded into BigQuery. This prevents incompatible or poorly formatted source values from being loaded directly into a table with a fixed target schema. Google Cloud documents Cloud Data Fusion as a service that can facilitate ETL processes for BigQuery.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to loading data | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data) · [Loading CSV data from Cloud Storage | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data-cloud-storage-csv)
